nodes.s: Tight Learned Inertial Odometry: a network regresses displacement and uncertainty from IMU windows, fused in a stochastic-cloning EKF.
nodes.w: Strong blueprint for combining a learned motion prior with a classical filter.
nodes.h: Training data is head-mounted; expect domain gap on other platforms.

nodes.s: Car dead reckoning from IMU only, using an invariant EKF whose noise covariances are adapted by a neural network, evaluated on KITTI.
nodes.w: Ground vehicle navigation through GNSS outages using only the IMU.
nodes.h: PyTorch; KITTI raw data needed. Clear demo of IMU-only drift reduction.

nodes.s: CNN that denoises low-cost gyroscope signals to improve attitude estimation.
nodes.w: Shows learned correction for cheap MEMS gyros.
nodes.h: Inactive since 2020; trained on EuRoC/TUM-VI.

nodes.s: Learns IMU error correction and uncertainty with a network, combined with differentiable IMU preintegration (CMU AirLab).
nodes.w: Learned IMU correction that feeds uncertainty into classical estimators.
nodes.h: PyTorch and PyPose; pretrained models available.

nodes.s: Learning-based inertial odometry for UAVs that improves feature observability by changing the IMU data representation (IEEE RA-L 2025).
nodes.w: Recent IMU-only drone odometry for GNSS-denied flight.
nodes.h: Recent research code; check README for datasets.

nodes.s: Subequivariant neural inertial odometry (ICLR 2025) that canonicalises IMU data so networks generalise across orientations; applied on top of TLIO and RoNIN.
nodes.w: State of the art learned inertial odometry with released code.
nodes.h: Builds on TLIO/RoNIN pipelines; set those up first.

nodes.n: Learned Inertial Odometry for Drone Racing
nodes.s: UZH RPG code fusing a learned inertial displacement model with an EKF for drone racing state estimation.
nodes.w: Shows learned IO on aggressive UAV flight.
nodes.h: Research code; datasets from UZH.

nodes.s: Header-only C++11 library for Lie theory (SO2, SE2, SO3, SE3, SE_2(3) and more) with Jacobians, built around Sola's micro Lie theory paper; Python bindings available.
nodes.w: Correct on-manifold Jacobians for custom ESKF or factor-graph code.
nodes.h: Header-only C++; Python bindings (manifpy) via conda install -c conda-forge manifpy or pip install from a clone - there is no PyPI package. Use alongside the micro Lie theory paper.

nodes.s: C++ Lie group library (SO2, SE2, SO3, SE3, Sim3) built on Eigen, used in many SLAM and VIO systems.
nodes.w: De facto Lie group dependency in SLAM codebases.
nodes.h: Header-mostly; widely packaged.

nodes.s: Python implementation of SO2, SE2, SO3 and SE3 matrix Lie groups with numpy and PyTorch backends.
nodes.w: Lie group operations inside PyTorch for learned estimators.
nodes.h: pip install from source; small and stable.

nodes.s: Python state estimation package on Lie groups (McGill DECAR): EKF, iterated EKF, sigma-point filters, batch estimation, and IMU kinematics models.
nodes.w: Fastest way to prototype on-manifold INS filters in Python.
nodes.h: pip install; has IMU and GNSS-like examples.

nodes.s: The standard ROS 2 navigation stack: behavior-tree driven navigator, global planners (NavFn, Smac hybrid-A*/lattice, Theta*), local controllers (DWB, MPPI, Regulated Pure Pursuit), costmaps, recovery behaviors and waypoint following, including GPS waypoints via robot_localization.
nodes.w: Default autonomy layer for ground robots in ROS 2; the place to plug a GNSS-denied localization source and still get full point-to-point and waypoint missions.
nodes.h: apt install ros-<distro>-navigation2 plus nav2_bringup gives a Gazebo TurtleBot demo in under an hour. Swap AMCL for your own localization by publishing map->odom TF. Tuning params YAML is the main time sink.

nodes.s: Nav2-compatible complete-coverage task server and navigator built on Fields2Cover, with behavior-tree utilities for field/area coverage and row following.
nodes.w: Gives Nav2 robots area-search and survey patterns (boustrophedon sweeps over a polygon) out of the box, useful for search, mapping and route clearance scenarios.
nodes.h: Needs a source build of Fields2Cover; send a polygon in GPS or map frame and get a coverage route. Best for flat open terrain.

nodes.s: Library of sampling-based motion planners (RRT, RRT*, PRM, BIT*, informed variants, kinodynamic planners) with a clean state-space abstraction and Python bindings.
nodes.w: The reference implementation for sampling-based planning; underpins MoveIt and many UAV/UGV planners, so it is the quickest way to get a correct baseline planner.
nodes.h: pip wheels exist for the Python bindings; define a state validity checker against your occupancy grid or DEM and you have a planner in an afternoon.

nodes.s: ESDF-free gradient-based local planner for quadrotors from ZJU FAST Lab: optimizes B-spline trajectories using collision terms computed only where the trajectory hits obstacles.
nodes.w: Lightweight onboard replanning for small drones flying through clutter; widely reused baseline for agile UAV navigation in unknown environments.
nodes.h: ROS1 (Noetic) with a bundled simulator; runs on a laptop. Porting to ROS 2 / PX4 needs a bridge. Good for a demo of reactive flight in a random forest map.

nodes.s: HKUST quadrotor planning framework: kinodynamic A* front-end plus B-spline optimization, with topological and perception-aware variants for fast flight in unknown environments.
nodes.w: Classic baseline that most later UAV planners compare against; modular enough to reuse its mapping (ESDF) and search components.
nodes.h: ROS1 + Gazebo-free lightweight sim; builds in minutes on Ubuntu 20.04. Expect NLopt dependency friction.

nodes.s: Frontier-information-structure based autonomous exploration for quadrotors, combining global tour planning over frontiers with local viewpoint refinement.
nodes.w: Autonomous mapping of unknown buildings or terrain without GNSS or prior map, a core reconnaissance capability.
nodes.h: Bundled sim; pairs naturally with a VIO/LiDAR odometry source from other lanes.

nodes.s: Rapid collaborative exploration with multiple UAVs: decomposes unknown space and allocates exploration regions between drones with pairwise communication.
nodes.w: A worked example of multi-robot task allocation for exploration under limited comms.
nodes.h: Same toolchain as FUEL; run 2-4 drones in sim and vary comm range.

nodes.s: General-purpose multicopter trajectory optimizer (MINCO) handling safe-corridor constraints and dynamic limits with spatial-temporal deformation.
nodes.w: Efficient, well-documented trajectory optimizer to turn waypoint paths into flyable minimum-control trajectories.
nodes.h: Header-heavy C++ with ROS1 examples; best used as a library behind your own front-end.

nodes.s: UPenn Kumar Robotics end-to-end autonomy stack for GPS-denied quadrotors: state estimation, mapping, planning and control in one system.
nodes.w: Full reference stack for flying without GNSS in forests and under canopy, from a lab with many field deployments.
nodes.h: Docker images help; large build. Use it to see how estimation and planning are glued, or reuse the planner.

nodes.s: MIT ACL decentralized and asynchronous trajectory planner for multiple UAVs in dynamic environments with obstacle and agent avoidance.
nodes.w: Multi-agent planning without synchronized clocks or central coordination, closer to real comms constraints.
nodes.h: No commits since 2022; ROS1. Use for ideas rather than code reuse.

nodes.s: PDDL-based symbolic planning system for ROS 2: domain/problem management, plan generation with off-the-shelf planners and execution via behavior trees.
nodes.w: Turns high-level mission goals (visit, inspect, deliver) into executable action sequences, the missing layer above Nav2.
nodes.h: apt-installable; write a PDDL domain and wrap Nav2 goals as actions. Learning PDDL is the time cost.

nodes.s: C++ behavior tree library with XML trees, async actions, logging and the Groot editor; the execution engine inside Nav2 and many mission frameworks.
nodes.w: Standard way to compose navigation, fallback and recovery logic into readable mission trees.
nodes.h: Header-friendly library; Groot2 GUI helps demo mission logic to judges.

nodes.s: Large collection of readable Python implementations of robotics algorithms: localization (EKF, particle filter), SLAM, path planning (A*, RRT*, D*, state lattice), path tracking and more, with animations.
nodes.w: Best teaching and prototyping resource; copy a planner or filter into a hackathon prototype in minutes.
nodes.h: Pure numpy/matplotlib; no build. Good for a quick 2D planner over a rasterized DEM.

nodes.s: Modular coverage path planning library: headland generation, swath generation, route ordering (boustrophedon, snake, spiral) and Dubins/Reeds-Shepp path smoothing, with Python bindings.
nodes.w: Ready coverage planner for area search or survey patterns by ground or air vehicles.
nodes.h: Build from source with GDAL dependency; Python bindings let you produce a sweep over a GeoJSON polygon quickly.

nodes.s: ETH ASL coverage planner for polygons with holes that treats boustrophedon sweep selection as a generalized TSP, aimed at UAV survey.
nodes.w: Handles no-fly holes inside a survey area, which simple lawnmower generators do not.
nodes.h: ROS1 + CGAL; last push 2023. Use as a reference or run offline to produce waypoint lists.

nodes.s: Universal multi-layer 2.5D grid map library for mobile robots with ROS/ROS 2 integration, filters, iterators and conversion to images, point clouds and costmaps.
nodes.w: Common data structure for elevation, slope and cost layers - the glue between DEMs and planners.
nodes.h: Available as ROS 2 binaries; load a GeoTIFF DEM (via GDAL) into a grid_map layer for terrain-aware costs.

nodes.s: Nav2 costmap layer using OpenVDB voxel grids with time decay to represent 3D obstacles from depth and LiDAR sensors.
nodes.w: Better 3D obstacle handling for ground robots in dynamic environments than the default voxel layer.
nodes.h: Drop-in Nav2 plugin via apt.

nodes.s: Python implementation of the Consensus-Based Bundle Algorithm for decentralized multi-agent task allocation with plotting examples.
nodes.w: CBBA is the classic decentralized auction for assigning tasks to UAV teams; this is an easy-to-read starting point.
nodes.h: numpy + matplotlib only; wrap in a ROS 2 node or call from a mission script to assign search cells to drones.

nodes.s: Task allocation library from Open-RMF that assigns tasks to fleets of robots, accounting for battery, travel time and task constraints.
nodes.w: Production-grade multi-robot task allocation with a fleet-level view, transferable from logistics to multi-vehicle missions.
nodes.h: Part of the larger Open-RMF stack; worth it only if you want fleet management, otherwise use CBBA.

nodes.s: Translator library and CLI tools for raster and vector geospatial formats (GeoTIFF, COG, GeoPackage, Shapefile, KML and hundreds more) with reprojection, warping and DEM utilities.
nodes.w: Every map, DEM and imagery pipeline goes through GDAL; gdalwarp, gdaldem and gdal_translate cover most reference-map preparation.
nodes.h: Use conda or the OSGeo Docker image to avoid version mismatches between GDAL and Python bindings.

nodes.s: Cartographic projection and coordinate transformation library with datum grids, time-dependent transformations and a pipeline syntax.
nodes.w: Correct datum and projection handling (WGS84, ITRF, local grids, UTM) is foundational for any nav system that mixes map sources.
nodes.h: Bundle the proj-data grids offline if your demo has no internet.

nodes.s: Python interface to PROJ for CRS definitions, coordinate transformations and geodesic computations.
nodes.w: Default Python tool for lat/lon <-> UTM/ECEF/local conversions in nav prototypes.
nodes.h: pip install pyproj ships PROJ inside the wheel; reuse a Transformer object for speed.

nodes.s: Pythonic raster I/O on top of GDAL: read/write GeoTIFF and COG, windowed reads, masks and affine georeferencing.
nodes.w: Easiest way to sample a DEM or orthophoto at a coordinate for terrain-referenced or visual navigation experiments.
nodes.h: pip wheels include GDAL; use windowed reads to crop tiles around a vehicle position.

nodes.s: Desktop open-source GIS for viewing, editing, analyzing and printing geospatial data, extensible via Python plugins.
nodes.w: The analyst's workbench for building mission areas, inspecting DEMs and checking flight logs on a map.
nodes.h: Install the LTR build; draw AOIs and export GeoJSON for planners. QGIS loads MBTiles/PMTiles for offline basemaps.

nodes.s: WebGL 3D globe and map library with terrain, 3D Tiles, time-dynamic data (CZML) and accurate WGS84 rendering.
nodes.w: Best open web option for a 3D situational awareness view with terrain and flight paths; widely used in defense demos.
nodes.h: npm install cesium. Default imagery/terrain use Cesium ion (token); for offline, serve your own quantized-mesh terrain and tiles.

nodes.s: Command-line tools to convert GDAL-readable DEMs into Cesium terrain tiles (heightmap and quantized-mesh with the docker variant).
nodes.w: Turns a Copernicus/SRTM DEM into offline 3D terrain for a CesiumJS display without internet.
nodes.h: Unmaintained since 2023; use the tum-gis docker image to avoid build pain.

nodes.s: Open-source WebGL vector tile map renderer (fork of Mapbox GL JS v1) with styles, 3D terrain and globe view.
nodes.w: Fast, license-clean 2D/2.5D web map for C2 dashboards, works fully offline with your own tiles.
nodes.h: Pair with martin or tileserver-gl and a PMTiles extract for an offline basemap.

nodes.s: Feature-rich web mapping library supporting many projections, WMS/WMTS, vector tiles and editing.
nodes.w: Strong choice when you need non-Web-Mercator projections or OGC services in a C2 web UI.
nodes.h: npm install ol; integrates with proj4js for custom CRS.

nodes.s: Small, simple JavaScript library for interactive raster/vector maps with a huge plugin ecosystem.
nodes.w: Quickest route to a working map with markers and tracks in a hackathon UI.
nodes.h: Works with milsymbol to render unit icons as markers.

nodes.s: GPU-powered large-scale data visualization framework with layers for points, paths, trips, hexbins and 3D tiles, usable over MapLibre or standalone.
nodes.w: Renders thousands of tracks (ADS-B, AIS, swarm telemetry) smoothly for a common operating picture.
nodes.h: Use TripsLayer for animated track histories; integrates with React.

nodes.s: High-performance road routing engine on OpenStreetMap data using contraction hierarchies or multi-level Dijkstra.
nodes.w: Offline road routing for ground vehicle convoy and logistics planning.
nodes.h: Docker image + a Geofabrik regional extract gives a routing API in under an hour.

nodes.s: Tiled OSM routing engine with dynamic costing per request (auto, truck, pedestrian, bicycle), isochrones and map matching.
nodes.w: Request-time costing makes it easy to avoid areas or prefer terrain types, and its map-matching snaps noisy tracks to roads.
nodes.h: Docker images available; build tiles for a region once and run offline. Elevation tiles enable grade-aware costing.

nodes.s: Java OSM routing engine usable as library or server, with custom models for per-request costing and map matching.
nodes.w: Embeddable routing on JVM/Android, relevant for on-device dismounted navigation apps.
nodes.h: Single jar + OSM pbf; custom model JSON lets you penalize road classes or areas.

nodes.s: Download, model and analyze street networks and other OSM features as NetworkX graphs.
nodes.w: Rapid road/path graph construction for planners and task allocation experiments in Python.
nodes.h: pip install osmnx; needs internet for Overpass unless you load a local OSM file.

nodes.s: CLI/Python tool to download, cache and clip global DEMs (SRTM, Copernicus DEM and others) for a bounding box.
nodes.w: One-command DEM for an AOI, the first input for terrain-referenced navigation and terrain-aware planning.
nodes.h: Needs GDAL on PATH; eio clip --bounds ... produces a GeoTIFF.

nodes.s: Vector and raster tile server that serves MBTiles/PMTiles with GL styles and renders raster tiles server-side with MapLibre Native.
nodes.w: Simplest offline basemap server for field laptops and TAK clients needing raster tiles.
nodes.h: docker run maptiler/tileserver-gl with an mbtiles file; also gives WMTS for QGIS.

nodes.s: Fast Rust tile server for PostGIS, MBTiles and PMTiles sources, with tile generation and mbtiles tooling.
nodes.w: Serves live PostGIS layers (tracks, zones) as vector tiles alongside static basemaps.
nodes.h: Single binary or docker; point at a PostGIS table to stream dynamic features.

nodes.s: Single-file tile archive format and tooling, served by HTTP range requests from static storage, with JS/Go readers and extraction CLI.
nodes.w: Ship an entire regional basemap as one file on a USB stick or static server - ideal for disconnected ops.
nodes.h: pmtiles extract from a planet build to cut your AOI; load with the MapLibre protocol plugin.

nodes.s: Fast vector tile generator that builds OpenMapTiles-compatible tilesets from OSM extracts on a single machine.
nodes.w: Build your own up-to-date offline basemap for an AOI in minutes.
nodes.h: java -jar planetiler.jar --area=<region> outputs mbtiles or pmtiles.

nodes.s: Python library converting between latitude/longitude and MGRS grid references, built on NGA GEOTRANS 3.10 (now a Rust port exposed through a pybind11 extension).
nodes.w: MGRS is the grid language of military users; needed for any C2 UI or report generator.
nodes.h: pip install mgrs; mind the precision argument for 1 m vs 10 m references. Since 1.6.0 inverse conversion returns the grid-cell centre, not the south-west corner.

nodes.s: C++ library for accurate geodesic problems, UTM/UPS/MGRS conversions, geoid heights, gravity and magnetic field models.
nodes.w: Gold-standard geodesy: geodesic distances, geoid (EGM96/2008) undulation for GNSS height vs DEM height, and MGRS.
nodes.h: Python and JS ports exist (geographiclib-python, geographiclib-js); geoid datasets download separately.

nodes.s: Pure-Python 3D coordinate conversions: geodetic, ECEF, ENU, NED, AER, ECI, with optional NumPy vectorization.
nodes.w: The everyday tool for converting GNSS fixes into a local ENU/NED frame for fusion and planning.
nodes.h: pip install pymap3d; no compiled deps.

nodes.s: Python client for Sentinel Hub and Copernicus Data Space services to search, download and process Sentinel and other satellite imagery.
nodes.w: Pull recent satellite imagery of an AOI to build reference maps for visual geolocalization.
nodes.h: Needs free Copernicus Data Space or Sentinel Hub credentials; set up before the event.

nodes.s: Python client for searching STAC APIs (Earth Search, Planetary Computer and others) by area, time and properties.
nodes.w: Credential-free path to Sentinel-2, Landsat and Copernicus DEM tiles via public STAC catalogs.
nodes.h: Search Earth Search (AWS) without a key and read COGs directly with rasterio.

nodes.s: Loads STAC items into xarray datasets with reprojection, resampling and mosaicking.
nodes.w: Turn a STAC search into a ready, aligned raster stack for map-matching experiments.
nodes.h: Works with Dask for larger AOIs.

nodes.s: Photogrammetry toolkit that turns aerial images into orthophotos, point clouds, 3D models and DEMs.
nodes.w: Build your own up-to-date reference orthophoto and DSM from a survey flight for visual and terrain navigation.
nodes.h: docker run opendronemap/odm on a folder of images; WebODM gives a GUI. Processing time scales with image count.

nodes.s: Open-source release of the TAK Server from the TAK Product Center: the federation and message routing server for ATAK/WinTAK/iTAK clients, handling CoT, data packages, missions and video.
nodes.w: Reference C2 backend used by many government users; integrating with it makes a demo interoperable with fielded TAK clients.
nodes.h: Java + PostgreSQL + certificate setup is the main hurdle; use a docker recipe and allow several hours.

nodes.s: Go implementation of a simple ATAK-compatible server and a web client, supporting CoT over TCP/UDP/SSL.
nodes.w: Single static binary TAK server and browser client - minimal footprint for edge devices.
nodes.h: go build or release binary; web map client is handy for judges without ATAK installed.

nodes.s: Browser-based TAK-compatible common operating picture with ETL connectors that push external data feeds into TAK.
nodes.w: Shows how to bridge arbitrary data sources (sensors, APIs) into a TAK network with a web COP.
nodes.h: AWS-oriented deployment; locally, reuse its node-CoT library and connector patterns.

nodes.s: JavaScript/TypeScript library for parsing, building and converting Cursor-on-Target messages, including GeoJSON conversion and TAK protobuf.
nodes.w: Quickest way to emit CoT from a Node/web app.
nodes.h: npm install @tak-ps/node-cot.

nodes.s: Encode and decode TAK protobuf (TAK Protocol v1) packets, including mesh and stream formats.
nodes.w: Needed when talking to modern TAK clients that prefer protobuf over XML CoT.
nodes.h: pip install takproto.

nodes.s: Go library for parsing, validating and generating Cursor-on-Target XML with security-focused input limits and optional schema validation.
nodes.w: Hardened CoT parsing for Go services that accept untrusted network input.
nodes.h: Schema validation needs libxml2 and CGO.

nodes.s: Pure JavaScript library generating MIL-STD-2525 (B/C/D/E) and APP-6 (B/D/E) military symbols as SVG or canvas.
nodes.w: Renders correct unit and track symbology on any web map without licensed assets.
nodes.h: npm install milsymbol; new ms.Symbol(sidc).asSVG() drops straight into a Leaflet or MapLibre marker.

nodes.s: Esri data encapsulation of MIL-STD-2525D and APP-6(D) symbology: symbol IDs, entity tables and SVG assets.
nodes.w: Machine-readable symbol tables useful for validating SIDCs or building your own renderer.
nodes.h: Archived in 2024; data still useful.

nodes.s: C/C++ and Python decoder for EUROCONTROL ASTERIX surveillance data from files, stdin or network, with XML category definitions and JSON/XML output.
nodes.w: ASTERIX is the format real radars and ATC surveillance use; decoding it lets a demo ingest professional air picture feeds.
nodes.h: Python module is on PyPI as asterix_decoder; feed it recorded or live UDP ASTERIX and get JSON per record.

nodes.s: EUROCONTROL ASTERIX category specifications in a structured machine-readable format, with generated JSON and docs.
nodes.w: Authoritative-structured spec source for building ASTERIX encoders/decoders in any language.
nodes.h: Companion asterix-libs repo has generated Python libraries.

nodes.s: Python decoder for Mode S and ADS-B messages including Comm-B / EHS fields, with live streaming tools.
nodes.w: Decode raw Mode S yourself, including derived wind and airspeed data; underlies The 1090MHz Riddle book.
nodes.h: pip install pyModeS now installs the v3 rewrite (Python 3.11+): a single decode() call plus a stateful PipeDecoder for streams, and a modes CLI. Older tutorials and The 1090MHz Riddle use the v2 pms.adsb.* API; pin pyModeS<3 to follow them. Pairs with a Beast/raw feed from readsb.

nodes.s: Toolbox for processing and analyzing air traffic trajectories: OpenSky access, filtering, resampling, airspace intersection and visualization.
nodes.w: Analyze flight tracks and airspace structures for airspace awareness or UAV deconfliction studies.
nodes.h: pip install traffic; OpenSky historical data needs an account.

nodes.s: Python and Java bindings for the OpenSky Network REST API for live and recent aircraft states.
nodes.w: Free crowd-sourced air picture when no local receiver is available.
nodes.h: Anonymous access is rate-limited. Since March 2026 authenticated access uses OAuth2 client credentials (basic auth was dropped); create an API client in your OpenSky account.

nodes.s: Long-wave infrared image dataset of a harbour environment with semantic and instance segmentation masks for maritime scene understanding.
nodes.w: Thermal perception is what keeps an autonomous surface vessel aware of obstacles at night and in haze, when RGB fails.
nodes.h: Download from the Google Drive links in the README; small enough to fine-tune a segmentation net in a few hours.

nodes.s: Evaluation scripts for LaRS, a panoptic maritime obstacle detection benchmark spanning lakes, rivers and seas.
nodes.w: Gives a standard scoring harness for USV obstacle detection so a team can compare its model against published baselines.
nodes.h: Pair with the LaRS dataset from the project page; use the evaluator to score a YOLO/segmentation baseline.

nodes.s: Underwater dataset recorded by a lightweight AUV inspecting a submarine pipeline, with camera, side-scan sonar and navigation data for segmentation and visual-inertial localization.
nodes.w: One of few open AUV datasets with ground-truth trajectories, useful for testing underwater VIO where GNSS never reaches.
nodes.h: Large download; start with one sequence and run an off-the-shelf VIO to show drift underwater.

nodes.s: Aerial RGB plus thermal dataset from natural terrain (rivers, coasts, deserts, forests) with GPS and inertial data, plus benchmarks for segmentation, RGB-to-thermal translation and VIO.
nodes.w: Thermal-aerial data with GPS/IMU is rare; it supports night-time visual and thermal navigation research without flying your own sensor rig.
nodes.h: Use the VIO split to test thermal-inertial odometry; or train RGB-to-thermal translation to build synthetic thermal maps.

nodes.s: Repository of the long-running Drone-vs-Bird challenge: annotations and instructions for a video dataset of small drones with birds as distractors.
nodes.w: Telling a distant drone from a bird is the core false-alarm problem in camera-based C-UAS; this is the reference benchmark.
nodes.h: Request the videos per README, train a small-object YOLO; the hard part is tiny targets, so tile the frames.

nodes.s: Indoor recordings of drone propeller noise augmented with noise clips, organised for binary and multiclass audio drone detection.
nodes.w: A common baseline audio set for acoustic drone detection. Note: its licence explicitly forbids military/defence use, so check fit before building on it.
nodes.h: Licence restricts defence-related use - use for learning only or pick another acoustic set.

nodes.s: Multi-sensor dataset with infrared and visible video plus audio clips of drones, birds, airplanes and helicopters, from a Swedish thesis project.
nodes.w: Lets a team prototype sensor fusion for C-UAS (thermal + RGB + audio) on one consistent set of targets and distractors.
nodes.h: Ready to download; good for a fused IR+audio classifier demo in a weekend.

nodes.s: Student project building a passive RF drone detector for a campus police department, with Wi-Fi monitoring scripts and visualization tools.
nodes.w: Shows a cheap passive RF detection path for drones that use Wi-Fi links.
nodes.h: Needs a monitor-mode Wi-Fi adapter; works only on Wi-Fi-controlled drones, not proprietary links.

nodes.s: Loader and inspection scripts for a drone RF classification benchmark hosted on Kaggle, with samples across a range of SNRs.
nodes.w: SNR-labelled RF samples let you measure how a drone RF classifier degrades with distance and noise.
nodes.h: Download from Kaggle, load with the provided PyTorch dataloader, train a small CNN in an hour.

nodes.s: Notebooks that classify drone presence and type from RF using DroneRF and DroneDetect data (PSD+SVM and CNN approaches), aiming at real-time use with GamutRF hardware.
nodes.w: Ready-made baselines on the two most-cited public drone RF datasets.
nodes.h: Fastest path to a working RF drone classifier; includes a Raspberry Pi test script.

nodes.n: Drone Detection and Identification using RF signals
nodes.s: Code for an ML framework for drone detection and identification from RF signals.
nodes.w: Another reproducible baseline on public drone RF data to compare against.
nodes.h: Notebook-based; pair with DroneRF data.

nodes.n: CNN for drone detection using RF
nodes.s: CNN code for drone detection and identification on RF spectra.
nodes.w: Simple CNN baseline for RF drone ID.
nodes.h: Older code (2020); use as reference only.

nodes.s: Colab notebooks that classify GNSS jamming types from spectrogram images built from a public raw-IQ jamming dataset, with ML, DL and CV approaches; companion to an arXiv paper.
nodes.w: Turnkey starting point for a jamming-type classifier using open data.
nodes.h: Open in Colab, download the Zenodo IQ set, and you have a classifier in an hour.

nodes.s: LSTM (Bayesian and standard) classifiers that identify individual jammers from IQ recordings, from an ICL-GNSS 2024 paper on how environment and receiver affect classification.
nodes.w: Fingerprinting which jammer is present is a step toward attribution and targeted mitigation.
nodes.h: Needs your own IQ recordings in the expected file layout; reuse the model code on Jammertest data.

nodes.s: Pipeline that detects radio-frequency interference in Sentinel-1 SAR imagery using temporal z-scores and DEM masking, to map GNSS jamming activity from orbit.
nodes.w: Free satellite data as a wide-area jamming sensor - complements ADS-B based maps.
nodes.h: Pull Sentinel-1 scenes for a region and produce a jamming heatmap; good OSINT-style demo.

nodes.s: Receive-only GNSS interference detection with radio direction finding and triangulation on Raspberry Pi and RTL-SDR.
nodes.w: Low-cost jammer localization is a practical defensive EW capability.
nodes.h: Cheap hardware; multiple nodes needed for triangulation. Receive-only, so legal to test.

nodes.s: Rust library with Python API that scores GNSS signal quality via C/N0 and flags jamming, spoofing and interference across constellations.
nodes.w: Drop-in signal-quality monitor for a navigation stack.
nodes.h: Feed it receiver observables; good as an integrity-monitor component.

nodes.s: Recordings of several simultaneous chirp jammers on GPS L1, captured in isolation, for studying notch-filter (ANF) mitigation.
nodes.w: Multi-jammer data is rare; useful for testing mitigation filters.
nodes.h: Use to test an adaptive notch filter in GNU Radio or Python.

nodes.n: GNSS jamming detection on maritime Antarctica dataset
nodes.s: Thesis code for ML jamming detection and temporal generalisation using real maritime receiver diagnostics (u-blox MON-RF, MON-SPAN, RXM-MEASX) from a public Antarctica voyage dataset.
nodes.w: Uses receiver-reported diagnostics a cheap u-blox already exposes, so it transfers to real hardware.
nodes.h: Reproduce on your own u-blox logs by enabling the same UBX messages.

nodes.s: MATLAB implementation of the power-distortion detector for GNSS spoofing and jamming.
nodes.w: Classic signal-level spoofing detector from the Humphreys line of work.
nodes.h: Inactive since 2020; read alongside the TEXBAT data.

nodes.s: Public code and simulations for spoof detection algorithms supporting Stanford GPS Lab publications.
nodes.w: Reference implementations of spoofing detection tests.
nodes.h: Old MATLAB; useful for algorithm reference.

nodes.s: MATLAB project exploring GNSS spoofing detection methods.
nodes.w: Small educational example.
nodes.h: Reference only.

nodes.n: NRC UAV vs bird radar tracks
nodes.s: Labelled real-world radar tracks of small UAVs, birds, humans and vehicles from an Echodyne EchoGuard radar over several Canadian field trials.
nodes.w: Radar track classification (drone vs bird) is central to C-UAS beyond micro-Doppler range; open labelled radar data is scarce.
nodes.h: Train a kinematic-feature classifier on the tracks; no RF hardware needed.

nodes.s: Multimodal low-altitude anti-drone dataset combining RGB, infrared, active radar and passive RF.
nodes.w: Rare dataset with all four C-UAS sensor modalities.
nodes.h: Check access instructions; data availability may be partial.

nodes.s: Datasets for acoustic echolocation and sound-source localization recorded on a Crazyflie drone and an e-puck robot.
nodes.w: Shows acoustic sensing as a localization modality on micro drones.
nodes.h: Niche; useful if exploring acoustic self-localization.

nodes.s: Acoustic datasets for drone detection on embedded devices such as ESP32-S3, including bio-acoustic interference samples.
nodes.w: Targets low-cost acoustic sensor nodes - the cheapest C-UAS tripwire.
nodes.h: Pair with the Batear firmware for a microcontroller acoustic sensor demo.

nodes.s: Open field-test toolkit for acoustic and radar detection of low-signature drones on COTS hardware, aiming at FPV detection baselines.
nodes.w: FPV-class detection baselines are missing in literature; this gives a reproducible method.
nodes.h: Follow the field protocol to measure your own detection ranges.

nodes.s: Benchmark and code for UAV geo-localization trained on synthetic game imagery with partial-match drone-satellite pairs (AAAI 2025).
nodes.w: Synthetic data generation for geo-localization reduces the need for real flight data.
nodes.h: Pretrained models available; fine-tune on your area's satellite tiles.

nodes.s: Neural pixel-to-3D registration for UAV ego-localization and target geo-localization against a geo-referenced 3D map; release uses 3D Gaussian Splatting map backends (CVPR 2026).
nodes.w: Absolute 6-DoF pose from a 3D map is a strong GNSS-denied fix for low-altitude drones.
nodes.h: GPU-heavy; demo data and pretrained model provided.

nodes.s: Transformer-based feature segmentation and region alignment for drone-to-satellite geo-localization (TCSVT 2021).
nodes.w: Widely used baseline on University-1652.
nodes.h: Train on University-1652; good comparison baseline.

nodes.s: Baseline for last-meter UAV navigation using diffusion-refined aerial visual servoing; serves as the baseline for the ACM MM 2026 UAV workshop challenge.
nodes.w: Moves geo-localization from retrieval to precise relative positioning for the final approach.
nodes.h: Use the HF test set; competition baseline.

nodes.s: Page for the ACM MM 2023 drone-satellite matching challenge on University-160k, listing team code repos and the leaderboard.
nodes.w: Index of open winning-team code for drone-satellite matching.
nodes.h: Follow links to public team repos.

nodes.s: Page for the ACM MM 2024 multi-weather drone-satellite matching challenge, listing team repos.
nodes.w: Adds weather robustness to cross-view geo-localization.
nodes.h: Follow links to public team repos.

nodes.s: Multiple-environment self-adaptive network for aerial-view geo-localization under varied weather (Pattern Recognition 2024).
nodes.w: Weather robustness for drone-satellite matching.
nodes.h: Baseline for the UAVM 2024 multi-weather track.

nodes.s: Siamese-network solution to the ACM MM 2024 multi-environment drone-satellite matching challenge.
nodes.w: Open challenge entry for weather-robust geo-localization.
nodes.h: Weights on Baidu pan; may be hard to fetch.

nodes.s: Team solution for the ACM MM 2023 drone-satellite matching challenge.
nodes.w: Open challenge entry.
nodes.h: Training script; needs University-1652.

nodes.s: Submission for the ACM MM 2023 drone-satellite matching challenge.
nodes.w: Open challenge entry.
nodes.h: Minimal docs.

nodes.s: Modern-backbone efficient geo-localization solution for UAVM 2023 including distillation training.
nodes.w: Open entry with distillation, useful for edge deployment.
nodes.h: Was disqualified for using test data, but the method code is still useful.

nodes.s: 10th-place solution for the Kaggle Google Smartphone Decimeter Challenge.
nodes.w: Readable Kaggle-style pipeline for smartphone GNSS post-processing.
nodes.h: Reference for feature engineering on Android GNSS logs.

nodes.s: MATLAB package from an ION GNSS+ 2021 decimeter challenge entry.
nodes.w: MATLAB route for smartphone GNSS positioning.
nodes.h: Reference only.

nodes.s: ML-based adaptive positioning to fuse smartphone GNSS and IMU, built for GSDC 2022.
nodes.w: Example of learned GNSS/IMU fusion on phone data.
nodes.h: Reference.

nodes.s: SSR and OSR GNSS correction data for the 2021 Google Smartphone Decimeter Challenge drives, in SBP, JSON, RTCM3 and RINEX.
nodes.w: Real correction streams aligned to a public phone dataset - good for practising RTK/PPP on phones.
nodes.h: Pair with GSDC 2021 data and RTKLIB.

nodes.s: Magnetic-field aided inertial navigation system for indoor positioning, compared against a magnetic EKF.
nodes.w: Magnetic field anomalies as a GNSS-free position aid indoors.
nodes.h: MATLAB with data; test on your own magnetometer arrays.

nodes.s: Magnetic-field aided inertial navigation using a magnetometer array for odometry.
nodes.w: Shows magnetometer arrays as odometry where cameras fail.
nodes.h: MATLAB reference.

nodes.s: Geo-localization of oblique thermal UAV image sequences against satellite maps.
nodes.w: Night-time thermal geo-localization with oblique cameras, closer to real FPV/ISR views.
nodes.h: Recent; check data availability.

nodes.s: Simulator (Ignition Fortress + ROS 2) for the MBZIRC Maritime Grand Challenge where UAVs and USVs cooperate in a GNSS-denied environment.
nodes.w: Ready-made maritime GNSS-denied multi-vehicle scenario.
nodes.h: Built for Ubuntu 20.04 / ROS 2 Galactic; use Docker.

nodes.s: Annotated dataset of fast autonomous and human-piloted quadrotor flight with visual, inertial and mocap data plus labelled racing gates, from TII.
nodes.w: High-speed VIO and gate-relative state estimation data.
nodes.h: Use to test VIO at high speed.

nodes.s: Block-programming interface for drone swarms on COEX Clover, CopterHack 2022 winner by team Atena.
nodes.w: Example of a winning open CopterHack project.
nodes.h: Runs on Clover simulation.

nodes.s: Frontend and backend from the Clover Rescue Team's CopterHack 2022 project.
nodes.w: Example finalist code.
nodes.h: Reference only.

nodes.s: Current-generation Gazebo robotics simulator with pluggable physics, rendering and a large sensor library (IMU, GPS/NavSat, lidar, cameras, magnetometer, altimeter). Successor to Gazebo Classic.
nodes.w: The default SITL backend for both PX4 and ArduPilot today; the place to inject sensor noise, GNSS dropouts and degraded conditions into a full autopilot stack.
nodes.h: Install a binary release (Harmonic or later) plus ros_gz. Pair with PX4 'make px4_sitl gz_x500' or ardupilot_gazebo. GPU helps for camera sensors; headless server mode works for CI.

nodes.s: Bridge packages that relay topics, services and clock between Gazebo Sim transport and ROS 1/ROS 2.
nodes.w: Needed whenever a ROS 2 navigation or SLAM stack has to consume simulated sensor streams from Gazebo.
nodes.h: Use parameter_bridge with a YAML of topic mappings. Match the ros_gz branch to your ROS 2 distro and Gazebo release or builds fail.

nodes.s: Model and world repository for the new Gazebo, used by PX4 SITL targets such as gz_x500.
nodes.w: Shows how PX4 vehicles and sensors are described for gz-sim; the starting point for adding custom sensors to a PX4 airframe.
nodes.h: Fetched automatically by PX4 SITL. Fork and edit SDF to add cameras or change sensor noise.

nodes.s: Lightweight Java multirotor simulator that speaks MAVLink to PX4, without a 3D-world physics engine.
nodes.w: Fastest way to get a PX4 SITL quad flying for MAVLink, GCS or mission-logic work when sensors and worlds do not matter.
nodes.h: Runs with 'make px4_sitl jmavsim'. Needs a JDK. No cameras or lidar, so not for perception work.

nodes.s: Collection of aircraft and vehicle models and parameter files for ArduPilot SITL across several simulator backends.
nodes.w: Ready-made airframes (including fixed-wing and VTOL) save hours when a hackathon scenario needs something other than a quadcopter.
nodes.h: Pick a model folder and follow its readme; each lists the backend it targets.

nodes.s: Unreal Engine based simulator for drones and cars with camera, depth, lidar, IMU, GPS, barometer and magnetometer models and a Python/C++ API. Microsoft wound down development and pointed users to Project AirSim.
nodes.w: Still the most widely used photorealistic drone sim in research papers; many visual-nav and geolocalization datasets were rendered with it.
nodes.h: Prebuilt binary environments are the quickest path. Building from source requires a matching old Unreal version. For new work prefer Colosseum or Project AirSim.

nodes.s: Community fork of AirSim that moved it to newer Unreal Engine 5 releases. The GitHub repository is now marked archived.
nodes.w: Was the main path to run AirSim on UE5; useful as a reference port even though it is no longer maintained.
nodes.h: Archived on GitHub, so expect unanswered issues. Use only if you need its UE5 changes specifically.

nodes.s: Open-source release of Project AirSim, the rewrite and successor of AirSim, for building and testing autonomous aerial systems in high-fidelity Unreal environments.
nodes.w: The actively developed line of the AirSim family, relevant for photorealistic aerial perception and autonomy testing.
nodes.h: Check its docs for supported Unreal version and OS. Heavier setup than AirSim binaries; budget several hours.

nodes.s: Unity3D and ROS framework from MIT for photorealistic camera rendering with real or simulated vehicle dynamics in the loop.
nodes.w: Pioneered vehicle-in-the-loop rendering: fly a real drone in a mocap room while feeding it synthetic imagery.
nodes.h: Not actively maintained since 2024; ROS1. Mostly of interest as a reference or alongside the Blackbird dataset.

nodes.s: Framework on top of NVIDIA Isaac Sim for simulating multirotors with PX4 in the loop and Python-defined vehicles and sensors.
nodes.w: Gives PX4 users photorealistic, GPU-accelerated Omniverse rendering while keeping the real autopilot stack.
nodes.h: Needs an RTX GPU and an Isaac Sim install; match Pegasus release to the Isaac Sim version listed in its docs.

nodes.s: NVIDIA's Omniverse-based robot simulator, now open source, with RTX sensor simulation (cameras, lidar, IMU) and ROS 2 bridges.
nodes.w: Base layer for Pegasus, OmniDrones and Isaac Lab; strong for synthetic data generation for perception models.
nodes.h: RTX GPU and a lot of disk required. Use the prebuilt container or pip install rather than building from source in a hackathon.

nodes.s: Robot-learning framework on Isaac Sim for massively parallel RL and imitation learning, with navigation and locomotion task examples.
nodes.w: Fast route to training learned navigation or locomotion policies with thousands of parallel simulated robots.
nodes.h: Install via pip on a supported Isaac Sim version. Start from an existing nav task config rather than writing environments from scratch.

nodes.s: Open-source autonomous-driving simulator on Unreal with camera, lidar, radar, GNSS and IMU sensors, traffic and weather control.
nodes.w: Standard ground-vehicle testbed for localization and planning under weather, night and sensor-degradation conditions.
nodes.h: Use packaged releases and the Python client; the ROS 2 bridge is separate. A decent GPU is required.

nodes.s: Gazebo Classic MAV simulator from ETH ASL with multirotor models, IMU and odometry sensor plugins and example controllers.
nodes.w: Classic reference for MAV sim used in many VIO and planning papers; its IMU noise models are still frequently copied.
nodes.h: ROS1 and Gazebo Classic only; use for reproducing older papers rather than new builds.

nodes.s: GPU-parallel aerial-robot simulator from NTNU ARL built on NVIDIA Isaac Gym, with depth/range sensors and RL navigation examples.
nodes.w: Train learned obstacle avoidance and navigation for drones at scale with simulated depth cameras and lidar.
nodes.h: Needs NVIDIA GPU and Isaac Gym preview (a legacy package); check README for current install path.

nodes.s: Gymnasium environments on PyBullet for single and multi-agent quadcopter control and RL (formerly under utiasDSL).
nodes.w: Lowest-friction multi-drone RL sandbox: pure Python, CPU-only, quick to modify.
nodes.h: pip install in a venv and run examples within minutes. No photorealistic sensors; good for control, swarming and planning logic.

nodes.s: GPU-parallel drone simulation and RL platform built on Isaac Sim.
nodes.w: Supports multi-drone and transport tasks with vectorized environments for learning-based autonomy.
nodes.h: Pinned to specific Isaac Sim versions; check compatibility before investing time.

nodes.s: Python multirotor simulator with aerodynamic effects (drag, wind) for education and research.
nodes.w: Good for studying estimator and controller behaviour under wind and disturbances without a game engine.
nodes.h: pip installable, runs on a laptop. Has IMU and mocap-style sensor models; add your own estimator in Python.

nodes.s: General-purpose open-source robot simulator with many robot models and sensors including GPS, compass, IMU, lidar and radar.
nodes.w: Cross-platform and easy to install; good for ground and multi-robot nav demos with ROS 2 integration.
nodes.h: Installers for Windows, macOS and Linux. webots_ros2 package for ROS 2. Less common in aerial autonomy.

nodes.s: Documentation repository for HoloOcean, BYU's Unreal-based underwater simulator with sonar, DVL, IMU, depth and camera sensors and multi-agent support. The simulator code itself is not hosted in this repo.
nodes.w: Photorealistic underwater sim aimed at marine navigation and SLAM research, including acoustic modems for multi-agent setups.
nodes.h: Follow the installation page of the docs; Python package plus downloadable worlds. Heavy GPU load for sonar rendering.

nodes.s: Notebooks and examples for the GRID platform from Scaled Foundations, which pairs the AirSim-derived AirGen simulator with foundation-model perception and LLM-driven robot control.
nodes.w: Shows a sim plus foundation-model workflow for aerial autonomy, close to 'LLM in the loop' hackathon ideas.
nodes.h: Uses the hosted GRID platform for the sim side; check account requirements before relying on it.

nodes.s: Open-source flight dynamics model library for fixed-wing and other aircraft, used by FlightGear and as an ArduPilot SITL backend.
nodes.w: Credible fixed-wing dynamics for testing navigation filters on aircraft profiles rather than quadcopters.
nodes.h: Python bindings via pip. Combine with ArduPilot SITL for an autopilot loop.

nodes.s: Lightweight point-realistic lidar simulator for UAVs from HKU MaRS, supporting rotating and solid-state lidar patterns.
nodes.w: Fast way to test lidar-based UAV navigation and planning without a full game-engine sim.
nodes.h: ROS based; runs on CPU or modest GPU. Pairs well with FAST-LIO-style stacks.

nodes.s: Event camera simulator from UZH RPG that renders event streams from simulated scenes.
nodes.w: Generates event-camera data for high-speed or low-light VIO research without hardware.
nodes.h: ROS1 and older build tooling. For converting existing video to events, rpg_vid2e is easier.

nodes.s: Python package and CLI for evaluating odometry and SLAM trajectories (ATE/RPE, alignment, plotting) in TUM, KITTI, EuRoC and ROS bag formats.
nodes.w: The default way to score a nav or SLAM result against ground truth; essential for any demo that claims accuracy.
nodes.h: pip install evo. Run evo_ape with alignment flags; it reads most dataset ground-truth formats directly.

nodes.s: Toolbox for quantitative trajectory evaluation of VO/VIO, implementing the alignment and relative-error protocol from Zhang & Scaramuzza (IROS 2018).
nodes.w: Implements the alignment conventions used in many VIO benchmarks; good for apples-to-apples comparisons.
nodes.h: Old Python 2 era code, ROS optional. evo is easier for quick use.

nodes.s: Python loaders for the KITTI raw and odometry datasets.
nodes.w: Removes boilerplate when using KITTI's GPS/IMU, lidar and stereo data for localization experiments.
nodes.h: pip install pykitti and point it at the dataset folders.

nodes.s: Companion repo for the UZH-FPV drone racing dataset with scripts and info.
nodes.w: Aggressive high-speed drone sequences stress VIO well beyond EuRoC.
nodes.h: Inactive since 2020; dataset itself is on the UZH site.

nodes.s: Repository for the 2022 Hilti SLAM Challenge with dataset info and evaluation tooling.
nodes.w: Construction-site sequences with accurate ground truth; a strong test of lidar/visual-inertial SLAM in GNSS-denied indoor spaces.
nodes.h: Download bags from the challenge site; scoring scripts in repo.

nodes.s: Repository for the 2023 Hilti SLAM Challenge, including multi-session sequences.
nodes.w: Multi-session data is useful for map reuse and relocalization experiments.
nodes.h: Same workflow as 2022; check the challenge site for current download links.

nodes.s: Site repo for MCD, a multi-campus dataset across Asia and Europe with spinning and non-repetitive lidar, stereo cameras, IMUs, UWB ranging, survey-grade prior maps and continuous-time ground truth.
nodes.w: Covers localization against prior maps and UWB-aided fusion in large outdoor areas.
nodes.h: Data downloads and tutorials are linked from the site.

nodes.s: Site repo for NTU VIRAL, an aerial dataset with lidars, cameras, IMU and UWB ranging from a drone.
nodes.w: Rare UWB-equipped drone dataset for range-aided fusion experiments.
nodes.h: ROS bags; download links on the site.

nodes.s: Multi-modal, multi-scenario ground robot dataset from SJTU with cameras, lidar, IMU, GNSS and more, indoor and outdoor.
nodes.w: Indoor/outdoor transitions with GNSS make it useful for testing GNSS-loss handling in fusion.
nodes.h: ROS bags; check repo for download mirrors.

nodes.s: Dataset with synchronized visual, inertial and raw GNSS measurements released with GVINS.
nodes.w: One of few datasets with raw GNSS pseudoranges plus camera and IMU, needed for tightly coupled GNSS-VIO.
nodes.h: ROS bags with custom GNSS message types; install the gnss_comm package.

nodes.s: Open multisensor urban positioning dataset from PolyU IPNL with GNSS, IMU, lidar and camera in deep urban canyons.
nodes.w: Benchmark for GNSS multipath and NLOS mitigation in cities.
nodes.h: Pick one Hong Kong sequence and run an RTKLIB plus loosely coupled baseline to show urban degradation.

nodes.s: Aerial-view, large-scale, terrain-oriented dataset for aerial place recognition and localization.
nodes.w: Directly targets UAV localization over terrain when GNSS is unavailable.
nodes.h: Inactive since 2022; check that the download links still work before planning around it.

nodes.s: Repo for VPAIR, an aerial visual place recognition dataset matching low-altitude flight imagery to reference orthophotos.
nodes.w: Benchmark for UAV visual geolocalization against georeferenced maps.
nodes.h: Small enough to evaluate quickly with VPR-methods-evaluation.

nodes.s: Visual geo-localization dataset and code designed for aerial vehicles.
nodes.w: Another aerial-to-map benchmark with sequential flights, useful for testing filtering over VPR outputs.
nodes.h: Check README for map tile download steps.

nodes.s: Tools for the Mapillary Street-level Sequences dataset for lifelong visual place recognition.
nodes.w: Large, diverse street-level VPR benchmark used to train many current VPR models.
nodes.h: Dataset download needs registration on Mapillary.

nodes.s: Open-source visual place recognition evaluation framework from the IJCV paper, with many datasets and techniques integrated.
nodes.w: Ready harness to compare VPR methods across conditions and viewpoints.
nodes.h: Older dependencies; consider VPR-methods-evaluation for modern models.

nodes.s: Python package for downloading, customizing and iterating the TartanAir-V2 synthetic dataset.
nodes.w: TartanAir's photorealistic scenes with weather and lighting variety stress-test SLAM and VO.
nodes.h: Download only the environments and modalities you need - full set is very large.

nodes.s: Devkit for the Boreas multi-season driving dataset with radar, lidar, camera and GNSS/INS ground truth.
nodes.w: Radar plus lidar over seasons and snow suits all-weather localization work.
nodes.h: Data is hosted on S3; download selected sequences.

nodes.s: SDK for the Oxford RobotCar dataset with loaders and projection tools.
nodes.w: Long-term, all-condition driving data is a staple for localization and place recognition research.
nodes.h: Inactive since 2022; Python and MATLAB helpers still work.

nodes.s: MIT dataset of aggressive indoor quadrotor flights with real IMU and motor data and rendered camera imagery.
nodes.w: Combines real flight dynamics with synthetic vision, good for VIO under aggressive motion.
nodes.h: Inactive since 2022; download scripts may need adaptation.

nodes.s: Feature-based SLAM for monocular, stereo and RGB-D cameras using ORB features, with loop closing and relocalization against a reusable map.
nodes.w: The reference visual SLAM baseline most papers compare against; cheap camera-only localization when GNSS is denied.
nodes.h: Superseded by ORB-SLAM3 and no longer developed; builds need patching on modern OpenCV/Eigen. Use only to reproduce old baselines.

nodes.s: Visual, visual-inertial and multi-map SLAM supporting monocular, stereo and RGB-D cameras with pinhole and fisheye models, using a map atlas to survive tracking loss.
nodes.w: Still the most cited open VI-SLAM system; a solid GNSS-denied drift baseline for drones and ground robots.
nodes.h: Build against Pangolin, OpenCV and Eigen; expect a few compile fixes. Run on EuRoC or TUM-VI first, then your own camera after Kalibr calibration. Upstream sees little activity.

nodes.s: ROS 2 wrapper package that exposes ORB-SLAM3 as nodes for monocular, stereo and RGB-D input.
nodes.w: Shortest path to running ORB-SLAM3 inside a ROS 2 robot stack.
nodes.h: Needs a working ORB-SLAM3 build first; check the README for the ROS 2 distro it targets before choosing your Docker base image.

nodes.s: Optimization-based monocular visual-inertial estimator with sliding-window bundle adjustment, online initialization, loop closure and pose-graph reuse.
nodes.w: The canonical one-camera-plus-IMU estimator; works on light UAV payloads where stereo or LiDAR is too heavy.
nodes.h: ROS 1 only and no longer maintained; run in a Melodic/Noetic container. Sensitive to time sync and initialization motion.

nodes.s: Extension of VINS-Mono supporting mono+IMU, stereo, and stereo+IMU, with optional loose fusion of global sensors such as GPS.
nodes.w: Shows how to plug intermittent GNSS into a VIO estimator, which is the core pattern for degraded-PNT navigation.
nodes.h: ROS 1; use a Docker image. The global-fusion node is a good template for injecting GNSS when it is trusted and dropping it when jammed.

nodes.s: MSCKF-based visual-inertial navigation platform with online calibration, a simulator, and extensive documentation for research use.
nodes.w: Probably the best-documented VIO codebase; filter-based, light enough for embedded boards.
nodes.h: Supports ROS 1 and ROS 2. Its built-in simulator lets you test without hardware on day one. Docs site explains every estimator component.

nodes.s: Multi-sensor aided inertial navigation that fuses IMU with camera, LiDAR, GNSS and wheel odometry, including online spatial/temporal calibration and a multi-sensor simulator.
nodes.w: Directly relevant to assured PNT: one estimator that degrades gracefully as individual sensors (including GNSS) drop out.
nodes.h: Start with the provided simulated data to see each sensor's contribution, then disable GNSS mid-run to demo a jamming scenario.

nodes.s: Stereo visual-inertial odometry with a factor-graph backend, robust loop closure and real-time 3D mesh generation; the odometry core of the Kimera stack.
nodes.w: Gives both a pose and a lightweight 3D mesh, useful for situational-awareness displays.
nodes.h: Heavier build (GTSAM, OpenGV, DBoW2); use the Docker setup. The ROS wrapper lives in a separate repo.

nodes.s: Robust pose-graph optimization that rejects bad loop closures via pairwise consistency maximization on top of GTSAM.
nodes.w: Outlier-robust loop closure is what keeps a long GNSS-denied mission from corrupting its map; reusable outside Kimera.
nodes.h: Small library; feed it any odometry + loop closure edges. Good drop-in back end for a custom front end.

nodes.s: GitHub mirror of Basalt, a visual-inertial odometry and mapping system built around non-linear factor recovery, with calibration tools; primary development is on GitLab.
nodes.w: Fast, accurate stereo VIO that runs well on CPUs; also ships camera-IMU calibration.
nodes.h: Submit issues upstream on GitLab. Builds cleanly on Ubuntu; ROS integration is via community wrappers.

nodes.s: Open release of SVO Pro: semi-direct visual(-inertial) odometry with fisheye/omni camera support, optional global map and loop closure.
nodes.w: Very low-latency front end suited to fast agile flight on compute-limited drones.
nodes.h: ROS 1 / catkin build; dormant since 2024. Good when CPU budget is tight.

nodes.s: Direct monocular visual odometry that optimizes photometric error over a sparse set of pixels with joint photometric calibration.
nodes.w: Works in low-texture scenes where feature-based methods fail; the basis for DM-VIO and many direct methods.
nodes.h: No IMU, no loop closure, scale-ambiguous; mostly useful as a building block or comparison.

nodes.s: Monocular visual-inertial odometry built on DSO using delayed marginalization and pose-graph bundle adjustment for IMU initialization.
nodes.w: Strong monocular VIO accuracy; good for single-camera drones.
nodes.h: Standalone build with an optional ROS wrapper repo. Expects photometrically calibrated input for best results.

nodes.s: Robust visual-inertial odometry using an iterated EKF directly on image-patch photometric errors.
nodes.w: Long a go-to VIO on PX4/MAV research platforms because it is cheap to run.
nodes.h: ROS 1 / catkin. Lightweight; tuning of patch and feature counts matters.

nodes.s: Stereo multi-state constraint Kalman filter VIO designed for fast autonomous flight.
nodes.w: Lean filter-based stereo VIO that runs comfortably on embedded CPUs.
nodes.h: ROS 1; unmaintained. Tested heavily on EuRoC; good comparison point to OpenVINS.

nodes.s: Keyframe-based visual-inertial SLAM with loop closure and a realtime scalable factor-graph design; second generation of OKVIS.
nodes.w: Mature research VI-SLAM from the ETH/TUM lineage with active maintenance.
nodes.h: CMake build; check the README for ROS integration and the camera/IMU config format for your sensor.

nodes.s: Extension of OKVIS2 that can additionally use dense depth or LiDAR and fuse GNSS.
nodes.w: Recent (2025-2026) multi-sensor VI-SLAM that includes GNSS fusion, matching assured-PNT architectures.
nodes.h: New codebase; expect some setup friction. Good showcase for switching GNSS on/off.

nodes.s: Point-and-line visual(-inertial) SLAM using learned features, designed for illumination-robust operation, with TensorRT acceleration; successor to AirVO.
nodes.w: Targets lighting changes (dawn/dusk/night), a common failure mode for camera navigation.
nodes.h: Needs an NVIDIA GPU (TensorRT). Docker recommended.

nodes.s: Modular multi-session, multi-modal mapping framework with map merging, optimization and localization against saved maps.
nodes.w: Build a map once, then localize repeatedly against it; supports multi-robot and multi-session merges.
nodes.h: Large ROS 1 codebase; only worth it if you need persistent map management.

nodes.s: Graph-based SLAM library and app supporting RGB-D, stereo and LiDAR, with memory management for large-scale loop closure and map reuse.
nodes.w: Practical all-rounder with GUI, database and localization modes; easiest way to get a working 3D map on a ground robot.
nodes.h: Install via apt binaries (ROS) or the standalone app. Supports phone/iPad LiDAR capture. Save a map, then switch to localization mode.

nodes.s: ROS and ROS 2 integration for RTAB-Map, exposing SLAM, localization and odometry nodes.
nodes.w: Drop-in SLAM for ROS 2 Nav2 stacks.
nodes.h: apt-installable for supported distros; launch examples cover common sensors.

nodes.s: Deep visual SLAM that iterates dense bundle adjustment through a recurrent update operator, for monocular, stereo and RGB-D input.
nodes.w: Much more robust than classic pipelines on hard sequences; strong learned baseline.
nodes.h: Needs a large-memory NVIDIA GPU; not real-time on embedded. Pretrained weights available.

nodes.s: Deep Patch Visual Odometry: learned sparse patch tracking for VO, plus DPV-SLAM with loop closure.
nodes.w: Lighter learned VO than DROID-SLAM, closer to real-time on a desktop GPU.
nodes.h: CUDA build of custom kernels; follow the conda instructions.

nodes.s: Real-time dense monocular SLAM built on the MASt3R two-view 3D reconstruction prior, needing no fixed camera model (CVPR 2025).
nodes.w: Works with uncalibrated cameras, useful for opportunistic imagery from unknown cameras.
nodes.h: Requires a capable NVIDIA GPU and model checkpoint downloads. Great demo value on handheld video.

nodes.s: Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer: a feed-forward network predicting camera poses, depth and point maps from one or many images (CVPR 2025 best paper).
nodes.w: Instant pose and geometry from a handful of frames; a building block for learned relocalization and mapping.
nodes.h: GPU inference via PyTorch; Hugging Face demo for quick tests. Not a full SLAM system by itself.

nodes.s: Gaussian-splatting SLAM for monocular, stereo and RGB-D cameras that tracks and maps directly against a 3D Gaussian representation.
nodes.w: Produces photorealistic maps useful for operator situational awareness and later simulation.
nodes.h: Needs a strong GPU; not real-time on embedded hardware. Best as an offline mapping demo.

nodes.s: Dense RGB-D SLAM that tracks and maps using 3D Gaussians and differentiable rendering (CVPR 2024).
nodes.w: Reference Gaussian-splatting SLAM for RGB-D sensors.
nodes.h: GPU-heavy and slower than real time; good for offline indoor captures.

nodes.s: Couples ORB-SLAM3-style geometric tracking with a photorealistic Gaussian map for monocular, stereo and RGB-D cameras (CVPR 2024).
nodes.w: Classic robust tracking plus a nice-looking map, closer to real time than pure splatting SLAM.
nodes.h: LibTorch + CUDA build; check version pins carefully.

nodes.s: Event-based stereo visual odometry using spatio-temporal consistency of two event cameras for mapping and tracking.
nodes.w: Event cameras keep working under high dynamic range and fast motion, where frame cameras blur or saturate.
nodes.h: Needs stereo event cameras or recorded datasets; ROS 1.

nodes.s: Open-source release of Ultimate SLAM, combining events, standard frames and IMU for VIO in HDR and high-speed scenarios (RA-L 2018).
nodes.w: Template for fusing event cameras with frames and IMU for robust flight state estimation.
nodes.h: ROS 1 / catkin; test on event datasets before buying hardware.

nodes.s: Community-curated list of event-camera papers, datasets, drivers, simulators and code.
nodes.w: Fastest way to find event-camera datasets and odometry code.
nodes.h: Use as a discovery index; not runnable code.

nodes.s: Dataset and index of event-based VO, VIO and SLAM work from HKU ArcLab, including stereo event sequences.
nodes.w: Ready-made event data for testing event odometry without hardware.
nodes.h: Download sequences as rosbags; pair with ESVO.

nodes.s: Visual-thermal-inertial odometry extending ROVIO to fuse asynchronous thermal and visual images with IMU, switching to whichever camera is informative.
nodes.w: Thermal keeps odometry alive in darkness and smoke; NTNU ARL targets subterranean and degraded environments.
nodes.h: Needs a thermal camera synced to IMU (or their datasets). Thermal calibration targets need a heated pattern.

nodes.s: Edge-based monocular thermal-inertial odometry that tracks thermal edges for visually degraded environments.
nodes.w: Low-cost night/smoke navigation from a single thermal camera plus IMU.
nodes.h: Code released with the paper; try on public thermal datasets first.

nodes.s: Radar visual/thermal inertial odometry fusing 4D mmWave radar with a visual or thermal camera and IMU for degraded visual conditions.
nodes.w: Radar plus thermal is a strong combination for fog, smoke and darkness.
nodes.h: ROS 1; datasets released by the author. Good for a degraded-visibility demo.

nodes.s: EKF-based radar-inertial odometry using 4D mmWave radar ego-velocity measurements.
nodes.w: Cheap automotive radars give velocity in fog/smoke/darkness; a minimal radar odometry template.
nodes.h: ROS 1; uses the author's radar ego-velocity estimator. Works with TI mmWave-class sensors.

nodes.s: 4D radar SLAM with scan-to-scan registration, loop closure and pose-graph optimization, released with an NTU 4D radar dataset.
nodes.w: One of the few full SLAM pipelines for 4D imaging radar, the all-weather sensor for ground vehicles.
nodes.h: ROS 1; structured like hdl_graph_slam. Test on their dataset first.

nodes.s: Learning-free spinning-radar odometry that filters returns to sparse oriented surface points and registers against keyframes.
nodes.w: Strong baseline for spinning (Navtech-style) radar odometry; robust in weather that defeats LiDAR.
nodes.h: ROS 1; benchmarked on Oxford Radar RobotCar and Boreas.

nodes.s: Ground-optimized 4D radar-inertial odometry integrating continuous velocity via Gaussian processes (ICRA 2025 best paper finalist).
nodes.w: Recent state of the art for 4D radar odometry on ground vehicles.
nodes.h: Recent code; check sensor assumptions against your radar.

nodes.s: 4D radar-inertial odometry using Gaussian modeling of radar points and multi-hypothesis scan matching.
nodes.w: Another recent open 4D radar odometry baseline, useful for comparison.
nodes.h: Small research codebase; read the paper before integrating.

nodes.s: Tightly coupled LiDAR-inertial odometry via factor-graph smoothing, with optional GPS factors and loop closure.
nodes.w: Popular LIO with built-in GNSS factors; the template for LiDAR+INS+intermittent GNSS.
nodes.h: ROS 1 main branch, community ROS 2 branch. Needs a 9-axis IMU and careful extrinsics.

nodes.s: Computationally efficient LiDAR-inertial odometry using an iterated error-state Kalman filter and incremental k-d tree map, mapping raw points directly.
nodes.w: The default LIO in many field robots; runs on ARM boards and supports solid-state and spinning LiDARs.
nodes.h: Easiest LIO to get running; Livox drivers supported. No loop closure; pair with a localization or loop-closure add-on.

nodes.s: High-bandwidth LiDAR-inertial odometry that updates the state point by point, tolerating aggressive motion and IMU saturation.
nodes.w: Handles violent motion (agile drones, vibration) where frame-based LIO breaks.
nodes.h: Same ecosystem as FAST-LIO; try when FAST-LIO diverges on aggressive motion.

nodes.s: Direct LiDAR-inertial-visual odometry fusing LiDAR, camera and IMU in a sequential ESIKF update with a unified voxel map.
nodes.w: High-accuracy colored mapping that stays robust when either LiDAR or camera degrades.
nodes.h: Needs hardware-synced LiDAR+camera; datasets available.

nodes.s: Tightly coupled LiDAR-inertial-visual estimation and RGB-colored mapping package.
nodes.w: Produces dense colored maps useful for operator displays and mapping.
nodes.h: ROS 1, heavy on dependencies; FAST-LIVO2 is the newer alternative.

nodes.s: Minimal LiDAR odometry based on point-to-point ICP with adaptive thresholding, working across sensors with few parameters.
nodes.w: Works out of the box on almost any LiDAR without IMU; ideal hackathon starting point.
nodes.h: `pip install kiss-icp` and run on a rosbag or KITTI folder in minutes. Add KISS-SLAM for loop closure.

nodes.s: LiDAR SLAM that adds loop closure and pose-graph optimization on top of KISS-ICP odometry.
nodes.w: Full LiDAR SLAM with the same low-configuration philosophy.
nodes.h: Pip-installable; quick to demo on outdoor bags.

nodes.s: Loop-closure detection using bird's-eye-view density images of local LiDAR maps.
nodes.w: Sensor-agnostic loop closure that plugs into any LiDAR odometry.
nodes.h: Python bindings via pip.

nodes.s: LiDAR-inertial odometry aiming to work without sensor-specific modelling or heavy tuning.
nodes.w: Recent (2025-2026) LIO from the KISS-ICP group; good for unknown hardware.
nodes.h: `pip install "rko_lio[all]"` then `rko_lio -v /path/to/bags` runs on ROS 1 or ROS 2 bags with a rerun viewer; a ROS 2 node is also available. You must supply IMU and LiDAR extrinsics if the bag's TF tree lacks them. No loop closure - see rko_slam for that.

nodes.s: Lightweight ground-optimized LiDAR odometry and mapping that segments ground to speed up feature extraction on UGVs.
nodes.w: Classic UGV LiDAR SLAM for rough terrain on modest compute.
nodes.h: ROS 1 only, unmaintained, tuned for Velodyne VLP-16. Use LIO-SAM or KISS-ICP instead unless reproducing baselines.

nodes.s: Real-time 2D and 3D SLAM with submaps and branch-and-bound loop closure across many sensor configurations.
nodes.w: Widely deployed 2D LiDAR SLAM for indoor and warehouse robots.
nodes.h: Project is in maintenance mode with little activity. Still available via ROS packages and works for 2D indoor mapping.

nodes.s: Versatile point-cloud localization and mapping framework with GPU-accelerated factor graphs, supporting many range sensors and optional IMU.
nodes.w: Modern, maintained 3D mapping with GPU speedups and an extensible module system.
nodes.h: Prebuilt packages exist for ROS 2; GPU optional but recommended.

nodes.s: Collection of fast GICP and VGICP point-cloud registration implementations, multithreaded and CUDA.
nodes.w: Fast scan registration building block used by many LiDAR and radar SLAM systems.
nodes.h: Successor library small_gicp is more actively maintained.

nodes.s: Efficient, parallel point-cloud registration library (GICP, ICP variants) with C++ and Python APIs.
nodes.w: Pip-installable registration to build your own LiDAR odometry or map-based relocalization fast.
nodes.h: `pip install small_gicp`; good for scan-to-map localization prototypes.

nodes.s: Lightweight tightly coupled LiDAR-inertial odometry using parallel sparse incremental voxels instead of a k-d tree.
nodes.w: Faster variant of the FAST-LIO design for constrained compute.
nodes.h: ROS 1; same config style as FAST-LIO.

nodes.s: Lightweight LiDAR-inertial odometry with coarse-to-fine continuous-time motion correction (ICRA 2023).
nodes.w: Accurate and compute-light LIO for aerial and ground robots.
nodes.h: ROS 1 main; check community ROS 2 forks.

nodes.s: Relocalization in a prebuilt map using FAST-LIO odometry plus global scan-to-map registration.
nodes.w: Localize in a map you surveyed earlier, the standard pattern for GNSS-denied ground ops in known areas.
nodes.h: ROS 1; build a map with FAST-LIO first, then localize. Needs a rough initial pose (RViz or another sensor). The global-localization node needs Python 2.7 and Open3D 0.9, so plan for a Melodic-era environment or a container.

nodes.s: LiDAR global place descriptor for loop detection and relocalization (backup of the original IRAP KAIST repo).
nodes.w: Simple, widely used LiDAR loop-closure descriptor; plugs into most LiDAR SLAM.
nodes.h: Header-only style C++; SC-LIO-SAM shows integration.

nodes.s: LIO-SAM combined with Scan Context loop closure for more reliable large-scale LiDAR-inertial SLAM.
nodes.w: Practical recipe for adding a global descriptor to an existing LIO.
nodes.h: ROS 1; same setup as LIO-SAM.

nodes.s: Stable Triangle Descriptor for 3D point-cloud place recognition and loop closure.
nodes.w: Works with solid-state LiDARs and small fields of view where Scan Context struggles.
nodes.h: ROS 1 demos; integrates with FAST-LIO.

nodes.s: Certifiable, outlier-robust point-cloud registration library with C++, Python and MATLAB bindings.
nodes.w: Global registration that tolerates extreme outlier rates, useful for map-to-map alignment and relocalization.
nodes.h: Needs correspondences (e.g. FPFH) as input; Python bindings make it quick to prototype.

nodes.s: Fast, robust global registration for terrestrial robots that assumes near-planar motion to cut degrees of freedom.
nodes.w: Faster global relocalization for ground vehicles.
nodes.h: Smaller research codebase; pair with KISS-ICP.

nodes.s: Tightly coupled sliding-window factor-graph fusion of IMU with LiDAR (geometric and photometric), radar radial-speed factors and external odometry such as VIO.
nodes.w: From the group behind DARPA SubT field robots; relevant to smoke/dark/dust scenarios.
nodes.h: ROS Noetic; publishes nav_msgs/Odometry. Radar factor lets you keep velocity constraints when LiDAR is blinded by dust or smoke.

nodes.s: ROS 1/ROS 2 driver for Livox LiDARs such as Mid-360 and HAP.
nodes.w: Mid-360 is a common cheap LiDAR for drones; you need this driver to feed FAST-LIO and friends.
nodes.h: Build with the Livox SDK2; set the custom message format expected by FAST-LIO.

nodes.s: 3D LiDAR graph SLAM with NDT/GICP scan matching odometry, loop detection and optional GPS, IMU and floor-plane constraints.
nodes.w: Simple, hackable graph SLAM that 4DRadarSLAM and others build on; GPS constraints make it handy for mixed GNSS/denied runs.
nodes.h: ROS 1; GLIM is the author's newer framework.

nodes.s: Distributed back end of Kimera-Multi handling inter-robot loop closures and distributed optimization.
nodes.w: Reusable distributed SLAM back end.
nodes.h: Used through Kimera-Multi.

nodes.s: Distributed pose-graph optimization library with certifiably correct solutions for multi-robot SLAM.
nodes.w: Solver core for decentralized multi-robot SLAM.
nodes.h: Library only; feed it pose graphs from each robot.

nodes.s: ROS 2 decentralized collaborative SLAM supporting LiDAR, stereo and RGB-D, with sparse inter-robot communication.
nodes.w: Designed for bandwidth-limited swarms, a realistic constraint under jamming.
nodes.h: ROS 2; experiments run on recorded multi-robot datasets. Pick one sensor type to start.

nodes.s: Centralized collaborative visual-inertial SLAM where agents run VIO and a server merges maps; COVINS-G is VIO-front-end agnostic.
nodes.w: Pattern for drones sharing maps through a ground station.
nodes.h: ROS 1 + Docker; COVINS-G can take poses from any VIO such as OpenVINS.

nodes.s: English edition of Gao Xiang's open textbook on visual SLAM, from geometry and Lie groups to back-end optimization.
nodes.w: Best free practical intro for a team ramping up on SLAM in a weekend.
nodes.h: PDF and code exercises (slambook2 repo).

nodes.s: ROS-based software stack and Raspberry Pi image for the Clover educational quadcopter (PX4 underneath). Ships ArUco marker detection, marker-map navigation published to PX4 as a vision position estimate, downward optical-flow position hold, and a Gazebo simulator. Documentation is written in Russian first, with English translations.
nodes.w: One of the most complete Russian-language open stacks for GNSS-free indoor/outdoor flight: optical flow plus marker maps fed into the autopilot EKF, with documented parameter sets.
nodes.h: Use the Docker/VM simulator image to fly ArUco-map navigation without hardware in hours. The marker-map => VPE path is a ready template for any external position source into PX4. ROS1 (Noetic) based; ROS2 only via community ports. Canonical repo is CopterExpress/clover; klever-coex/clover is a recent fork.

nodes.s: Python/OpenCV return-to-home for a quadcopter with a downward camera and no GPS. Instead of integrating optical flow, it stores keyframes ('rungs') on the way out and, on the way back, matches the nearest rung and truncates history, sending the residual offset to the controller. README and the companion Habr article are in Russian.
nodes.w: A small, readable alternative to drift-prone flow integration for the specific job of getting home when GNSS is gone; the same idea as teach-and-repeat.
nodes.h: Pure Python + OpenCV, runs on a laptop against recorded downward video. Integration with a flight controller is left to the user (README sends offsets; no MAVLink bridge verified). Good seed for a 'return home under jamming' demo.

nodes.s: Russian-language hackathon solution for 'Полёт вслепую' (Blind flight): estimate aircraft position, ground speed and heading without GNSS by reconstructing a terrain profile (barometric altitude minus radar altimeter) and matching it against a DEM, TERCOM style.
nodes.w: A compact, documented TERCOM pipeline on real DEM data; shows how a GNSS-denied hackathon problem was posed and solved in 2026.
nodes.h: Reads DEM + altimeter series; small dependency set. Useful as a baseline if a hackathon gives altimeter/DEM data. Accuracy figures are not independently checked here.

nodes.s: Second public solution to the same 'Полёт вслепую' hackathon task: web prototype that reads a GeoTIFF DEM and NMEA-0183 radar-altimeter messages, searches start point, speed and azimuth hypotheses by RMSE/correlation, and reports a confidence and a flat-terrain check.
nodes.w: Shows the practical details (UTM projection, bilinear DEM sampling, weighted scoring for informative relief, flat-terrain rejection) that a TERCOM demo needs.
nodes.h: Streamlit app on rasterio + pyproj; an optional Rust core (built automatically if cargo is installed) speeds up the hypothesis search. Includes a synthetic NMEA generator from a real DEM, which is handy for building test data fast. Small repo (about a dozen commits).

nodes.s: Controller for an autonomous ground cargo platform in the amr-sim simulator plus an operator workstation, built for the 'Безопасный маршрут' case of KosmoHackathon 2026 (2nd place in the final). A Kalman filter fuses wheel odometry, gyro and lidar-to-wall-map matching to keep position in GNSS shadow, and speed is set from a 3 s pedestrian motion forecast.
nodes.w: Worked example of GNSS-shadow ground navigation with a scored simulator benchmark, written in Russian.
nodes.h: README reports position error and collision results against the organisers' baseline (their numbers, not verified here). Depends on the organisers' amr-sim, which may not be public.

nodes.s: Pet project for local UAV navigation without GNSS: AirSim video streamed over ZeroMQ into monocular ORB-SLAM3, a ROS node converts NED/ENU frames, IMU data corrects monocular scale, and a PID controller tracks a trajectory. Russian README.
nodes.w: A minimal end-to-end sim loop (simulator => SLAM => control) that a team can copy to test VO under GNSS loss.
nodes.h: Needs ORB-SLAM3 built separately and AirSim (archived upstream). Useful mainly as an architecture reference.

nodes.s: Russian graduate thesis code: 'Development of a UAV inertial navigation module using auxiliary navigation data'. C++ client for INS/GNSS fusion, a C# flight simulator with sensor emulation, a Node.js telemetry server and a Vue web UI.
nodes.w: Small, self-contained INS + aiding simulator with a visual front-end; good for teaching drift and aiding.
nodes.h: Mixed C++/C#/Node stack; setup cost moderate. Treat as reference, not a library.

nodes.s: MIPT (FAKT) 2026 diploma: local navigation for a UAV under GNSS suppression, correcting a strapdown INS with LoRa two-way-ranging (TWR) distances to ground beacons. Python code includes INS mechanization, an error-state EKF, a tightly coupled MSCKF variant, least-squares triangulation, an IMU simulator and parameter studies; thesis and slides are in Russian (.docx/.pptx).
nodes.w: Open, inspectable version of the 'ground beacons instead of satellites' approach that Ukrainian vendors also describe publicly (see Vyriy beacon navigation).
