nodes.h: Pure Python simulation, no hardware needed; good basis for a beacon-ranging + INS demo. No README; read Code/main.py and the thesis.

nodes.s: Scripts (packaged as an agent skill) that repair Garmin/Strava .fit activities corrupted by GNSS spoofing or jamming: tracks that teleport to a fixed far-away location, impossible speed spikes, phantom distance. Bilingual English/Ukrainian README written from the Ukrainian civilian experience of EW.
nodes.w: Encodes practical spoof signatures seen by civilians in Ukraine (position jumps, speed outliers) as simple detection rules; a quick start for track-level spoof detection.
nodes.h: Tiny Python codebase; the detection heuristics can be lifted into any trajectory plausibility checker. Very new (Oct 2026).

nodes.s: Unofficial Ukrainian translation of key sections of the ArduPilot Copter documentation, with a translation-status file and a built site. CC BY-SA 3.0 like the original.
nodes.w: Lowers the entry barrier for Ukrainian-speaking teams and operators configuring ArduPilot, including non-GPS navigation sections.
nodes.h: Reference only. May lag the English wiki; the original wins on conflicts.

nodes.s: Student project from SPbU (CITEC) on returning a UAV to its launch point when both GNSS and the ground-station link are lost, targeting a RockPi 4 companion computer. Description in Russian; README is minimal and points to an external Notion board.
nodes.w: Same problem statement as many Ukrainian field requirements (lost link + lost GNSS => come home), from the Russian academic side.
nodes.h: Sparse docs; read the C sources directly. Reference value only.

nodes.s: Meta-repository from Russian vendor Geoscan for the Pioneer Max educational quadcopter: system images, ROS workspace, web control apps and guides, documented in Russian.
nodes.w: Shows how a Russian educational drone ecosystem packages ROS, mission tools and indoor positioning for schools and competitions.
nodes.h: Hardware-specific; useful only as reference for packaging and docs. Last push March 2024.

nodes.n: Vision-based GNSS-Free Localization for UAVs in the Wild
nodes.s: Proposes matching drone camera frames to open satellite imagery with learned feature matching to get absolute position without GNSS, evaluated on flights over non-urban areas.
nodes.kt: Satellite tiles + learned matcher is a workable visual GPS baseline Failure cases cluster over low-texture and changed terrain

nodes.n: AnyLoc: Towards Universal Visual Place Recognition
nodes.s: Shows that unsupervised aggregation of foundation-model (DINOv2) features gives place recognition that generalizes across domains including aerial imagery, without VPR-specific training.
nodes.kt: Foundation features + VLAD work training-free Aerial domain included in the evaluation

nodes.n: Exploring the best way for UAV visual localization under Low-altitude Multi-view Observation Condition: a Benchmark
nodes.s: Builds a benchmark for low-altitude, oblique-view UAV absolute visual localization and systematically compares retrieval, matching and refinement choices.
nodes.kt: Low-altitude oblique views are much harder than nadir Gives evidence for picking retrieval/matcher combos

nodes.n: UAV-VisLoc: A Large-scale Dataset for UAV Visual Localization
nodes.s: Introduces a dataset of real UAV flight images paired with satellite maps over varied terrain for evaluating UAV visual localization.
nodes.kt: Real flights with ground truth Covers terrain types beyond cities

nodes.n: Long-range UAV Thermal Geo-localization with Satellite Imagery
nodes.s: Matches night-time UAV thermal imagery to satellite RGB maps using domain adaptation to cope with scarce paired thermal-satellite data; releases code and a nighttime dataset.
nodes.kt: Night visual GPS is possible via thermal-to-RGB matching Domain adaptation offsets missing paired data

nodes.n: STHN: Deep Homography Estimation for UAV Thermal Geo-localization with Satellite Imagery
nodes.s: Refines thermal-to-satellite localization with learned homography estimation for precise alignment.
nodes.kt: Coarse-to-fine: retrieval then homography

nodes.n: UASTHN: Uncertainty-Aware Deep Homography Estimation for UAV Satellite-Thermal Geo-localization
nodes.s: Adds uncertainty estimation to satellite-thermal homography so a navigation filter can weight or reject visual fixes.
nodes.kt: Uncertainty makes visual fixes filter-ready

nodes.n: University-1652: A Multi-view Multi-source Benchmark for Drone-based Geo-localization
nodes.s: Introduces the drone/satellite/ground benchmark that most drone cross-view geo-localization work evaluates on.
nodes.kt: Defines drone->satellite and satellite->drone retrieval tasks

nodes.n: SUES-200: A Multi-height Multi-scene Cross-view Image Benchmark Across Drone and Satellite
nodes.s: Drone-satellite benchmark with imagery at several flight heights across varied scenes.
nodes.kt: Altitude changes strongly affect retrieval accuracy

nodes.n: Sample4Geo: Hard Negative Sampling For Cross-View Geo-Localisation
nodes.s: Shows that a simple contrastive setup with careful hard-negative sampling performs strongly on cross-view geo-localization benchmarks.
nodes.kt: Data sampling matters as much as architecture

nodes.n: LightGlue: Local Feature Matching at Light Speed
nodes.s: Redesigns SuperGlue-style attention matching to be faster and adaptive, stopping early on easy pairs.
nodes.kt: Adaptive depth trades compute for difficulty Permissive license, easy to deploy

nodes.s: Dense matcher combining foundation-model coarse features with fine refinement, robust to large appearance change.
nodes.kt: Dense warps + certainty help on cross-season, cross-sensor pairs

nodes.n: Grounding Image Matching in 3D with MASt3R
nodes.s: Frames matching as a 3D problem on top of DUSt3R, producing dense matches robust to extreme viewpoint change.
nodes.kt: 3D reasoning handles oblique-vs-nadir gaps

nodes.n: The EAR and Open Source Software

nodes.kt: Code published without restriction is generally outside the EAR Encryption source has an extra BIS/NSA notification step Private repos shared with foreign nationals can count as exports

nodes.s: The regulation text defining when information and software count as 'published' and therefore not subject to the EAR.
nodes.kt: Primary source to cite in an export-control slide Read with 734.3(b)(3) and 742.15(b)

nodes.n: U.S. Export Controls and Published Encryption Source Code Explained
nodes.s: EFF explainer on the 2016-era EAR changes for published encryption source and when email notification is still needed.
nodes.kt: Relevant if your PNT code includes signal authentication crypto

nodes.n: Regulatory Definitions of Publicly Available, Public Domain, and Published (ITAR/EAR)
nodes.s: University compliance guide comparing ITAR public-domain (22 CFR 120.34) and EAR published definitions and the fundamental-research exclusion.
nodes.kt: ITAR-controlled data cannot simply be put in the public domain by an individual Fundamental-research protection can be lost via publication restrictions Military GNSS items (e.g. M-code receivers, some anti-jam antenna tech) may be ITAR or EAR controlled - keep hackathon code on public civil signals and published methods

nodes.n: DOD adopts 5 principles of artificial intelligence ethics
nodes.s: Announcement of the DoD's AI ethical principles - responsible, equitable, traceable, reliable, governable - recommended by the Defense Innovation Board.
nodes.kt: Traceable and governable map to logging and safe fallback in nav autonomy Judges increasingly ask how an AI component can be disengaged

nodes.n: Summary of the NATO Artificial Intelligence Strategy (Principles of Responsible Use)
nodes.s: NATO's 2021 AI strategy summary setting six principles of responsible use: lawfulness, responsibility and accountability, explainability and traceability, reliability, governability, bias mitigation.
nodes.kt: Applies across the whole AI lifecycle Expect a NATO-flavored jury to probe reliability and governability

nodes.n: DoD Directive 3000.09: Autonomy in Weapon Systems (2023 reissue)
nodes.s: DoD policy governing development and use of autonomous and semi-autonomous weapon systems, reissued January 2023. Cited here as the boundary marker: navigation and awareness tools are outside its scope, weapon autonomy is not.
nodes.kt: Clear line between navigation/autonomy for mobility and weapon autonomy Keep hackathon scope on the navigation and awareness side

nodes.s: The EU's recast dual-use export control regulation covering items, software and technology including navigation and avionics categories, with public-domain and basic-research de-control notes.
nodes.kt: Category 7 covers navigation and avionics items Public-domain and basic scientific research notes protect open publication

nodes.n: Commission Recommendation (EU) 2021/1700 on internal compliance programmes for controls of research involving dual-use items
nodes.s: Non-binding guidance helping universities and researchers spot and manage dual-use export risks, with scenarios, red flags and FAQs.
nodes.kt: Practical red-flag checklist for collaborative or international teams Contact national authority when control status is unclear

nodes.n: IS-GPS-200N: NAVSTAR GPS Space Segment / Navigation User Segment Interfaces
nodes.s: The master interface specification for the legacy GPS L1 C/A and L2C (and P(Y) at the public level) signals: code generation, signal structure, and the full LNAV/CNAV navigation message bit layouts. Every GPS receiver, simulator and spoofing detector ultimately decodes against this document.
nodes.kt: Defines LNAV subframe and CNAV message formats bit-for-bit Ephemeris, clock and ionosphere parameter algorithms live here Revisions are managed through the public ICWG process Authoritative source for ephemeris and clock equations Defines L1 C/A and L2C signal structure Needed to build or audit any navigation message decoder

nodes.n: IS-GPS-705J: NAVSTAR GPS Space Segment / User Segment L5 Interfaces
nodes.s: Interface specification for the GPS L5 safety-of-life band signal: I5/Q5 codes, the L5 CNAV message, and signal characteristics. L5's higher chipping rate and wider band make it more robust to narrowband interference than L1 C/A.
nodes.kt: Defines the L5 dataless pilot (Q5) and data (I5) channels CNAV message types shared with L2C Draft uprevisions were discussed at the 2025 public ICWG

nodes.n: IS-GPS-800J: NAVSTAR GPS Space Segment / User Segment L1C Interfaces
nodes.s: Interface specification for the modernized L1C civil signal designed for interoperability with Galileo E1 and other GNSS: BOC/TMBOC modulation, Weil-code ranging codes, and the CNAV-2 message.
nodes.kt: L1C uses a pilot plus data component, like Galileo E1 CNAV-2 adds FEC-coded subframes Key reference for multi-GNSS L1 receiver design

nodes.s: Index page for the public GPS ICDs and ISs (200, 705, 800, 870 etc.), change notices and public ICWG meeting material. Useful to find the current revision and pending changes such as integrity support message formats.
nodes.kt: Single place to check which revision is in force Hosts proposed change notices and meeting redlines Single entry point for all GPS signal ICDs Historic versions also linked

nodes.n: GPS Standard Positioning Service (SPS) Performance Standard, 5th Edition
nodes.s: The formal commitment the US government makes about civil GPS signal-in-space accuracy, availability, continuity and integrity. It is the baseline to compare against when judging whether a receiver anomaly is the signal or interference.
nodes.kt: States guaranteed SIS user range error and availability levels Defines what counts as a major service failure Basis for RAIM and integrity assumptions in aviation

nodes.n: Galileo Open Service Signal-In-Space Interface Control Document (OS SIS ICD) Issue 2.1
nodes.s: Specification of the Galileo open service signals (E1, E5a, E5b, E6 at the structure level) and the F/NAV and I/NAV navigation messages. Needed for any multi-constellation receiver or Galileo decoder.
nodes.kt: Defines I/NAV and F/NAV page layouts Ranging code and modulation details for E1 and E5 Newer issues are listed in the GSC reference documents library Required for decoding Galileo navigation data I/NAV is the carrier for OSNMA bits

nodes.n: Galileo OSNMA Signal-In-Space Interface Control Document Issue 1.1
nodes.s: Defines Open Service Navigation Message Authentication: how TESLA-chain MACs and keys are embedded in spare I/NAV bits so a receiver can cryptographically verify that navigation data came from Galileo. It is the first civil GNSS data-authentication service in operation.
nodes.kt: Uses a TESLA key chain with delayed key disclosure Authenticates navigation data, not the ranging signal itself Requires loose time sync and a public key obtained out of band Civil signal authentication is available today on Galileo E1-B Receivers need loose time synchronization to verify TESLA keys Defines what an authenticated vs unauthenticated navigation message means

nodes.s: Companion to the OSNMA ICD describing how a receiver should process OSNMA: time-sync requirements, key and Merkle-tree handling, verification procedures and how to report authentication status to the user.
nodes.kt: Spells out the receiver time-sync assumption that OSNMA security depends on Covers cold start, key renewal and chain transitions Practical checklist for implementing OSNMA in software Explains which attacks OSNMA does and does not stop (e.g. replay/meaconing limits) Covers key renewal and alert handling

nodes.n: Galileo Open Service Navigation Message Authentication (OSNMA) - service page
nodes.s: Official landing page for the OSNMA service with status, public key and Merkle tree downloads, and links to the ICD and guidelines.
nodes.kt: Where to get the current OSNMA public key and Merkle root Links to service notices and documentation Where to download the cryptographic material receivers need

nodes.n: Galileo High Accuracy Service Signal-In-Space ICD (HAS SIS ICD) Issue 1.0
nodes.s: Defines the free Galileo High Accuracy Service: PPP orbit, clock and bias corrections broadcast on E6-B (and via internet), including message structure and Reed-Solomon encoding.
nodes.kt: Free PPP corrections broadcast from the satellites themselves Enables decimetre-level PPP without a ground subscription E6-B message decoding details for receiver builders

nodes.n: European GNSS Service Centre - Programme Reference Documents
nodes.s: Library of current Galileo ICDs, service definition documents and receiver guidelines (OS, HAS, OSNMA, SAR). Check here for the latest issue numbers before implementing.
nodes.kt: Authoritative versions of all public Galileo specs Includes service definition documents with committed performance Includes the HAS (High Accuracy Service) ICD for free PPP corrections

nodes.n: BeiDou Navigation Satellite System Signal-In-Space ICDs (B1I, B3I, B1C, B2a, B2b)
nodes.s: Official English-language ICD library for BeiDou open service signals, including the BDS-3 B1C and B2a signals that are interoperable with GPS L1C/L5 and Galileo E1/E5a, plus PPP-B2b.
nodes.kt: BDS-3 B1C and B2a are designed for multi-GNSS interoperability PPP-B2b carries free regional precise corrections The BeiDou site is the official distribution channel

nodes.n: QZSS Performance Standards and Interface Specifications (IS-QZSS)
nodes.s: Japan's QZSS interface specifications covering GPS-compatible signals, the L6 CLAS centimetre-level augmentation and MADOCA PPP services.
nodes.kt: QZSS signals are GPS-interoperable and improve urban-canyon availability in Asia-Oceania CLAS and MADOCA give free precise positioning corrections Specs are published openly by the Cabinet Office

nodes.s: The paid-access RTCM v3 standard that defines the binary messages used to stream GNSS corrections and observations (legacy RTK 1001-1012, MSM 1-7 per constellation, ephemerides, SSR). Practically every NTRIP caster and RTK base station speaks it.
nodes.kt: MSM messages replaced legacy observation messages and align with RINEX 3 MSM4/MSM7 are the common choices for RTK Standard itself is purchased; open parsers document much of it

nodes.s: Free encyclopedia overview of the RTCM correction message families and transport (NTRIP) used for real-time kinematic positioning. A good orientation before buying or parsing the RTCM standard.
nodes.kt: Explains the role of RTCM 2.x vs 3.x messages Covers NTRIP for internet transport

nodes.s: The ASCII serial sentence standard (GGA, RMC, GSA, GSV, VTG...) used by nearly all GNSS receivers and marine electronics. The official standard is sold; open references cover the common sentences.
nodes.kt: Talker IDs distinguish GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, BeiDou and multi-GNSS output Checksummed ASCII over serial, easy to parse and to fake Still the lowest-common-denominator GNSS output

nodes.s: CAN bus based marine network standard that carries position, heading, AIS and engine data as PGNs between devices. Paid standard; the community has reverse-documented many PGNs.
nodes.kt: PGNs carry GNSS position, COG/SOG, heading and AIS Plug-and-play backbone on modern vessels Unauthenticated bus, relevant to maritime spoofing resilience

nodes.s: A free, detailed field-by-field reference to NMEA 0183 sentences as actually emitted by real receivers, including vendor quirks and version differences. The practical substitute for the paywalled standard.
nodes.kt: Documents real-world deviations from the standard Covers talker IDs for multi-GNSS output Written by gpsd maintainers who parse these daily

nodes.s: Official documentation for the MAVLink micro air vehicle messaging protocol: message definitions, microservices (mission, parameters, camera, FTP), dialects and code generators.
nodes.kt: Lightweight binary protocol between autopilots, GCS and companion computers Microservices define stateful exchanges like mission upload Generators produce bindings for C, Python, Rust and more

nodes.s: Reference of all messages and commands in the common dialect, including GPS_RAW_INT, GPS_INPUT for injecting external position, ODOMETRY and VISION_POSITION_ESTIMATE for non-GNSS navigation sources.
nodes.kt: GPS_INPUT and VISION_POSITION_ESTIMATE are the hooks for feeding alternative PNT into an autopilot ODOMETRY carries full pose plus covariance Enumerations document EKF and GPS fix status flags

nodes.s: Describes MAVLink 2 packet signing: a shared-secret SHA-256 based signature and timestamp appended to frames to authenticate the link and resist replay.
nodes.kt: Signing authenticates but does not encrypt traffic Key distribution is left to the integrator Relevant for hardening drone C2 links against injection

nodes.s: The microservice used to upload, download and clear waypoint missions, geofences and rally points between a GCS and an autopilot, with its handshake and retry rules.
nodes.kt: Defines MISSION_COUNT / MISSION_ITEM_INT handshake Same protocol carries geofence and rally point plans

nodes.s: Briefing introducing the Cursor on Target XML event schema: the minimal event/point/detail model for exchanging what-when-where of tracked entities between C2 systems.
nodes.kt: Base schema is tiny: event, point, detail Type strings follow a hierarchical a-f-G-... code derived from symbology Extensibility lives in the detail element

nodes.n: TAK Protocol (takproto) - protobuf encoding of CoT
nodes.s: Documentation of the TAK protocol used by ATAK and TAK Server: how CoT events are framed and carried as protocol buffers over mesh (UDP multicast) and streaming (TCP/TLS) transports, alongside legacy XML.
nodes.kt: Explains version negotiation between XML and protobuf CoT Mesh vs streaming framing headers Essential to get a custom app talking to ATAK

nodes.n: STANAG 4586 - Standard Interfaces of UAV Control System (UCS) for NATO UAV Interoperability
nodes.s: Public overview of NATO's UAS interoperability standard, which defines a core UCS, a vehicle-specific module and five levels of interoperability from receiving payload data up to full flight control including launch and recovery.
nodes.kt: LOI 1-3 cover payload data and control; LOI 4-5 cover flight control Vehicle Specific Module isolates proprietary air vehicle interfaces Full text distributed via NATO / national channels

nodes.s: NATO's public explanation of how STANAGs and Allied publications are produced and ratified, and how interoperability standards flow into national forces. Starting point for locating public STANAG/AP summaries.
nodes.kt: STANAGs record national agreement to implement an Allied publication Most full texts are restricted; summaries and some APs are public

nodes.s: Overview of APP-6, the NATO standard for map symbols of units, equipment and tactical graphics, now at edition E and aligned with the US MIL-STD-2525 family. Explains frames, affiliation colours and the symbol identification code.
nodes.kt: Affiliation (friend/hostile/neutral/unknown) is encoded by frame shape and colour APP-6 and MIL-STD-2525 share a common symbol code structure Open renderers implement it for COP displays

nodes.s: Summary of the US military symbology standard and its revisions (2525B through E), including the SIDC code formats that symbol renderers and CoT type strings map onto.
nodes.kt: 2525D/E moved to a numeric 20/30-digit SIDC Basis for symbology in TAK and many C2 tools

nodes.n: Executive Order 13905: Strengthening National Resilience Through Responsible Use of PNT Services
nodes.s: US executive order that defines 'responsible use of PNT' and tasks Commerce/NIST, DHS and others to produce PNT profiles, identify critical infrastructure dependencies and pilot-test resilience. It is the root of NIST IR 8323 and the DHS conformance framework.
nodes.kt: Treats PNT disruption as a critical infrastructure risk Directs creation of voluntary PNT profiles Calls for testing PNT resilience in federal contracts

nodes.n: NIST IR 8323r1: Foundational PNT Profile - Applying the Cybersecurity Framework for the Responsible Use of PNT Services
nodes.s: Maps the NIST Cybersecurity Framework functions (identify, protect, detect, respond, recover) onto systems that produce or consume PNT data. A checklist-style profile for building resilient PNT into an architecture.
nodes.kt: Revision 1 supersedes the 2021 original Organized around CSF functions, applicable to both GNSS and non-GNSS sources NIST has signalled alignment with CSF 2.0

nodes.s: Companion to the conformance framework describing architectural patterns (source diversity, integrity checking, holdover) that map to its resilience levels.
nodes.kt: Architectural guidance for multi-source PNT Mapped to conformance framework levels

nodes.n: DHS S&T Positioning, Navigation, and Timing Program
nodes.s: Program hub for DHS PNT work: conformance framework, reference architecture, timing guidance and test events for critical infrastructure.
nodes.kt: Links all DHS resilient PNT publications Shows the civil critical-infrastructure angle of PNT resilience

nodes.n: DoD Directive 4650.05: Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT)
nodes.s: DoD policy directive governing the department's PNT enterprise, including the PNT Oversight Council and responsibilities for assured PNT and navigation warfare. Change 3 (2023) updated the oversight structure.
nodes.kt: Establishes the DoD PNT Oversight Council Assigns responsibilities for PNT and navigation warfare

nodes.n: GAO-21-320SP: Defense Navigation Capabilities - DOD Is Developing Positioning, Navigation, and Timing Technologies to Complement GPS
nodes.s: Technology assessment of DoD's alternative PNT efforts (inertial, vision, celestial, magnetic, signals of opportunity, clocks), with maturity status and challenges. A concise government map of the alt-PNT landscape.
nodes.kt: DOD keeps GPS at the core and adds complements Reviews maturity of many alt-PNT technology families Flags integration and testing as recurring challenges

nodes.n: National Positioning, Navigation, and Timing Resilience R&D Plan
nodes.s: Federal R&D plan responding to EO 13905, laying out research priorities for resilient PNT: threat detection, alternative sources, timing distribution and integrity.
nodes.kt: Identifies federal R&D priorities for PNT resilience Ties research areas back to EO 13905

nodes.s: US DOT plan to drive adoption of complementary PNT for transportation and critical infrastructure via stakeholder engagement, specifications, field trials and test ranges.
nodes.kt: Five lines of effort starting with engagement and standards Leads to field testing of commercial CPNT technologies

nodes.n: Analyzing a More Resilient National Positioning, Navigation, and Timing Capability (RR-2970)
nodes.s: DHS-sponsored RAND study of civil US PNT dependence that argues GPS is not the only PNT source in practice and that no single system is a perfect backup. It is a deliberately contrarian counterweight to the 'GPS loss is catastrophic' framing.
nodes.kt: Realistic adaptation lowers estimated economic cost of GPS loss High bar for a large government-funded GPS backup Recommends modest investment in threat detection

nodes.n: Assessing Alternative Positioning, Navigation and Timing Technologies for Potential Deployment in the EU
nodes.s: JRC test campaign at Ispra of commercial alternative PNT systems (terrestrial beacons, LEO, eLoran-like, fibre timing and others) for DG DEFIS. One of the few side-by-side public evaluations of A-PNT products.
nodes.kt: Mature commercial A-PNT already exists for positioning or timing Recommends a system-of-systems approach Warns the diverse tests do not allow a fair head-to-head ranking

nodes.n: JRC Complementary Position, Navigation and Timing
nodes.s: JRC activity page hosting the A-PNT assessment report with per-vendor appendices and related EU complementary PNT work.
nodes.kt: Official host for the report and vendor appendices

nodes.s: UN forum where GNSS providers coordinate compatibility, interoperability and spectrum protection, including interference detection and mitigation work.
nodes.kt: Venue for multi-GNSS interoperability agreements Hosts work on interference detection and mitigation

nodes.n: EASA Safety Information Bulletin 2022-02R4: GNSS Outage and Alterations Leading to Communication / Navigation / Surveillance Degradation
nodes.s: EASA's running bulletin on GNSS jamming and spoofing affecting aviation since February 2022, with recommendations for authorities, ANSPs, operators and manufacturers. Revision 4 is the current issue.
nodes.kt: Spoofing is treated as the harder-to-detect, higher-risk threat Recommendations are informational, not mandatory Affected FIRs are tracked on the EASA website

nodes.n: FAA GPS/GNSS Interference Reports and Anomaly Reporting
nodes.s: FAA page for reporting and reviewing GPS anomalies and interference events, with links to notices about planned GPS interference testing and operator guidance.
nodes.kt: Where US pilots file post-flight interference reports Links to GPS test NOTAM information

nodes.n: FAA SAFO 24002: Recognizing and Mitigating GPS/GNSS Disruptions
nodes.s: Safety alert for operators describing how jamming and spoofing manifest in the cockpit and what crews should do: revert to conventional procedures, report to ATC, and file written reports.
nodes.kt: Describes cockpit symptoms of jamming vs spoofing Advises readiness to use conventional navaids Later FAA guidance revisions followed in 2026

nodes.n: ICAO workshop presentation: GNSS Radio Frequency Interference
nodes.s: ICAO panel presentation on GNSS RFI impacts on flight operations and the regulatory response, from the Flight Safety Measures Panel working group.
nodes.kt: Summarizes operational impacts on avionics Frames the ICAO-level mitigation agenda

nodes.s: Program to field low-SWaP optical atomic clocks with timing holdover beyond GPS satellite clocks, in a portable airborne variant and a transportable land/sea variant, to keep precise time without GNSS.
nodes.kt: Two technical areas: portable and transportable clocks Two two-year phases from physics package to operational clock

nodes.n: DARPA's ROCkN Program Targets GNSS-Free Precision Timing in Contested Environments
nodes.s: Progress report on ROCkN field tests, including optical clock hardware flown on aircraft and deployed aboard a ship.
nodes.kt: Reports field synchronization and platform trials Shows optical clocks leaving the lab

nodes.s: Challenge site for airborne magnetic anomaly navigation: compensate the aircraft's own magnetic field out of magnetometer data so the remaining crustal anomaly can be map-matched for GPS-free navigation. Challenge is closed but data and code remain.
nodes.kt: Scored against a professionally compensated tail-stinger magnetometer Real flight data from survey aircraft Directly reusable as a hackathon benchmark Sensors: scalar and vector magnetometers, INS, GPS truth Domain: airborne Code: MagNav.jl

nodes.s: Zenodo record holding the MagNav challenge flight data: magnetometer, INS, GPS truth and map data from survey flights.
nodes.kt: HDF5 flight lines with truth position Paired with MagNav.jl loaders

nodes.n: Developing a Series of AI Challenges for the United States Department of the Air Force
nodes.s: Describes the Air Force AI challenge series including MagNav, covering both the compensation stage and a navigation stage that turns cleaned readings into position estimates.
nodes.kt: MagNav split into compensation and navigation sub-challenges Context on how DAF releases open benchmarks

nodes.n: NovAtel GAJT-410ML Anti-Jam Antenna Product Sheet
nodes.s: Datasheet for a compact CRPA anti-jam antenna that combines an antenna array and null-forming electronics for land vehicles and small platforms, protecting GPS and Galileo bands and supporting M-code.
nodes.kt: Null-steering CRPA as a drop-in in front of an existing receiver Shows typical number of nulls and suppression claims for this class

nodes.s: Product page for the larger 7-element GAJT CRPA unit in a hardened enclosure for land vehicles and fixed sites.
nodes.kt: More elements give more simultaneous nulls Typical military vehicle CRPA form factor

nodes.n: Septentrio AIM+ GNSS jamming and spoofing protection
nodes.s: Vendor explanation of AIM+ interference monitoring and mitigation: narrowband and wideband (chirp) jamming suppression in the receiver's signal processing plus layered spoofing detection including Galileo OSNMA.
nodes.kt: Single-antenna, in-receiver mitigation rather than CRPA Tiered feature levels OSNMA is one of the anti-spoofing layers

nodes.n: Most resilient GNSS receiver: results from Jammertest in Norway
nodes.s: Vendor write-up of its receivers' behaviour during the Jammertest live jamming and spoofing campaign in Norway. Read as a vendor claim, but useful for the scenario descriptions.
nodes.kt: Describes live jamming and spoofing scenarios Vendor-authored results, not independent

nodes.n: The looming threat of GPS jamming and spoofing (u-blox insights)
nodes.s: u-blox explainer on how jamming and spoofing affect mass-market receivers and which receiver-side defences (multi-band, multi-constellation, signal monitoring) help.
nodes.kt: Spoofing many signals consistently is harder with multi-GNSS Mass-market receivers expose jamming/spoofing indicators that apps can read

nodes.n: White Paper: Protecting GNSS Against Intentional Interference
nodes.s: Open white paper summarizing the threat of jamming and spoofing to civil GNSS and the countermeasure landscape (signal authentication, antenna arrays, consistency checks, regulation).
nodes.kt: Taxonomy of intentional interference Argues for layered defence and authentication

nodes.s: ESA's free wiki covering GNSS fundamentals, systems, signals, receivers, augmentation and applications. The fastest authoritative lookup for any GNSS term.
nodes.kt: Peer-reviewed style articles maintained by ESA Covers GPS, Galileo, GLONASS, BeiDou, SBAS Best free reference for GNSS concepts Good RAIM and error-model explanations Reliable quick reference for GNSS equations Covers Galileo signal and service details

nodes.n: Navipedia: Galileo Open Service Navigation Message Authentication
nodes.s: Navipedia article explaining OSNMA's design and status in plain terms before you tackle the ICD.
nodes.kt: Gentle introduction to TESLA-based navigation message authentication

nodes.n: GNSS Data Processing, Vol. I: Fundamentals and Algorithms (ESA TM-23)
nodes.s: Free ESA textbook covering GNSS measurement modelling, SPP, differential positioning and PPP algorithms with full equations. Pairs with the gLAB tool.
nodes.kt: Complete measurement model incl. clocks, troposphere, ionosphere SPP through PPP derivations Designed to accompany gLAB exercises

nodes.n: GNSS Data Processing, Vol. II: Laboratory Exercises (ESA TM-23)
nodes.s: Hands-on lab volume with step-by-step exercises on real data using the gLAB software, from SPP to carrier-phase PPP.
nodes.kt: Ready-made labs usable as a GNSS bootcamp Real RINEX data throughout

nodes.n: A Software-Defined GPS and Galileo Receiver: A Single-Frequency Approach
nodes.s: Classic textbook that walks through a complete MATLAB GPS software receiver: acquisition, code/carrier tracking, navigation decoding and positioning. The linked University of Colorado page is the official support site for the book's code.
nodes.kt: The canonical entry point to SDR GNSS receivers MATLAB code makes every loop inspectable Foundation for many later open SDR receivers Teaches acquisition and tracking loops by code Still the standard SDR GNSS teaching text

nodes.n: Stanford Center for Position, Navigation and Time (SCPNT) / GPS Lab
nodes.s: Home of the Stanford GPS Lab and the annual PNT symposium; hosts papers and presentations on integrity, interference monitoring, spoofing and alternative PNT.
nodes.kt: Annual symposium talks are a good snapshot of the field Lab papers on aviation integrity and RFI localization

nodes.s: Research group site with publications and theses on GNSS integrity, interference detection and localization, and navigation for aviation.
nodes.kt: Thesis archive is a deep free resource Publications on GNSS RFI detection and localization

nodes.s: Grace Gao's lab working on robust navigation for autonomous systems: GNSS in urban environments, sensor fusion, integrity and lunar PNT. Course and paper material is linked from here.
nodes.kt: Research on GNSS+vision/lidar fusion and integrity Home of AA272-related teaching on smartphone GNSS

nodes.s: Analyses a real spoofing event in the Mediterranean recorded on low-cost u-blox F9P receivers and evaluates detection approaches on that live data rather than a simulator.
nodes.kt: Real spoofing captured on commodity hardware Shows which detection cues actually fire in the wild

nodes.n: Recent Advances on Jamming and Spoofing Detection in GNSS
nodes.s: Open-access Sensors review of GNSS jamming and spoofing detection methods, finding machine learning is now the dominant approach, and covering combined jamming-plus-spoofing scenarios.
nodes.kt: ML-based detection dominates recent work Separates jamming-only, spoofing-only and combined attacks

nodes.n: Detecting and Mitigating Attacks on GPS Devices
nodes.s: Open-access review of GPS attack detection and mitigation focused on the GPS-denied case, including the alternative sensors and methods used to keep navigating.
nodes.kt: Covers both detection and what to fall back on Does not cover timing-only alternatives

nodes.n: Overview of satellite navigation spoofing and anti-spoofing techniques
nodes.s: Open-access Frontiers in Physics overview grouping anti-spoofing countermeasures into detection, identification, suppression and localization of the spoofer.
nodes.kt: Four-stage countermeasure taxonomy Contrasts spoofing with suppression jamming

nodes.n: Survey on positioning technology based on signal of opportunity from low earth orbit
nodes.s: Open-access survey of LEO signals-of-opportunity positioning: Doppler methods, error sources, and extracting observables from signals never designed for navigation (unknown codes, poor onboard clocks).
nodes.kt: Doppler positioning is the workhorse for LEO SoOP Unknown modulation and clock quality are the core difficulties

nodes.n: Enter LEO on the GNSS Stage: Navigation with Starlink Satellites
nodes.s: Opportunistic navigation using Starlink downlink signals without cooperation from the operator, describing two ways to extract navigation observables from unknown signals.
nodes.kt: Starlink is usable for navigation without operator support Signal structure must be partly estimated blind

nodes.n: Navigation with Multi-Constellation LEO Satellite Signals of Opportunity: Starlink, OneWeb, Orbcomm, and Iridium
nodes.s: Experimental multi-constellation LEO SoOP navigation combining four commercial constellations, using the simultaneous tracking and navigation (STAN) framework.
nodes.kt: Combining constellations improves geometry and accuracy STAN estimates satellite states and receiver state together

nodes.n: Preliminary Lessons in Conventional Warfighting from Russia's Invasion of Ukraine: February-July 2022
nodes.s: RUSI analysis of the first months of the war, including the scale of Russian electronic warfare and its effect on Ukrainian UAV survival and GNSS-dependent systems.
nodes.kt: EW is a dominant factor in small-UAV attrition Lessons for resilience of navigation and C2 links

nodes.s: Previous edition of the CSIS counterspace assessment; useful to see how GNSS interference reporting escalated between years.
nodes.kt: Baseline for year-over-year comparison

nodes.n: Jammertest - open GNSS jamming and spoofing test event (Andoya, Norway)
nodes.s: Annual open field event where Norwegian agencies transmit real jamming, spoofing and meaconing so vendors and researchers can test PNT equipment. The public test catalogue and community datasets make it the best source of real interference recordings.
nodes.kt: Real over-the-air jamming and spoofing in a controlled area Published test catalogue and plan Participants release datasets on GitHub Real jamming/spoofing scenarios documented in the public test plan Use the catalog to design realistic sim scenarios

nodes.n: Stone Soup: No Longer Just an Appetiser
nodes.s: FUSION 2023 paper announcing Stone Soup version 1.0, describing the framework's stable architecture and its use across the tracking community.
nodes.kt: Marks the stable 1.0 API Background on why defence labs backed an open tracking testbed

nodes.n: MIT 2.680 Unmanned Marine Vehicle Autonomy, Sensing and Communications
nodes.s: MIT course site with lectures and hands-on labs built on MOOS-IvP, covering behaviour-based autonomy, multi-vehicle coordination, collision avoidance and marine sensing.
nodes.kt: Lab sequence is a ready MOOS-IvP onboarding path Includes COLREGs-style collision avoidance behaviours

nodes.s: Documentation hub for MOOS-IvP with install guides, the IvP Helm manual, behaviour and app references and example missions.
nodes.kt: Helm manual explains multi-objective behaviour arbitration Mission files are simple text, quick to adapt

nodes.n: COLREGs - Convention on the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea, 1972
nodes.s: IMO page for the collision regulations that define give-way and stand-on duties, lights and signals; the rule set autonomous surface vessels must encode.
nodes.kt: Rules 13-17 (overtaking, head-on, crossing) drive most USV avoidance logic Rules are written for human judgement, which makes formalization hard

nodes.n: ITU-R M.1371 - Technical characteristics for an automatic identification system using TDMA in the VHF maritime mobile band
nodes.s: The ITU recommendation defining AIS radio, TDMA access and message formats that decoders such as pyais implement.
nodes.kt: Defines message types 1-27 decoded by pyais and AIS-catcher AIS is unauthenticated, so spoofing detection is an open problem

nodes.s: Published Signal K specification describing the JSON data model, REST and streaming APIs for marine data.
nodes.kt: Defines navigation.* paths for position, attitude and speed WebSocket delta stream is easy to consume from any language

nodes.s: User and developer documentation for ArduSub, covering ROV configuration, sensors, and integration of external positioning such as DVL and USBL via MAVLink.
nodes.kt: Explains how external position sources feed the EKF on a sub Good companion to BlueOS extensions

nodes.n: Water Linked documentation (DVL and Underwater GPS)
nodes.s: Vendor documentation for Water Linked DVLs and Underwater GPS (USBL-style) systems, including the JSON-over-TCP and serial protocols.
nodes.kt: DVL reports velocity and dead-reckoning over JSON/TCP Check firmware version against protocol version

nodes.s: Official Autoware documentation with architecture, installation, tutorials and design notes for localization, perception and planning components.
nodes.kt: Localization design docs explain NDT plus EKF fusion Planning simulator tutorial runs without hardware

nodes.n: RELLIS-3D Dataset: Data, Benchmarks and Analysis
nodes.s: Paper introducing the RELLIS-3D multimodal off-road dataset with annotated lidar and images and baseline results.
nodes.kt: Off-road semantics differ sharply from urban datasets Includes GNSS/IMU for localization work

nodes.n: Wild Visual Navigation: Fast Traversability Learning via Pre-Trained Models and Online Self-Supervision
nodes.s: Describes learning visual traversability online from pre-trained features and robot experience, adapting within minutes in forests and grassland.
nodes.kt: Self-supervision removes manual traversability labels Pre-trained vision features make online learning feasible

nodes.s: Bitcraze documentation for its UWB positioning system covering anchor placement, two-way ranging versus TDoA modes and configuration with Crazyflies.
nodes.kt: TDoA scales to many tags, TWR is simpler Anchor geometry dominates accuracy

nodes.s: Project page for a UWB TDoA dataset collected with Loco Positioning hardware, with ground truth for evaluating indoor UWB localization.
nodes.kt: Real UWB data including non-line-of-sight effects Useful to benchmark estimators before buying hardware

nodes.s: Docs for Crazyswarm2 with installation, simulation backends, swarm configuration and tutorials.
nodes.kt: Simulation mode lets you prototype swarm logic on a laptop

nodes.n: Onboard Ranging-based Relative Localization and Stability for Lightweight Aerial Swarms
nodes.s: Presents onboard UWB ranging with an EKF for relative localization among small quadrotors, with a stability analysis of formation control built on those estimates.
nodes.kt: Relative localization needs no anchors Observability depends on relative motion between agents

nodes.n: Swarm-SLAM: Sparse Decentralized Collaborative Simultaneous Localization and Mapping Framework for Multi-Robot Systems
nodes.s: Decentralized collaborative SLAM aimed at swarms, prioritizing which inter-robot loop closures to compute and share to limit communication.
nodes.kt: Budgeted loop-closure exchange keeps bandwidth low Works across lidar, stereo and RGB-D Communication budget is a first-class design constraint Supports LiDAR, stereo and RGB-D

nodes.n: DCL-SLAM: A Distributed Collaborative LiDAR SLAM Framework for a Robotic Swarm
nodes.s: Describes a fully distributed lidar C-SLAM using compact descriptors for inter-robot place recognition.
nodes.kt: Compact LiDAR-Iris descriptors reduce data exchange

nodes.n: Anti-UAV: A Large Multi-Modal Benchmark for UAV Tracking
nodes.s: Introduces the Anti-UAV RGB and thermal infrared video benchmark for UAV tracking and an evaluation protocol.
nodes.kt: Thermal IR matters for night and small-target tracking Targets frequently disappear, so trackers must handle absence

nodes.s: Site for the recurring Anti-UAV workshop and challenge with tracks for single and multiple UAV tracking in infrared video.
nodes.kt: Leaderboards give a reference point for hackathon results

nodes.n: Enabling Novel Mission Operations and Interactions with ROSA: The Robot Operating System Agent
nodes.s: Describes ROSA, an LLM agent that lets operators inspect and command ROS systems in natural language through a curated tool set, and discusses safety and operational considerations.
nodes.kt: Tool-based LLM access keeps robot actions auditable Targets operators, not only developers

nodes.n: OpenFly: A Comprehensive Platform for Aerial Vision-Language Navigation
nodes.s: Presents a multi-engine aerial VLN platform with automated data generation, a large outdoor benchmark and a keyframe-aware VLN model.
nodes.kt: Automated toolchain scales aerial VLN data Multiple rendering engines reduce sim bias

nodes.s: ICCV 2023 paper introducing a city-scale UAV vision-and-language navigation task, simulator and baselines.
nodes.kt: Aerial VLN is much harder than indoor VLN Long trajectories and 3D actions

nodes.n: CityNav: A Large-Scale Dataset for Real-World Aerial Navigation
nodes.s: Introduces a language-goal aerial navigation dataset built on real-city 3D data with geographic metadata, and baselines using map-based grounding.
nodes.kt: Geographic map priors improve aerial language navigation Human demonstrations from a web simulator

nodes.n: ViNT: A Foundation Model for Visual Navigation
nodes.s: Trains a transformer navigation policy across many robot datasets and shows it adapts to new robots and tasks with little data.
nodes.kt: Cross-embodiment pretraining works for navigation Image-goal policy plus topological graph

nodes.n: NoMaD: Goal Masked Diffusion Policies for Navigation and Exploration
nodes.s: Single diffusion policy that handles both goal-directed navigation and undirected exploration by masking the goal.
nodes.kt: One model for explore and goal-reach Runs on small robots

nodes.n: Visual Language Maps for Robot Navigation
nodes.s: Fuses visual-language features into 3D maps so robots can localize landmarks named in open-vocabulary language and navigate to them.
nodes.kt: Language-indexed spatial maps Enables spatial instructions like 'between X and Y'

nodes.n: LM-Nav: Robotic Navigation with Large Pre-Trained Models of Language, Vision, and Action
nodes.s: Combines an LLM for landmark extraction, CLIP for grounding and a visual navigation model to follow long route instructions outdoors.
nodes.kt: No language-annotated robot data needed Modular pretrained composition

nodes.n: TypeFly: Flying Drones with Large Language Model
nodes.s: Proposes a compact drone programming language for LLM output, cutting token count and latency while keeping plans checkable.
nodes.kt: Constrain LLM output to a small DSL Latency matters for flight

nodes.n: ChatGPT for Robotics: Design Principles and Model Abilities
nodes.s: Early study of prompting strategies and API design for using ChatGPT to generate robot and drone control code, with AirSim demos.
nodes.kt: Expose a high-level function library to the LLM Keep a human in the loop to review code

nodes.n: ConceptGraphs: Open-Vocabulary 3D Scene Graphs for Perception and Planning
nodes.s: Builds object-centric 3D scene graphs with open-vocabulary labels from RGB-D and uses an LLM to plan over them.
nodes.kt: Compact object-level maps for LLM planning Uses 2D foundation models

nodes.n: NaVid: Video-based VLM Plans the Next Step for Vision-and-Language Navigation
nodes.s: Video-based VLM that plans navigation actions from monocular RGB history without maps, odometry or depth.
nodes.kt: Map-free language navigation Sim-to-real transfer

nodes.s: The specification for MCP, the protocol LLM clients use to call tools and read resources from servers; the basis of the ROS, MAVLink and QGIS MCP servers.
nodes.kt: Tools, resources and prompts as server primitives Transport and authorization rules

nodes.n: OpenShoe: open source embedded foot-mounted INS
nodes.s: Project site (offline since 2026; archived copy) for OpenShoe, an open hardware and software ZUPT-aided foot-mounted INS module, described in the PLANS 2012 paper 'Foot-mounted INS for Everybody' and follow-up IPIN 2014 work.
nodes.kt: Open hardware + firmware for ZUPT-aided INS Module reports per-step displacement and heading change

nodes.s: Learned event-only monocular VO trained on simulated events that generalizes to real event datasets.
nodes.kt: Event-only VO without frames Simulation-trained, real-world tested

nodes.n: cuVSLAM: CUDA accelerated visual odometry and mapping
nodes.s: Describes NVIDIA's GPU-accelerated VO/SLAM supporting from one to many cameras with optional IMU, designed for real-time edge deployment.
nodes.kt: Multi-camera rigs supported Runs in real time on Jetson

nodes.s: DLR project page for R-Mode Baltic, which built a Baltic Sea testbed adding ranging signals to existing maritime radio beacons and AIS base stations as a terrestrial backup to GNSS, continued by R-Mode Baltic 2 and ORMOBASS.
nodes.kt: Reuses existing MF beacons and VHF AIS for ranging Moving toward IALA standardisation

nodes.n: The Global Loran / eLoran Infrastructure Evolution: A Robust and Resilient PNT Backup for GNSS
nodes.s: Briefing by the FAA's chief navigation systems engineer to the US Space-Based PNT Advisory Board (3 June 2014) on the history of Loran/eLoran and the findings of the 2006-2008 Independent Assessment Team, which judged eLoran a viable independent backup to GPS.
nodes.kt: eLoran has different physical failure modes than GNSS IAT found eLoran meets non-precision approach (RNP 0.3), harbor entrance (10-20 m) and Stratum 1 timing needs

nodes.s: Tutorial hub for running generative AI, VLMs and robotics models on Jetson devices, built around jetson-containers.
nodes.kt: Step-by-step onboard LLM/VLM deployment Covers ROS and robotics integrations

nodes.n: EUSPA GNSS Market and User Technology Reports
nodes.s: Download page for EUSPA's market reports and GNSS User Technology Reports, which survey receiver, antenna and resilience technology trends.
nodes.kt: User Technology Report covers anti-jamming, authentication and multi-constellation trends Useful for framing a pitch

nodes.s: Flightradar24's map of GNSS interference, computed from navigation integrity category values broadcast by aircraft over its receiver network.
nodes.kt: Grey areas mean insufficient flights or receivers, not absence of jamming Covers all GNSS, not just GPS

nodes.n: Assessing the Spoofing Threat: Development of a Portable GPS Civilian Spoofer
nodes.s: Landmark ION GNSS 2008 paper that built a receiver-based civil GPS spoofer and analysed how hard it is to detect, kicking off modern civil spoofing defense research.
nodes.kt: Receiver-based spoofers can align with authentic signals and drag the victim smoothly Simple checks are insufficient against a sophisticated spoofer Motivates cryptographic and signal-level defenses

nodes.s: Proceedings of the IEEE survey of spoofing attack types and detection/mitigation techniques, from navigation-data checks to signal distortion monitoring and multi-antenna methods.
nodes.kt: Taxonomy of defenses: cryptographic, signal-processing, geometric Multi-antenna angle-of-arrival checks are powerful Combining several weak tests beats any single test

nodes.s: Public set of recorded high-rate IQ files of GPS L1 spoofing scenarios (static and dynamic, time and position push) used as a standard benchmark for spoofing detection.
nodes.kt: De facto benchmark for signal-level spoofing detectors Recordings are large IQ files suitable for GNSS-SDR

nodes.n: Signal Structure of the Starlink Ku-Band Downlink
nodes.s: Reverse-engineers the Starlink Ku-band downlink as OFDM and identifies synchronization sequences usable for opportunistic ranging and positioning.
nodes.kt: Starlink frames contain known sequences usable as pilots Enables LEO signals-of-opportunity PNT without operator cooperation

nodes.n: The First Carrier Phase Tracking and Positioning Results With Starlink LEO Satellite Signals
nodes.s: IEEE TAES letter showing carrier-phase tracking of Starlink signals with unknown structure and positioning from several satellites.
nodes.kt: Positioning from Starlink is feasible without knowing the signal format Accuracy reported at metre level with known altitude

nodes.s: Kaggle competition with raw GNSS and IMU logs from Android phones in cars, scored on positioning accuracy against high-grade truth.
nodes.kt: Large public smartphone GNSS dataset with truth Winning solutions used factor graphs and carrier phase Sensors: phone raw GNSS, IMU Size class: medium Kaggle account required

nodes.s: Earlier edition of the smartphone GNSS positioning competition with Android raw measurement logs and ground truth.
nodes.kt: Good secondary dataset for testing detectors on diverse phones Sensors: phone raw GNSS, IMU Kaggle account required

nodes.n: Android Raw GNSS Measurement Datasets for Precise Positioning
nodes.s: ION GNSS+ 2020 paper releasing the first public Android raw GNSS datasets with corrections and ground truth, the origin of the GSDC series.
nodes.kt: Describes data collection and ground truth Basis for all later GSDC editions

nodes.n: Android raw GNSS measurements developer guide
nodes.s: Android documentation on the GnssMeasurement API: which phones expose pseudorange, carrier phase and AGC, and how to log them.
nodes.kt: AGC and C/N0 fields support jamming detection on phones Duty cycling must be disabled for continuous carrier phase

nodes.n: NTRIP: Networked Transport of RTCM via Internet Protocol (BKG)
nodes.s: BKG's overview of the NTRIP protocol for streaming GNSS corrections, with links to its caster, client and server software.
nodes.kt: NTRIP is HTTP-based streaming of RTCM BKG maintains the reference caster

nodes.s: Page for BNC, BKG's multi-stream NTRIP client that records, decodes, converts to RINEX, monitors and can compute real-time PPP from correction streams.
nodes.kt: Swiss-army tool for real-time correction streams Can monitor stream latency and outages

nodes.s: Tutorials and reference for configuring the GNSS-SDR receiver, including signal processing blocks, front-end setup and monitoring outputs.
nodes.kt: Step-by-step first-fix tutorials with sample files Explains each receiver block for modification

nodes.s: Long-running practitioner blog on getting centimetre-level RTK/PPK from low-cost u-blox receivers with the demo5 RTKLIB fork, with configuration walk-throughs and data analysis.
nodes.kt: Configuration recipes that save hours Honest comparisons of receivers and settings Practical RTK tuning tips you will not find in papers Maintainer of the demo5 RTKLIB fork

nodes.s: Catalog of International GNSS Service precise orbits, clocks, biases and atmospheric products used by PPP and precise processing.
nodes.kt: Precise products are free Product latency ranges from real-time to final

nodes.n: Quaternion kinematics for the error-state Kalman filter
nodes.s: Long tutorial report covering quaternion conventions, rotation perturbations and their derivatives, and a full derivation of an IMU-driven error-state Kalman filter including the reset step.
nodes.kt: Pins down Hamilton vs JPL quaternion conventions Step-by-step ESKF prediction, correction and reset Global vs local error definitions Standard reference for implementing an INS/ESKF Covers local vs global perturbation conventions

nodes.n: A micro Lie theory for state estimation in robotics
nodes.s: Tutorial paper giving just enough Lie theory (groups, exponential map, adjoint, Jacobians, uncertainty on manifolds) to write correct estimators for 3D pose; it is the basis of Solà's 'Lie theory for the roboticist' course and the manif library.
nodes.kt: Unified plus/minus notation for manifold states Ready-to-use Jacobians for SO(3), SE(3) and others Ready-to-use Jacobians for SO(3)/SE(3) Fixes the most common EKF-on-rotations mistakes

nodes.n: Principles of GNSS, Inertial, and Multisensor Integrated Navigation Systems, Second Edition
nodes.s: Standard reference on satellite, inertial and terrestrial radio navigation and their integration, including INS/GNSS integration architectures, dead reckoning, feature matching and integrity monitoring.
nodes.kt: Loose, tight and deep INS/GNSS coupling explained Covers fault detection and integrity Companion MATLAB simulation software for buyers

nodes.s: Classic IET text on strapdown inertial navigation: sensor technologies, mechanisation, error propagation and compensation, and aided navigation.
nodes.kt: Physical principles and error growth of INS Sensor technology from mechanical gyros to MEMS

nodes.s: Textbook on probabilistic estimation for robotics, from linear-Gaussian filtering and batch estimation to matrix Lie groups for 3D pose; the second edition adds variational inference and inertial navigation material. Author hosts a PDF; print edition from Cambridge University Press.
nodes.kt: Batch vs recursive estimation from first principles Matrix Lie groups for pose and uncertainty New inertial navigation section in 2nd edition Rigorous treatment of SE(3) uncertainty Bridges filtering and batch optimization

nodes.s: Foundations and Trends monograph (free author PDF) explaining SLAM and sensor fusion as inference on factor graphs, with incremental smoothing (iSAM) and the reasoning behind the GTSAM library.
nodes.kt: Why sparsity makes smoothing tractable From batch to incremental (iSAM) inference Why smoothing beats filtering for multi-sensor nav Direct conceptual guide to GTSAM

nodes.n: iSAM2: Incremental Smoothing and Mapping Using the Bayes Tree
nodes.s: Introduces the Bayes tree and the iSAM2 algorithm for incremental nonlinear smoothing with fluid relinearization, the engine behind GTSAM's online estimators.
nodes.kt: Incremental updates without periodic batch steps Bayes tree data structure

nodes.n: On-Manifold Preintegration for Real-Time Visual-Inertial Odometry
nodes.s: Derives IMU preintegration on the SO(3) manifold with bias-correction Jacobians, enabling IMU factors between keyframes in factor-graph optimization.
nodes.kt: Summarise many IMU samples into one relative-motion factor First-order bias correction avoids re-integration

nodes.n: The invariant extended Kalman filter as a stable observer
nodes.s: Foundational paper showing that for group-affine systems the invariant EKF has error dynamics independent of the trajectory, giving stability guarantees standard EKFs lack.
nodes.kt: Error defined on the Lie group, not in vector space Better consistency under large initial errors

nodes.n: Contact-Aided Invariant Extended Kalman Filtering for Robot State Estimation
nodes.s: Applies the invariant EKF to legged robots, fusing IMU with leg contact kinematics, and evaluates it against a quaternion EKF.
nodes.kt: Contact points as extra states in the group Faster convergence than quaternion EKF

nodes.s: Car localisation from IMU alone by combining an invariant EKF with a neural network that adapts measurement noise covariances (pseudo-measurements), evaluated on KITTI.
nodes.kt: Learned covariances, classical filter structure IMU-only ground vehicle dead reckoning

nodes.s: Combines a network that predicts displacement and uncertainty from IMU data with an EKF, for pedestrian inertial odometry.
nodes.kt: Learned measurement plus learned uncertainty in a filter

nodes.n: RoNIN: Robust Neural Inertial Navigation in the Wild: Benchmark, Evaluations, and New Methods
nodes.s: Introduces a large smartphone IMU dataset with ground truth and benchmarks neural architectures for pedestrian velocity regression.
nodes.kt: Benchmark dataset for learned pedestrian navigation Body-frame heading-agnostic representation

nodes.n: AirIO: Learning Inertial Odometry with Enhanced IMU Feature Observability
nodes.s: UAV-focused learned inertial odometry that changes how IMU data are represented to the network to make motion features more observable.
nodes.kt: IMU-only odometry for drones Representation choice matters for UAV learned IO

nodes.s: Practical explanation of white noise and random-walk bias parameters for IMUs, how to convert datasheet values to continuous/discrete form and how to inflate them for real use.
nodes.kt: Continuous vs discrete noise density conversion Inflate Allan-derived noise for real-world use

nodes.n: Factor Graphs and GTSAM: A Hands-on Introduction
nodes.s: Hands-on introduction to the GTSAM library: modelling robot odometry, landmark and pose-graph SLAM as factor graphs, solving with Levenberg-Marquardt or iSAM2, and reading marginal covariances, with C++ and Python snippets.
nodes.kt: Best first hour with GTSAM Shortest path to a working pose-graph in Python Pattern reusable for GNSS/INS/visual factor fusion

nodes.n: An efficient orientation filter for inertial and inertial/magnetic sensor arrays
nodes.s: Internal report introducing the gradient-descent orientation filter now known as the Madgwick filter, for IMU and MARG sensors.
nodes.kt: Low computational cost attitude filter Single tuning parameter

nodes.n: Auterion Skynode S and Auterion Visual Navigation
nodes.s: Auterion sells PX4-derived AuterionOS plus Skynode flight/mission computers. Skynode S (2024) is a small integrated autopilot/mission computer marketed for operation when GNSS and links are jammed; Auterion Visual Navigation is the company's camera-based position source, named in its 2025 DIU Artemis completion announcement.
nodes.kt: Vendor claim: AuterionOS detects GNSS jamming/spoofing and stops trusting GNSS (Jan 2024 announcement) Vendor/press claim: used in Ukraine; no public accuracy figures found Open-source base is PX4; the visual navigation layer is proprietary

nodes.s: Hivemind is Shield AI's onboard autonomy software, flown on its V-BAT and on partner aircraft. In an interview the CTO describes a state-estimation framework fusing visual, EO/IR and inertial observations so the aircraft keeps operating without GNSS or comms.
nodes.kt: Vendor description: multi-sensor state estimation for GNSS-denied and comms-denied flight No published accuracy numbers found ViDAR (acquired with Sentient Vision, 2024) is an EO/IR detection product, not a navigation source

nodes.n: Helsing HX-2 - map/landmark-based GNSS-denied navigation (navigation aspect only)
nodes.s: Helsing's HX-2 is a loitering UAS supplied to Ukraine. Indexed here only for its navigation approach: press reporting says an onboard computer with stored map data lets it navigate by recognising landmarks when satellite navigation is denied. Helsing navigation job postings mention vision-aided, terrain-relative, celestial and signals-of-opportunity methods.
nodes.kt: Press/vendor claim: landmark recognition against stored maps; no public accuracy data Shows the European market expects map-based visual nav as a baseline feature

nodes.n: Q-CTRL Ironstone Opal quantum-assured magnetic navigation
nodes.s: Q-CTRL's navigation product pairs quantum magnetometers with its software to match measured crustal magnetic anomalies against maps (MagNav). The company reports flight, ground and maritime trials and positions it as a GNSS backup for aviation, including work with Airbus.
nodes.kt: Vendor claims (not independent): RNP 0.3 met in flight (error under 0.3 nm for 95% of a flight); the linked case study claims 50x lower positioning uncertainty than an INS over a ~500 km flight and at least 11x with the sensor inside the cabin; other Q-CTRL materials give different multipliers Vendor claim: RTCA DO-160 environmental qualification - not an airworthiness or RNP operational approval Underlying method is the same map-matching problem as the open AFRL/MIT MagNav challenge

nodes.s: AQNav is SandboxAQ's magnetic anomaly navigation system: magnetometers plus learned compensation, matched against magnetic anomaly maps. Flight-tested with Acubed (Airbus) on a Beechcraft Baron using public maps, and, per later SandboxAQ announcements, with the USAF on C-17/C-130J and in 2026 on a Northrop Grumman Lumberjack drone.
nodes.kt: Vendor claims (July 2025 Acubed campaign, 150+ flight hours on a Beechcraft Baron 58 with the public NAMAM map): within RNP 2 100% of the time and RNP 1 95%; outperformed INS without GNSS on every flight over 2 h Sept 2026 drone test announcement gave no error figures (noted by press) Accepted into the 2025 NATO DIANA cohort (vendor/press)

nodes.n: Xona Space Systems Pulsar LEO PNT constellation
nodes.s: Xona is building Pulsar, a commercial LEO constellation broadcasting dedicated L-band navigation signals with authentication. Pulsar-0 launched in June/July 2025 as an in-orbit demonstrator; production satellites and initial service were planned for 2026-2027 per later reporting, and the FCC granted conditional approval in August 2026 (initially 16 satellites, more after a debris review).
nodes.kt: LEO PNT signals are stronger at the ground than MEO GNSS, which is the anti-jam argument Service is not yet generally available; dates in press reports conflict Open work in this space uses existing LEO signals of opportunity (Starlink, Iridium Doppler) instead

nodes.s: TrustPoint is developing a commercial C-band LEO navigation constellation. Its third demonstration satellite (Time Flies) launched in June 2025 carrying a C-band payload for testing partner receivers.
nodes.kt: Vendor claim: commercial GPS alternative from LEO; no independent performance reports found C-band choice moves PNT away from crowded and jammed L-band

nodes.n: Iridium PNT (Satellite Time and Location) and Iridium PNT ASIC
nodes.s: Iridium broadcasts a high-power LEO timing and location signal (STL, from the Satelles acquisition) usable as a GNSS backup and cross-check. A dedicated PNT ASIC was unveiled in October 2025 and announced commercially available in July 2026; integrators include Solace and Skyband, and VectorNav/NAL Research announced STL-aided INS work in 2025.
nodes.kt: Positioning is coarse compared to GNSS; main value is timing and an independent plausibility check Vendor claim on ASIC size: 8 x 8 mm, under 0.2 g (Iridium fact sheet, Oct 2025) Open LEO Doppler code in the index can use Iridium signals of opportunity without a subscription

nodes.n: Honeywell Vision Aided Navigation (Alternative Navigation Suite)
nodes.s: Honeywell's VAN correlates live visible or IR imagery against onboard reference maps for an absolute fix, paired with its inertial units. It sits in an Alternative Navigation Suite with magnetic-anomaly and celestial modules.
nodes.kt: Vendor description: passive, sensor-agnostic image-to-map correlation Press claim: 'GPS-like' performance on Embraer E170 and AW139 tests; no numbers published Same problem as open UAV absolute visual localization benchmarks

nodes.n: Honeywell HGuide o480 single-card INS and HGuide i700 IMU
nodes.s: HGuide o480 (May 2025) is a single-card INS for small UAVs and ground robots that accepts velocity aiding (e.g. Honeywell radar velocity sensor) and embeds a Septentrio receiver with AIM+ anti-jam/anti-spoof. The HGuide i700 IMU is marketed as near navigation grade with a no-license-required export classification.
nodes.kt: Shows the commodity pattern: tactical IMU + velocity aid + hardened GNSS in one card Export classification is a selling point, which matters for team hardware choices

nodes.n: Advanced Navigation Boreas FOG INS with LVS laser velocity sensor
nodes.s: Advanced Navigation's Boreas fibre-optic-gyro INS line, fused with its LVS laser velocity sensor or wheel odometry, is marketed for long GNSS-denied ground and maritime runs; reported trials include a US Army testbed and an underground mine.
nodes.kt: Vendor/press claims: 11.7 m error over 65 km with GNSS jammed (wheel-encoder config, US Army testbed, linked article); better than 0.1% of distance travelled in BHP's Callio mine trial (Advanced Navigation case study) Strategy is inertial-centric dead reckoning with velocity aiding, not vision

nodes.n: Inertial Labs VINS visual-aided INS (with Maxar Raptor)
nodes.s: Launched June 2025, VINS combines an Inertial Labs INS with Maxar Raptor software that matches camera frames to Maxar Precision3D satellite-derived 3D maps for absolute position on long-range UAV flights.
nodes.kt: Vendor claims: about 35 m horizontal / 5 m vertical without GNSS Options for Iridium-based PNT and M-code receivers Commercial map product (Precision3D) is the moat; open teams use free orthophotos and DEMs

nodes.n: Safran VersaPNT and Geonyx resilient PNT units
nodes.s: Safran's defense PNT range includes VersaPNT (GNSS receiver + IMU + disciplined oscillator with jamming/spoofing detection and NTP/PTP time serving) and the Geonyx HRG-based INS; GPS World reports a NAVKITE kit combining Geonyx M with VersaSync for French Navy commandos.
nodes.kt: Combined position + timing holdover in one box is the standard defense product shape Detection flags and holdover timing are reproducible in open stacks at lower grade

nodes.n: SBG Systems Ellipse INS - 2025 GNSS-denied firmware
nodes.s: A March 2025 free firmware update for SBG's Ellipse (v3 hardware) adds jamming/spoofing detection flags and lets users reject or re-enable GNSS and other aiding sensors without resetting the filter.
nodes.kt: Vendor claim: improved accuracy in GNSS-denied and magnetically disturbed conditions Integrity flags plus manual sensor rejection is now an expected feature even in small INS

nodes.n: VectorNav - Iridium STL-aided INS collaboration with NAL Research
nodes.s: VectorNav makes small tactical-grade IMU/GNSS-INS units widely used on research drones (PX4 has a driver). In April 2025 it announced work with NAL Research on Iridium STL-aided INS for GNSS-denied operation.
nodes.kt: Collaboration announcement, not a shipped product feature VN-series units are a common drop-in for PX4 testbeds

nodes.n: Spirent GSS7000 and PNT X GNSS/PNT simulators
nodes.s: Spirent's lab simulators generate multi-GNSS RF with controllable interference and spoofing (meaconing, trajectory spoofing, nav data spoofing) for hardware-in-the-loop receiver testing; PNT X extends this to combined PNT/sensor simulation.
nodes.kt: Lab-grade, export-controlled tooling; judges from industry will know it Open alternatives are SDR-based signal simulators - legal only into a cable or shielded enclosure

nodes.n: Safran Skydel simulation engine / GSG-8 GNSS simulator (ex-Orolia)
nodes.s: Skydel is the SDR/GPU-based simulation engine behind Safran's GSG-8 simulators, with built-in jamming and spoofing scenarios, CRPA wavefront variants and LEO PNT signal options; Safran offers it to universities through an academic programme.
nodes.kt: Vendor datasheet: jamming and spoofing generated without extra hardware Spoofing workflows run a 'truth' and a 'spoofer' instance - a useful mental model for test design

nodes.n: infiniDome GPSdome / GPSdome 2 small-UAS anti-jam module
nodes.s: infiniDome sells retrofit anti-jam modules that sit between antenna elements and a commercial GNSS receiver on small drones and vehicles; GPSdome 2 is dual-band with up to four elements for nulling several jammer directions.
nodes.kt: Vendor claim: CRPA-like protection without CRPA cost or export restrictions Weight figures differ across press releases (500 g in the linked GPS World piece, 350 g elsewhere)

nodes.n: Twist Robotics OSCAR visual navigation module (Ukraine)
nodes.s: Ukrainian company Twist Robotics announced OSCAR in January 2026: a camera-based module that recognises landmarks, matches them to a map and feeds coordinates to the UAV autopilot when GNSS is jammed.
nodes.kt: Vendor claim: platforms with the module have flown more than 500,000 km Architecture (camera => map match => coordinates into autopilot) is the same one open repos implement

nodes.n: Blue Arrow - Ukrainian visual navigation for drones (Brave1 cluster)
nodes.s: Brave1 cluster member Blue Arrow was presented by Ukraine's minister Fedorov in 2025 as having an autonomous visual navigation system that lets drones fly without GNSS under jamming and spoofing.
nodes.kt: Claim relayed from a ministerial post; no technical detail or numbers published One of many Ukrainian vendors in this niche (others named by Brave1: Norda Dynamics, The Fourth Law, ZIR)

nodes.s: US startup whose founders started at the February 2024 El Segundo Defense Tech Hackathon (Aviation Week coverage). Its VNS uses a camera, an IMU and pre-loaded satellite imagery to estimate position and feeds the drone a substitute GPS signal.
nodes.kt: Vendor claims: six months from hackathon to a SOCOM sale (YC launch post); integration under 30 minutes (company statement relayed by press) Direct precedent that a hackathon visual-nav demo can become a product - and that judges have seen this pitch

nodes.n: Spleenlab VISIONAIRY perception and GNSS-free navigation software
nodes.s: German company Spleenlab sells VISIONAIRY, an AI perception suite for drones (vendor description: VIO, map-based relocalization, EO/IR and LiDAR SLAM) that joined the Auterion ecosystem in 2022 and integrates with PX4/Auterion and ROS. Quantum Systems later acquired Spleenlab and uses it for GNSS-denied navigation (press).
nodes.kt: Vendor description only; no published accuracy Module list mirrors what open VIO + VPR repos offer

nodes.s: UAVOS markets NavAI as an add-on vision-based navigation module for UAS in GNSS-degraded conditions (GPS World product announcement).
nodes.kt: Product announcement; performance figures not verified here

nodes.s: RoQS (solicitation DARPA-PS-25-11) aims to make quantum sensors robust to platform vibration and motion so they work on real vehicles; Phase 1 launched August 2025 with compact sensors to be tested on a government helicopter plus platform integration studies.
nodes.kt: Problem statement: quantum sensors lose their advantage on moving platforms Signals where defense money is going for GNSS-independent inertial/magnetic sensing

nodes.s: DIU programme fielding quantum sensors for PNT: lines of effort cover quantum inertial sensors, gravimeters for gravity-aided naval navigation, quantum magnetic sensing, magnetic navigation and component insertion, with more than 10 field tests planned in the first ~12 months (announced March 2025).
nodes.kt: 18 named performers including Honeywell, Lockheed Martin, Q-CTRL, AOSense, Anduril, Northrop Grumman, Vector Atomic Honeywell flew a quantum MagNav test on an Embraer 170 under TQS (press)

nodes.n: DAF-MIT AI Accelerator MagNav real-time C-17 demonstration (2023)
nodes.s: In May 2023 the Air Force and MIT flew a real-time MagNav demo on a C-17A during exercise Golden Phoenix, training the compensation network in flight on a laptop. Follows the open MagNav challenge problem and dataset.
nodes.kt: No accuracy figure is public: the linked article and the official releases defer it to a government technical report. The value shown is RF independence Public dataset and Julia/Python code make this the most reproducible alt-PNT track for a hackathon

nodes.n: UK quantum navigation flight trials (Infleqtion, BAE Systems, QinetiQ)
nodes.s: In May 2024 an optical atomic clock and a cold-atom sensor flew on QinetiQ's RJ100 testbed from Boscombe Down, toward a quantum inertial navigation system concept. Linked to the UK National Quantum Strategy mission of quantum navigation on aircraft by 2030.
nodes.kt: Government claim: first publicly acknowledged in-flight tests of this kind Government funding stated as nearly GBP 8 million

nodes.n: UK DASA Early Market Engagement: PNT problem statement for uncrewed systems
nodes.s: Published September 2024. Asks for assured PNT for small UAS: low-cost, low-SWaP CRPA (multi-frequency, SDR-based), SDR/GPU GNSS receivers, AI for spoofing detection and multi-source fusion, as plug-in replacements for COTS GNSS.
nodes.kt: Explicit platform example: under 1.5 m wingspan Unit cost must suit mass use - cost is a first-class requirement

nodes.n: UK national eLoran, Timing Centre and GNSS warning investment (2025)
nodes.s: November 2025 UK announcement of about GBP 155M for a national timing centre, a sovereign eLoran system and GNSS interference warning; a Find a Tender notice targets eLoran IOC by 2028 and FOC by 2030.
nodes.kt: Terrestrial backup and GNSS warning, not only alt-nav on the vehicle

nodes.n: ESA NAVISP (Navigation Innovation and Support Programme)
nodes.s: ESA's PNT R&D programme funding industry projects including GNSS-independent PNT; 2025 examples include ALL.SPACE (EUR 950k per the October 2025 ALL.SPACE announcement, signals of opportunity from a multi-orbit terminal, with GMV NSL) and maritime alt-PNT via VDES and R-Mode.
nodes.kt: Permanent open call route for European companies Shows European emphasis on SoOP and terrestrial backups

nodes.s: EDF 2025 work programme (EUR 1.065B) closed 16 October 2025 with 410 proposals; results expected April 2026. Indexed as the current EDF cycle; the explicit drone-navigation challenge topic in the index is from EDF 2024.
nodes.kt: No 2025 topic explicitly on GNSS-denied navigation confirmed in this pass EDF 2024 challenge (multi-sensor drone navigation) is the best-matched prior topic

nodes.n: UNITE - Brave NATO: Brave1 and NATO Innovation HQ joint competition (2026)
nodes.s: March 2026 programme pairing Ukrainian and NATO-country companies on joint solutions: first round EUR 10M, up to EUR 1M per project split between partners. Focus areas are counter-UAS and navigation where EW disrupts positioning; NATO-side funding limited to non-lethal categories.
nodes.kt: Ministerial framing: 'robust navigation in GPS-denied environments' as a critical field

nodes.n: EUDIS Defence Hackathon, 5th edition (Oct 2026) - GNSS-denied navigation challenge
nodes.s: EU-funded 48-hour hackathon held 15-17 October 2026 at eight sites under the theme 'Autonomy on the Battlefield'. Common challenges were GNSS-denied navigation and swarm coordination, plus one local challenge per host (e.g. counter-UAS in Cyprus).
nodes.kt: Most direct precedent for this hackathon's likely problem statement Eligibility: EU, Norway, Ukraine citizens aged 18+

nodes.n: European Defense Tech Hackathon series (Paris, London, Sheffield, Prague...)
nodes.s: Independent recurring European defense hackathon series. The December 2024 Paris edition had a second-place magnetic navigation entry for underwater drones; 2025 London and Sheffield editions listed GNSS-denied navigation tracks.
nodes.kt: Navigation tracks recur; winners skew toward working demos with real data

nodes.n: El Segundo Defense Tech Hackathon (Feb 2024) - origin of Theseus GPS-denied drone
nodes.s: Aviation Week story (March 2024) on three non-defense engineers who built a GPS-denied drone for under USD 500 at a 24-hour defense tech hackathon; the team became Theseus.
nodes.kt: Cheap visual nav prototypes are a known hackathon genre in the US

nodes.n: Online Training: Mobile Robotics (Basics + Robotics blocks)
nodes.s: A curated self-study path of short recorded lectures from Bonn's Photogrammetry & Robotics lab, going from linear algebra, rotations and least squares through Bayes filters, EKF localization, particle filters, ICP, RANSAC and graph-based SLAM. Each topic pairs a '5 Minutes with Cyrill' teaser with a full-length lecture.
nodes.kt: Fastest structured on-ramp to probabilistic state estimation Covers EKF/MCL localization and pose-graph SLAM end to end Links the older full SLAM course playlist

nodes.s: Full semester recording of the Freiburg Robot Mapping course: EKF-SLAM, sparse extended information filters, FastSLAM, grid-based mapping, least-squares and graph-based SLAM, and front-end/back-end design. Still one of the most-cited free SLAM courses.
nodes.kt: Classic derivations of EKF-SLAM and FastSLAM Graph-SLAM via least squares, robust kernels Slides and Octave exercises on the course page
