nodes.n: Robot Mapping - WS 2013/14 course page (slides, exercises)
nodes.s: Course page that accompanies the Robot Mapping lecture videos, with lecture slides and programming exercises (EKF-SLAM, UKF, FastSLAM, least-squares calibration, graph-SLAM) in Octave/Matlab.
nodes.kt: Hands-on exercises missing from the video playlist Good template for a 1-day SLAM crash course

nodes.s: Recorded two-semester photogrammetry course (2015/16 playlist): camera models, direct linear transform, projective geometry, epipolar geometry, bundle adjustment, and image-based 3D reconstruction. The geometric backbone for visual navigation and map-matching against imagery.
nodes.kt: Camera calibration and orientation from first principles Bundle adjustment as used in VIO and visual geolocalization Useful before attempting aerial image-to-map registration

nodes.n: Cyrill Stachniss YouTube channel (incl. '5 Minutes with Cyrill')
nodes.s: Channel hosting Stachniss's full lecture courses plus the '5 Minutes with Cyrill' series of short explainers on single concepts (Kalman filter, factor graphs, ICP, RANSAC, SIFT, occupancy grids).
nodes.kt: Short explainers ideal for onboarding teammates during a hackathon Also hosts newer courses on LiDAR and photogrammetric vision

nodes.s: Graduate course building a monocular visual odometry pipeline step by step: image formation, calibration, feature detection, two-view geometry, P3P+RANSAC, bundle adjustment, KLT tracking, place recognition, visual-inertial fusion and event cameras. Slides and Matlab/Python exercises with solutions are public; recordings go to the UZH platform.
nodes.kt: Exercises culminate in a working mini VO pipeline Covers place recognition and VIO fusion Python templates available alongside Matlab

nodes.n: Visual Odometry: Part I - The First 30 Years and Fundamentals / Part II - Matching, Robustness, Optimization, and Applications
nodes.s: Two-part IEEE Robotics & Automation Magazine tutorial (Part II at rpg.ifi.uzh.ch/docs/VO_Part_II_Scaramuzza.pdf). Explains the VO problem formulation, 2D-2D/3D-2D motion estimation, feature matching, outlier rejection and local optimization in a compact, readable form.
nodes.kt: Best single-read primer on VO design choices Part II covers RANSAC and windowed bundle adjustment

nodes.n: MIT 16.485 Visual Navigation for Autonomous Vehicles (VNAV)
nodes.s: MIT graduate course on the math and software of visual navigation: 3D geometry, Lie groups, quadrotor modelling and control, trajectory optimization, feature tracking, two-view geometry, nonlinear optimization, VIO and SLAM. Lecture slides/notes and ROS 2 based lab handouts are public, with lab code on GitHub.
nodes.kt: Labs walk from ROS basics to a quadrotor VIO stack Strong on certifiable/robust estimation Lecture notes downloadable per topic

nodes.s: Award-winning TUM lecture on making quadrotors navigate with cameras: 3D geometry, sensors, state estimation, visual motion estimation, SLAM, dense reconstruction, planning and exploration. Each lecture has slides and a recorded video.
nodes.kt: Compact quadrotor-centric syllabus Bridges control, estimation and visual SLAM

nodes.n: Autonomous Navigation for Flying Robots (TUM edX, AUTONAVx)
nodes.s: MOOC version of the TUM flying-robots lecture with lecture videos and browser-based Python exercises on quadrotor state estimation, Kalman filtering, control and visual navigation.
nodes.kt: Lighter-weight than the full lecture Python exercise format is easy to adapt

nodes.n: Kalman and Bayesian Filters in Python
nodes.s: Free interactive book as Jupyter notebooks: g-h filters, discrete Bayes, univariate and multivariate Kalman filters, EKF, UKF, particle filters and smoothers, all with runnable code built on the companion FilterPy library.
nodes.kt: Intuition-first, code-first; ideal for teammates new to filtering Notebooks run in Binder or locally FilterPy gives drop-in KF/EKF/UKF classes for prototypes

nodes.s: Free web tutorial deriving the Kalman filter through worked numerical examples (alpha-beta filter, 1D and multidimensional KF, EKF, UKF), written for engineers who want the equations without heavy theory.
nodes.kt: Numeric step-by-step examples you can check by hand Good companion to Labbe for tracking problems

nodes.n: SLAM Handbook: From Localization and Mapping to Spatial Intelligence
nodes.s: Community-written handbook released in three parts during 2024-2025 and published by Cambridge University Press; the free PDF is mirrored on the editors' project page. Covers factor graphs, Lie groups, robust estimation, certifiable methods, visual/LiDAR/radar/event-based SLAM, and learned spatial representations.
nodes.kt: Most current one-stop reference on SLAM (2025) Chapters on non-visual sensors such as radar Free PDF; GitHub repo tracks newest release Single up-to-date reference spanning classic estimation and learned methods Free chapter PDFs on GitHub

nodes.n: SLAM toolbox for Matlab (EKF-SLAM teaching code)
nodes.s: Solà's Matlab EKF-SLAM toolbox, used as teaching material for his SLAM courses: modular robots, sensors, landmark parameterizations (including inverse-depth points and lines) and graph-SLAM variants. Old but clear code for learning.
nodes.kt: Readable reference implementation of EKF-SLAM Shows landmark parameterization trade-offs

nodes.n: 14 Lectures on Visual SLAM: From Theory to Practice
nodes.s: English translation of the popular Chinese visual SLAM textbook, from rigid-body motion and Lie algebra through camera models, nonlinear optimization, feature/direct VO, backend optimization, loop closure and dense mapping, each with C++ examples.
nodes.kt: Code-heavy: every chapter compiles Good bridge from theory to ORB-SLAM-style systems

nodes.n: State Estimation and Localization for Self-Driving Cars (Coursera)
nodes.s: Course 2 of the UofT Self-Driving Cars specialization: least squares, KF/EKF/ES-EKF/UKF, IMU and GNSS sensor models, LiDAR scan matching with ICP, culminating in an error-state EKF that fuses IMU, GNSS and LiDAR on CARLA data.
nodes.kt: Final project is a ready template for GNSS/IMU/LiDAR fusion Explicit error-state EKF derivation Free to audit

nodes.s: Four-course specialization covering vehicle dynamics and control, state estimation and localization, visual perception, and motion planning, using the CARLA simulator for assignments.
nodes.kt: End-to-end autonomy pipeline in one program CARLA-based assignments transfer to hackathon sims

nodes.n: GPS: An Introduction to Satellite Navigation, with an interactive Worldwide Laboratory using Smartphones
nodes.s: Stanford MOOC (originally on Coursera) now freely available as a long video series: how GPS works, pseudoranges, orbits and signals, receiver design, assisted GPS and the future of GNSS, with smartphone-based labs.
nodes.kt: Best intro to pseudoranges and receiver basics Smartphone labs pair with Android raw GNSS measurements

nodes.n: Sensor Fusion and Non-linear Filtering for Automotive Systems (edX)
nodes.s: Self-paced edX course on Bayesian filtering: state-space and motion/measurement models, Kalman filter, EKF/UKF/CKF, and particle filters, with Matlab assignments building a personal filtering toolbox.
nodes.kt: Rigorous but practical nonlinear filtering Pairs with Chalmers' multi-object tracking course

nodes.s: edX course on single- and multi-object tracking: data association, GNN/JPDA/MHT, random finite sets and PMBM filters, with Matlab assignments. Relevant for situational awareness and C-UAS track management.
nodes.kt: Modern RFS/PMBM trackers explained Direct use for radar/EO track fusion

nodes.s: Free classic course by Sebastian Thrun programming robot localization (histogram filter, Kalman filter, particle filter), search/planning, PID control and GraphSLAM in Python.
nodes.kt: Gentle, code-along intro to localization filters Particle-filter lesson is a 1-hour hackathon primer

nodes.n: Understanding Sensor Fusion and Tracking (MATLAB Tech Talks)
nodes.s: Short video series on sensor fusion for autonomous systems: what sensor fusion is, IMU/magnetometer orientation estimation, fusing GPS and IMU for pose with an asynchronous EKF, single- and multi-object tracking, and track-level fusion.
nodes.kt: Clear 10-15 minute visual explanations GPS+IMU episode maps directly to a nav-filter build

nodes.s: Annual Stanford SCPNT symposium page (8-9 October 2025) with the agenda and links to recorded student talks (Day 1) and invited speaker talks (Day 2), plus downloadable slides for many presentations.
nodes.kt: Current state of GNSS integrity, resilience and alt-PNT from leading labs Student talks are a good source of fresh project ideas

nodes.n: 2025 PNT Symposium - Day 2 Invited Speaker Presentation Videos
nodes.s: Video album of invited speaker talks from the 2025 Stanford PNT Symposium, featuring speakers such as Brad Parkinson and Jade Morton.
nodes.kt: Primary-source talks on the direction of GPS and resilient PNT

nodes.s: Page for the 28-29 October 2024 symposium with agenda, student and invited-speaker video albums, and slides; topics span GNSS, inertial sensing, timing and alternative navigation.
nodes.kt: Year-over-year view of resilient PNT research Slides downloadable for many talks

nodes.n: SCPNT Photo and Video Gallery (PNT Symposium recordings archive)
nodes.s: Archive index of Stanford PNT Symposium recordings going back to 2007, organised by year into student and invited-speaker albums.
nodes.kt: Deep back-catalogue of GNSS and PNT talks

nodes.s: Pre-conference tutorial programme of ION GNSS+, the main annual GNSS technical meeting: half-day in-depth courses by field experts on topics such as GNSS signals, receivers, PPP/RTK, inertial integration and interference.
nodes.kt: Expert-taught deep dives; topics change yearly Paid add-on to conference registration

nodes.n: ION GNSS+ Short Courses (GPS/GNSS 101 and more)
nodes.s: Short courses run at ION GNSS+ for registered attendees, including a GPS/GNSS 101 course taught by John Raquet and a space applications of GNSS course by Penina Axelrad.
nodes.kt: Fast fundamentals refresh for newcomers attending ION GNSS+

nodes.n: ION Online Tutorial: The Basics of Satellite Navigation
nodes.s: ION's free online tutorial introducing satellite navigation fundamentals: trilateration with pseudoranges, clocks, signals, error sources and augmentation.
nodes.kt: Free, short, authoritative intro

nodes.n: ION Webinar Series (archive and YouTube recordings)
nodes.s: Running ION webinar programme with summary pages per talk and a YouTube playlist of past recordings (youtube.com/playlist?list=PLPiP0PPIY2x4k1OemLZH8_OJPyLjGLYFY). Topics include GNSS spoofing and jamming, LEO PNT, signals of opportunity, quantum sensors and GNSS-denied robotics.
nodes.kt: Hour-long talks from active researchers, free Strong coverage of spoofing detection and LEO PNT

nodes.n: First results from three years of GNSS interference monitoring from low Earth orbit
nodes.s: UT Radionavigation Lab results from detecting and geolocating terrestrial GNSS jammers using receivers on LEO satellites, revealing persistent interference hotspots in conflict regions.
nodes.kt: Space-based RFI monitoring is practical Maps of jamming hotspots tied to conflict zones

nodes.s: Presents work on exploiting Starlink downlink signals for opportunistic positioning, including signal structure discovery and Doppler/pseudorange-based navigation results.
nodes.kt: Starlink can serve as an alt-PNT source without operator cooperation

nodes.n: Navigation using carrier Doppler shift from a LEO constellation: TRANSIT on steroids
nodes.s: Analysis of Doppler-only positioning from large LEO constellations, revisiting the TRANSIT concept with modern megaconstellations and quantifying achievable accuracy.
nodes.kt: Doppler positioning theory for LEO PNT

nodes.n: Implementation and Accuracy of Doppler Navigation with LEO Satellites
nodes.s: Implementation-focused talk on navigating with Doppler measurements from LEO satellites and the accuracy achieved in practice.
nodes.kt: Practical error budget for LEO Doppler nav

nodes.n: Detecting GNSS Jamming and Spoofing on Android Devices
nodes.s: Shows how Android raw GNSS measurements (AGC, C/N0, pseudoranges) can flag jamming and spoofing on commodity phones.
nodes.kt: Phones can be cheap distributed interference sensors

nodes.n: Results on GNSS Spoofing Mitigation Using Multiple Receivers
nodes.s: Spoofing detection and mitigation using several spatially separated receivers, exploiting the fact that a single spoofer produces geometrically inconsistent measurements.
nodes.kt: Multi-antenna/multi-receiver consistency checks

nodes.n: GNSS Spoofing Detection through Spatial Processing
nodes.s: Stanford work on detecting spoofing from spatial signal characteristics (angle-of-arrival consistency) using antenna motion or arrays.
nodes.kt: Direction-of-arrival is a strong spoofing discriminator

nodes.n: Robust Interference Mitigation in GNSS Snapshot Receivers
nodes.s: Interference mitigation techniques adapted to snapshot (short-capture) GNSS receivers used in low-power and IoT devices.
nodes.kt: Snapshot receivers need different mitigation than tracking receivers

nodes.n: A Robust Approach to Vision-Based Terrain-Aided Localization
nodes.s: Vision-based terrain-aided localization for aircraft, matching onboard imagery against terrain/map references as a GNSS-independent position source.
nodes.kt: Map-matching as a GNSS-denied position fix

nodes.n: Cooperative Localization for GNSS-Denied Subterranean Navigation: A UAV-UGV Team Approach
nodes.s: West Virginia University work on UAV and UGV teams sharing ranging and odometry to localize jointly in GNSS-denied underground environments.
nodes.kt: Cooperative ranging reduces drift in heterogeneous teams

nodes.n: Relative navigation of fixed-wing aircraft in GPS-denied environments
nodes.s: AFRL perspective on relative navigation for fixed-wing aircraft without GPS, keeping estimation consistent by working in a relative frame with periodic global updates.
nodes.kt: Relative navigation frames tame unobservable global drift

nodes.n: Quantum Sensors for Navigation, From Physics to Field Deployment
nodes.s: Overview of quantum sensing for navigation (atom interferometers, quantum magnetometers, clocks) and what it takes to move them from lab to field.
nodes.kt: Realistic timeline for quantum inertial and magnetic nav

nodes.n: Should It Be TPN? Prioritizing Timing in Positioning and Navigation
nodes.s: Webinar arguing for timing as the foundation of resilient PNT, covering precision terrestrial time distribution and timing/positioning from current and future LEO constellations.
nodes.kt: Timing resilience underpins telecom and power grid LEO as a timing source

nodes.n: LTE Receiver Design and Multipath Analysis for Navigation in Urban Environments
nodes.s: Design of a software receiver that extracts navigation observables from cellular LTE signals and analysis of multipath effects in urban settings.
nodes.kt: Cellular signals of opportunity are viable in cities

nodes.n: Resilience Monitoring for Multi-Filter All-Source Navigation Framework With Assurance
nodes.s: AFIT research on all-source navigation that runs multiple filters and monitors sensor integrity to detect and isolate faulty or spoofed inputs.
nodes.kt: Plug-and-play all-source nav with integrity monitoring

nodes.n: When GNSS fails, what will you do? MarRINav!
nodes.s: UK maritime resilient navigation study (MarRINav) on backups for GNSS at sea, including eLoran and R-Mode style terrestrial systems; co-sponsored by the RNT Foundation.
nodes.kt: Maritime PNT backup architecture options

nodes.s: Accessible TEDx talk from the head of UT Austin's Radionavigation Lab on GPS jamming and spoofing and why civil GPS is trivially counterfeitable, given around the time of his lab's drone and yacht spoofing demonstrations.
nodes.kt: Why unauthenticated civil GNSS is a systemic risk Good opener for a resilient-PNT pitch

nodes.n: UT Austin Radionavigation Laboratory (talks, papers, news)
nodes.s: Lab site of Todd Humphreys' group, indexing talks, briefings and papers on GNSS spoofing detection, LEO interference monitoring, Starlink-based PNT and precise automotive positioning.
nodes.kt: Hub for Humphreys' talks on spoofing and LEO PNT Papers on spoofing detection are linked from here

nodes.n: Ad Astra: Navigation with Megaconstellation LEO Satellites (GRASP on Robotics)
nodes.s: UPenn GRASP seminar by Zak Kassas on opportunistic PNT from Starlink, OneWeb and other LEO megaconstellations, addressing unknown signal structure, poor ephemerides and clock instability with his STAN (simultaneous tracking and navigation) framework validated on ground and aerial vehicles.
nodes.kt: LEO signals of opportunity as a GNSS backup Covers SDR receiver design to navigation filter

nodes.n: Low-cost GPS simulator: GPS spoofing by SDR (DEF CON 23)
nodes.s: DEF CON 23 talk showing that open-source tools and cheap SDRs can generate counterfeit GPS L1 signals that fool phones and a consumer drone; the speakers end with defensive advice such as multi-constellation positioning and spoofing detection in chipsets.
nodes.kt: Shows how low the barrier to civil GPS spoofing is Motivates detection and multi-source fusion in any drone build

nodes.n: Who cares about the Baltic Jammer? Terrestrial Navigation in the Baltic Sea Region (39C3)
nodes.s: 39th Chaos Communication Congress talk from DLR researchers on R-Mode, a terrestrial maritime navigation backup built on existing radio beacons and coastal infrastructure, tested in the heavily jammed Baltic. Covers real-world jamming impacts, transmitter/receiver build-out and the path from research to critical infrastructure.
nodes.kt: Concrete view of Baltic jamming/spoofing effects on ships, aircraft, timing Terrestrial backups as an alternative to space-based ones

nodes.n: Detect GNSS jamming and spoofing (Android developer guide)
nodes.s: Android developer documentation on the platform APIs and signals that apps can use to detect GNSS jamming and spoofing on phones.
nodes.kt: Phone-based interference sensing for a hackathon prototype No custom hardware needed

nodes.n: Results Jammertest 2025 - Resilient GNSS in an Era of Rising Jamming & Spoofing (webinar)
nodes.s: On-demand vendor webinar reviewing receiver behaviour during the high-power interference trials of Jammertest 2025 in Norway, with speakers from Septentrio, the GPS Innovation Alliance and drone maker UVify.
nodes.kt: Field results under interference levels like Baltic/Eastern Europe Vendor view; treat claims accordingly

nodes.n: Jamming, spoofing and secure positioning: Jammertest insights (u-blox webinar)
nodes.s: On-demand u-blox webinar on what multi-band receiver testing at Jammertest revealed about positioning continuity under interference and hybrid spoofing detection.
nodes.kt: Multi-band receivers and spoofing detection in mass-market chips

nodes.s: Spectrum-policy podcast episode with PNT consultant Logan Scott on GNSS jamming, spoofing, adjacent-band interference and mitigations, and the global rise in spoofing incidents affecting aviation.
nodes.kt: Policy and spectrum angle on GNSS interference

nodes.n: From the Crows' Nest - growing threats to GPS/GNSS (Dana Goward)
nodes.s: Episode of the Association of Old Crows electronic warfare podcast in which RNT Foundation president Dana Goward discusses threats to GPS and the case for terrestrial and other backups.
nodes.kt: EW-community framing of PNT resilience

nodes.n: Dana A. Goward on Geospatial FM podcast (RNT Foundation)
nodes.s: RNT Foundation post linking Dana Goward's Geospatial FM podcast appearance on GPS vulnerability and national PNT resilience policy.
nodes.kt: Advocacy perspective on eLoran and PNT backups

nodes.n: EUDIS Defence Hackathon, 3rd edition (with BraveTech EU)
nodes.s: EU defence hackathon (17-19 October 2025, eight locations) with challenges on protecting space assets, space for defence (including navigation and coordination) and sovereign aerospace including drone countermeasures; a recorded pre-hackathon webinar is on YouTube (watch?v=gLrCkk6XEuY).
nodes.kt: Shows how EU frames navigation and C-UAS challenge statements Pre-hackathon webinar recording available

nodes.n: Ukraine's DefTech at the End of 2025: From Drone Mass to Systems Warfare
nodes.s: Analysis of Ukraine's defence-tech ecosystem at the end of 2025, noting that GNSS-denied operation is now the norm and expecting broad adoption of radio-beacon, visual and fused alternative navigation in 2026.
nodes.kt: GNSS denial is a baseline requirement in current conflict Context for prioritising alt-nav in hackathon scope

nodes.s: Nav2 tutorial on outdoor navigation with GPS: fusing GNSS, IMU and odometry with robot_localization's navsat_transform, configuring Nav2 for GPS waypoints, and demonstrating it in Gazebo.
nodes.kt: Shortest working path to GPS waypoint following on a ROS 2 robot Shows datum and frame setup that trips people up

nodes.n: ROSCon UK 2025 - State Estimation for Mobile Robotics Workshop
nodes.s: Hands-on workshop material comparing two ROS 2 state-estimation approaches: Kalman filtering with robot_localization (EKF/UKF, covariance tuning, frames, rate handling) and factor-graph fixed-lag smoothing with fuse. Exercises and solutions are in a public repo.
nodes.kt: Filter vs smoother trade-offs with runnable exercises Directly reusable configs for IMU/odom/GPS fusion

nodes.n: Nav2 first-time robot setup: Odometry and robot_localization
nodes.s: Setup guide for fusing wheel odometry and IMU with robot_localization's EKF to produce the odom frame Nav2 expects.
nodes.kt: Minimal correct EKF config for a new robot

nodes.s: Index of ROSCon talks by Nav2 developers and the community (Vimeo links), including SLAM Toolbox and large-scale indoor mapping talks.
nodes.kt: Curated entry point into ROSCon navigation videos

nodes.s: Documentation for the widely used ROS EKF/UKF state estimation package, including state-estimation node configuration, sensor integration, and navsat_transform for GPS.
nodes.kt: Explains covariance and frame conventions in depth navsat_transform page is essential for GPS fusion

nodes.s: Announcement and index of ROSCon 2023 recordings and slides, including navigation talks such as bidirectional navigation with Nav2 and localization on 3D mesh surfaces.
nodes.kt: One place to find localization/navigation ROSCon talks

nodes.s: ROSCon 2024 site with the programme and links to recorded talks, including localization talks such as Ekumen's Beluga particle-filter localization library.
nodes.kt: Recent ROS 2 localization tooling talks

nodes.s: Annual PX4 developer conference; recordings are posted on the PX4 YouTube channel. The 2025 Atlanta programme included an EKF2 session on handling multiple data sources with 'reset by fusion' rather than hard resets.
nodes.kt: Primary source on EKF2 design changes Talks on external vision/non-GNSS aiding in PX4

nodes.s: Official channel with PX4 Developer Summit recordings, dev calls and feature demos.
nodes.kt: Search 'EKF2' for estimator deep dives

nodes.s: How to run PX4 software-in-the-loop with Gazebo and other simulators, including multi-vehicle setups and connecting ROS 2 and ground stations.
nodes.kt: Fastest way to test nav changes without hardware Start here for PX4 SITL Covers Gazebo, jMAVSim and community sims

nodes.s: Official Gazebo (gz) docs and tutorials: building worlds, sensors (IMU, GPS/NavSat, cameras, LiDAR), ROS 2 bridging and plugins.
nodes.kt: NavSat and IMU sensors enable GNSS-denied scenario testing

nodes.s: Docs and quickstarts for NVIDIA's GPU-accelerated stereo visual-inertial odometry and SLAM package for ROS 2 on Jetson, including tutorials with Isaac Sim and RealSense cameras.

nodes.s: Documentation for the OpenVINS MSCKF-based visual-inertial estimator, including derivations of the propagation and update steps, calibration, evaluation tooling and ROS usage.

nodes.s: Wiki for Kalibr covering multi-camera, camera-IMU and rolling-shutter calibration, target generation and data collection practice.

nodes.s: Tutorials for the open-source GNSS-SDR software receiver: signal acquisition and tracking, configuring front ends, processing recorded IQ files, and generating observables and PVT.
nodes.kt: Learn receiver internals with real IQ data Base for interference-detection experiments

nodes.kt: Factor graphs make it straightforward to add or drop GNSS Keyframe-local scan matching keeps it real time

nodes.n: KISS-ICP: In Defense of Point-to-Point ICP -- Simple, Accurate, and Robust Registration If Done the Right Way
nodes.s: Argues that a carefully engineered point-to-point ICP with motion compensation and adaptive thresholds matches far more complex LiDAR odometry across platforms.
nodes.kt: Few parameters, works across sensors and platforms Strong baseline before reaching for complex pipelines

nodes.s: Presents an error-state iterated Kalman filter that sequentially fuses LiDAR and image measurements against a shared voxel map, with exposure and plane-prior handling.
nodes.kt: Sequential updates handle LiDAR/camera dimension mismatch Robust when one modality degrades

nodes.n: DROID-SLAM: Deep Visual SLAM for Monocular, Stereo, and RGB-D Cameras
nodes.s: Learned SLAM that iteratively refines poses and depth through a differentiable dense bundle adjustment layer.
nodes.kt: Big robustness gains on hard sequences GPU-heavy

nodes.n: MASt3R-SLAM: Real-Time Dense SLAM with 3D Reconstruction Priors
nodes.s: Builds a real-time dense monocular SLAM system on the MASt3R two-view reconstruction prior, without assuming a fixed parametric camera model.
nodes.kt: 3D foundation models can serve as SLAM front ends Works with uncalibrated video

nodes.n: Kimera: an Open-Source Library for Real-Time Metric-Semantic Localization and Mapping
nodes.s: Describes the Kimera stack: VIO, robust pose-graph optimization, mesh reconstruction and semantic mapping in one open library.
nodes.kt: Metric-semantic maps on CPU in real time Modular: VIO, RPGO, mesher, semantics

nodes.n: Kimera-Multi: Robust, Distributed, Dense Metric-Semantic SLAM for Multi-Robot Systems
nodes.s: Distributed multi-robot SLAM where robots exchange compact information peer to peer and jointly optimize with outlier-robust distributed pose-graph optimization.
nodes.kt: Peer-to-peer, no central server Robust to bad inter-robot loop closures

nodes.s: Comprehensive survey of event cameras: sensing principle, algorithms (feature tracking, optical flow, VO/SLAM) and applications.
nodes.kt: Microsecond latency and high dynamic range Algorithms must be redesigned for asynchronous data

nodes.n: How NeRFs and 3D Gaussian Splatting are Reshaping SLAM: a Survey
nodes.s: Survey of SLAM methods that use neural radiance fields or 3D Gaussian splatting as the map representation, organized by sensor and technique.
nodes.kt: Radiance-field maps trade compute for photorealism Most methods are GPU-bound and not yet embedded-ready

nodes.s: Monocular and RGB-D SLAM that tracks and maps directly against 3D Gaussians using analytic Jacobians for camera pose optimization.
nodes.kt: Single representation for tracking, mapping and rendering

nodes.n: LiDAR Odometry Survey: Recent Advancements and Remaining Challenges
nodes.s: Survey of LiDAR-only, LiDAR-inertial and multi-sensor LiDAR odometry, with discussion of datasets, evaluation and open challenges such as degeneracy.
nodes.kt: Taxonomy of LiDAR, LiDAR-inertial and LiDAR-plus-other fusion Geometric degeneracy (tunnels, open fields) is a key open issue

nodes.n: 4D Millimeter-Wave Radar in Autonomous Driving: A Survey
nodes.s: Survey of 4D imaging radar: signal processing, datasets, calibration, perception and SLAM/odometry uses.
nodes.kt: 4D radar adds elevation and works in adverse weather Sparse, noisy point clouds need radar-specific methods

nodes.n: CFEAR Radarodometry - Conservative Filtering for Efficient and Accurate Radar Odometry
nodes.s: Learning-free spinning-radar odometry that keeps the strongest returns per azimuth, builds oriented surface points and registers against a keyframe history (IROS 2021).
nodes.kt: Simple filtering beats heavier radar pipelines Runs fast on a single CPU thread per the authors

nodes.n: Edge-based Monocular Thermal-Inertial Odometry in Visually Degraded Environments
nodes.s: Thermal-inertial odometry that tracks thermal image edges instead of corner features, targeting darkness and smoke where visible cameras fail.
nodes.kt: Thermal edges are more stable than corners in low-contrast IR Relevant for night and obscurant operations

nodes.n: В Україні представили візуальний навігаційний модуль OSCAR, що забезпечує стійкість дронів до РЕБ
nodes.s: English: 'Ukraine unveils the OSCAR visual navigation module that makes drones resilient to EW'. Twist Robotics' OSCAR (Optical System of Coordinates with Automatic Relocalization) recognises terrain landmarks in camera frames, matches them to a map, computes coordinates and passes them to the autopilot. Vendor claims: up to 20 m accuracy, day and night, over 500,000 km flown in 24 months, development aided by an in-house combat simulator ('Obrii').
nodes.kt: Map-matching visual positioning is fielded as an autopilot position source, not as a research demo Vendor accuracy claim is ~20 m, which sets a realistic bar for hackathon VPS demos Simulation of combat conditions is part of the development loop Interfaces, weight and supported autopilots are not stated

nodes.n: Компанія, що постачає CRPA-антени для російських дронів, показала нову 32-елементну модель
nodes.s: English: 'Company supplying CRPA antennas for Russian drones shows a new 32-element model'. Explains CRPA (controlled reception pattern antenna) as a multi-element array with digital beamforming that nulls interference directions while keeping satellite signals, and lists vendor specs of a 32-element Harxon unit shown at DWC2026 (up to 31 simultaneous interferers, under 6.5 kg, up to 90 W).
nodes.kt: CRPA element count is escalating (4 => 16 => 24 => 32) as an arms race against jamming An N-element array can null up to N-1 interference sources Size, weight and power of high-element CRPAs limit them to larger airframes Explains why broadband jamming alone is losing effectiveness against long-range UAVs

nodes.n: Brave1 запускає лабораторію для тестування CRPA-антен
nodes.s: English: 'Brave1 launches a lab for testing CRPA antennas'. Ukraine's defense-tech cluster opened a lab with EW equipment where domestic developers can test anti-jam GNSS antenna prototypes against jamming and get feedback before fielding. Test procedures are not described.
nodes.kt: Ukraine treats anti-jam GNSS antennas as a domestic product category with a dedicated test facility Testing against real EW emitters is the gate before field use Shows the government-cluster model (Brave1) for EW-resilience hardware

nodes.n: «Інколи від РЕБ очікують більше, ніж вона може». Як радіоелектронна боротьба працює проти FPV і «Шахедів»
nodes.s: English: 'Sometimes more is expected from EW than it can deliver. How electronic warfare works against FPVs and Shaheds'. Explainer for engineers on defensive EW: control uplink, video downlink and GNSS as separate attack surfaces, why radio reconnaissance must precede jamming, why spoofing is weaker against drones with CRPA antennas and position-jump filters, and why fiber-optic and vision-autonomous drones bypass RF EW.
nodes.kt: Detection/RF reconnaissance comes before any effective jamming; protocols and frequencies shift often Plausibility filters on position jumps plus CRPA blunt GNSS spoofing Fiber-optic and onboard-vision drones remove the RF link entirely, so layered defense (EW + interceptors + fire) is the field answer Friendly-fire on own drones is a real cost of EW

nodes.n: Як модернізуються «Шахеди» і чи є там штучний інтелект. Розбір DOU
nodes.s: English: 'How Shaheds are being upgraded and whether there is AI inside. DOU breakdown'. Threat-side view of a long-range one-way UAV's navigation stack, useful for defenders: satellite navigation plus INS on pre-planned routes, 16-element CRPA antennas for jam/spoof resistance, and cellular modems used as trackers rather than as a navigation link.
nodes.kt: Upgraded long-range UAVs combine GNSS, INS and CRPA, which reduces the value of GNSS jamming as a defense Cellular modems are telemetry/tracking aids, not navigation Defensive conclusion in the article: interceptors outperform EW against these threats

nodes.n: «Ми почали будувати захищену екосистему для всіх військових застосунків». Архітектор DELTA - про розвиток системи
nodes.s: English: 'We started building a secure ecosystem for all military applications. DELTA's architect on the system's development'. Interview on Ukraine's DELTA situational-awareness system: a shared core fed by aerial recon, satellites, drones and radars; a map as one view; a synchronization matrix linking drone missions to map objects; streaming, chat with zone alerts, mobile app, AI video detection; security built on NIST 800-53 and FIDO2.
nodes.kt: SA systems in Ukraine evolved from a single map into a product ecosystem on a common data core Contrasted with the NATO model of separate systems joined by custom integration Security baseline cited: NIST 800-53 and FIDO2 phishing-resistant auth Offline/edge operation is not discussed

nodes.n: Шукають РЕБ/РЕР рішення для боротьби з ворожими дронами. Деталі про Jammer Hackathon
nodes.s: English: 'EW/ELINT solutions against enemy drones wanted: Jammer Hackathon details'. Problem statement of the Brave1 + D3 Jammer Hackathon (29 Nov - 1 Dec 2024, $100k pool). Tracks: disrupting commercial-class drones via their control protocols, and automatic drone detection and tracking.
nodes.kt: Counter-UAS detection and tracking was an explicit hackathon track Organisers named concrete commercial reference drones, so problem statements are platform-specific Shows the typical Brave1 hackathon format: short sprint, jury pitch, follow-on funding

nodes.n: Завершився Jammer Hackathon, де шукали РЕБ/РЕР рішення для фронту. Які проєкти перемогли
nodes.s: English: 'Jammer Hackathon is over: which EW/ELINT projects won'. Results page: winners include a reactive EW system, an FPV video-signal detector, and a radio-monitoring / direction-finding decision-support system (SPRMT); prizes $20k/$10k/$7k with a further $50k for one-month progress.
nodes.kt: Winning themes cluster around detection, direction finding and decision support, not only jamming Short one-line descriptions only; no technical depth published Follow-on prize for progress after a month is part of the format

nodes.n: У 17 років створив навігацію для дронів, яку не глушить РЕБ. Історія киянина, який переміг на «Олімпіаді геніїв» у США
nodes.s: English: 'Built EW-proof drone navigation at 17: the story of a Kyiv student who won the Genius Olympiad in the USA'. Describes an urban GNSS-free concept: an IMU dead-reckons, side-looking rangefinders measure distances to buildings at roughly 7th-floor height, and the ranges are matched to OpenStreetMap building geometry about once per second. Simulation in C#/MonoGame; hardware tests on a Betaflight FPV were at bench stage.
nodes.kt: Rangefinder-to-building matching against OSM is a cheap urban alternative to camera VPS Correction at ~1 Hz bounds IMU drift Status at publication: simulation plus bench tests, not flight-proven

nodes.n: Vyriy створила маякову навігацію для дронів, яка працює без GPS і зв’язку
nodes.s: English: 'Vyriy built beacon navigation for drones that works without GPS or a data link'. Ground radio beacons placed along a route in advance; an onboard board ranges to several beacons by delay or signal strength and trilaterates, like a local terrestrial GNSS. Frequencies, range and accuracy are not disclosed.
nodes.kt: Local terrestrial ranging beacons are a fielded GNSS substitute in Ukraine Works without any link to the operator once the route is confirmed No performance numbers published

nodes.n: Троє 20-річних хлопців за 24 години створили дрон, якому не потрібен GPS
nodes.s: English: 'Three 20-year-olds built a drone that needs no GPS in 24 hours'. Ukrainian retelling (citing Defense One) of a US hackathon-born build motivated by Ukrainian front-line feedback: downward camera frames matched to stored imagery, ~256 GB of compressed map tiles covering 10,000+ sq km on an SD card, under $500 of hardware.
nodes.kt: Hackathon-scale VPS is feasible with commodity compute and pre-loaded tiles Map storage and preloading time are the practical bottlenecks Body text says several days of work, not 24 hours; open problems are altitude and speed envelope

nodes.n: 12 переможців і призовий фонд у 120 000 доларів: результати Хакатону «Наступ машин»
nodes.s: English: '12 winners and a $120,000 prize pool: results of the Onslaught of Machines hackathon'. Official MoD results page: 2,000+ applications, 450 participants, 12 winners at $10k each. Winning-idea areas include advanced navigation systems, resilient communications, real-time recon data transfer, coordination of unmanned systems and network integration of heterogeneous unmanned systems.
nodes.kt: Navigation and resilient comms were named winning areas at a state-run drone hackathon Judging criteria: deployment readiness, scalability, timeline Winners are not named on the page

nodes.n: European Defense Tech Hackathon: Як стартапи в Мюнхені вирішують проблеми оборони України
nodes.s: English: 'European Defense Tech Hackathon: how startups in Munich tackle Ukraine's defense problems'. Report from the Feb 2025 Munich edition (48 h, 200+ participants). Tracks included machine vision for counter-drone use, autonomous underwater navigation and improved radio reconnaissance. Brave1's stated expectation: integrable components, not finished systems.
nodes.kt: Hackathon outputs are valued as quickly integrable components Underwater navigation appeared as a track Teams, networks and investor access are the main realistic outcomes of 48 h

nodes.n: Боротьба за координати. Глобальні навігаційні системи та їх значення у сучасних військових конфліктах
nodes.s: English: 'The fight for coordinates. GNSS and its role in modern military conflicts'. Pre-invasion (Jan 2022) Ukrainian overview of GNSS dependence, documented Russian interference during exercises in the Nordics/Baltics and Crimea, and responses: multi-constellation receivers, modernised GPS signals, quantum navigation research.
nodes.kt: Baseline for how the GNSS-interference picture looked just before 2022 Multi-constellation use is the first-line civilian mitigation Good intro context for non-specialists

nodes.s: English: 'Drone optical navigation algorithm'. Master's defense slides (Kyiv-Mohyla Academy): a GeoTIFF map is cut into field-of-view tiles with precomputed keypoints; each drone frame is matched (ORB vs SuperPoint+SuperGlue) against tiles near the current estimate, a homography gives position, and fallback strategies handle lost or repeating fixes. Reported on 930 tiles: SuperPoint+SuperGlue reached the goal in fewer steps with more matches but ~631 s run time vs ~26 s for ORB; goal reached in 30/30 runs.
nodes.kt: Tile pre-indexing plus local search around the last fix is the practical VPS structure Learned matchers win on match count but cost ~25x run time in this setup Explicit fallback behaviours (repeat detection, default heading) matter as much as the matcher Motivation cites both EW and fiber-optic range limits

nodes.n: Метод навігації БПЛА в умовах відсутності GPS-сигналу на основі візуальної одометрії
nodes.s: English: 'UAV navigation method in GPS-denied conditions based on visual odometry'. Short Ukrainian conference paper: ORB features, a modified RANSAC and Kalman refinement for frame-to-frame VO, targeting +/-5 m and 10 Hz. Authors report 4.8 m position error (33% better than their baseline) and 42 ms per frame on a 10,000-frame closed-loop flight set.
nodes.kt: Sets a concrete target spec (+/-5 m, +/-2 deg, >=10 Hz) typical of Ukrainian academic work Classic ORB + RANSAC + KF pipeline, not learned features Results are the authors'; dataset not published

nodes.n: Інтелектуальна кіберфізична система для навігації БПЛА в умовах дії засобів РЕБ противника
nodes.s: English: 'Intelligent cyber-physical system for UAV navigation under enemy EW'. Journal article fusing IMU data with optical-flow cameras via an EKF to hold position without any external radio signal, with a comparison of sparse (Lucas-Kanade), dense (Farneback) and learned (RAFT) optical flow.
nodes.kt: Side-by-side of LK, Farneback and RAFT for UAV flow is a handy reference EKF remains the default fusion choice in Ukrainian applied work Framed explicitly around full loss of external RF

nodes.s: English: 'UAV control and navigation system'. KPI authors describe an ArduPilot-based control and navigation architecture intended to keep working under EW: protected GPS module, inertial navigation, backup channels, and ArduPilot code modifications including pseudo-random frequency reassignment for the link.
nodes.kt: Ukrainian practice modifies ArduPilot rather than writing autopilots from scratch Link resilience (frequency agility) is treated together with navigation resilience System-level description; limited quantitative evaluation

nodes.n: Комбіноване керування безпілотними літальними апаратами в умовах радіоелектронної боротьби
nodes.s: English: 'Combined UAV control under electronic warfare'. Lviv Polytechnic article proposing a fiber-optic outbound leg plus anti-jam radio return leg, EO/IR fusion, and GNSS-free navigation with visual-inertial and lidar odometry corrected by baro and magnetometer, switched by a deterministic state machine. Reports prototype results over a 40 km mission (author figures: drift under 0.7%, 96% success over 50 runs).
nodes.kt: Mixed fiber + radio links appear as an EW-resilience pattern in Ukrainian research Deterministic mode switching between nav sources is emphasised Numbers are self-reported prototype results

nodes.n: Шляхи підвищення стійкості управління безпілотним літальним апаратом у завадовій обстановці
nodes.s: English: 'Ways to increase UAV control resilience in a jamming environment'. Survey-style article from the National Guard Academy: optical/landmark navigation, hybrid GPS+optics, lidar, wideband data links, swarm concepts and adaptive signal processing as resilience levers.
nodes.kt: Readable Ukrainian-language map of the resilience options considered by practitioners Lists landmark-based optical navigation systems as a key direction Survey, not new results

nodes.n: Помехи в глобальных навигационных спутниковых системах
nodes.s: English: 'Interference in global navigation satellite systems'. Habr article by a developer of interference-resistant receivers: why GNSS is below the noise floor, receiver structure (front end, 1-2 bit sampling, per-satellite correlator channels), narrowband vs wideband jamming and spoofing, and their effect on code/carrier tracking loops.
nodes.kt: Clear receiver-level explanation of how jamming breaks tracking loops Low-bit quantization trades SNR for simpler correlators, which matters under jamming Anti-jam methods were deferred to a part 2

nodes.s: English: 'GPS: jammers, spoofing and vulnerabilities'. Early Russian-language overview: how spoofing gradually walks a receiver off, the 2013 UT Austin yacht demonstration, consumer jammers sold in Russia, lab results on car jammers, and proposed defenses. The comment thread adds practitioner views (TERCOM as a GPS backup, antenna shielding limits).
nodes.kt: Gradual pull-off is the core spoofing technique Cheap personal jammers were already widespread years before 2022 Comments are a source of practitioner folklore, not verified data

nodes.s: English: 'SDR GPS receiver on a microcontroller'. Builds a real-time software GPS receiver on an STM32F4 (later ESP32) fed with 1-bit samples from a MAX2769 front end: XOR-based correlation, table bit-sums, four time-multiplexed channels with DLL/PLL, navigation decoding, RTCM 3 pseudorange output and on-chip RTKLIB positioning (author reports ~80 m indoors).
nodes.kt: A GPS receiver can run on a commodity MCU without FPGA Exposes the tracking loops that interference attacks Good hands-on companion to receiver-theory articles

nodes.s: English: 'High-precision GNSS RTK navigation'. Hands-on review of the u-blox ZED-F9P: tracing letters and spinning the antenna on a carousel to visualise RTK Fixed track quality. Comments add practical limits (lower RTK rate with more constellations, LoRa correction links, urban canyon dropouts).
nodes.kt: Simple visual tests (carousel, letters) expose RTK fix quality without survey gear RTK output rate drops with the number of constellations Comment thread has DIY base-station experience

nodes.n: RTKLib - Сантиметровая точность GPS/ГЛОНАСС в пост-обработке
nodes.s: English: 'RTKLIB: centimeter-level GPS/GLONASS accuracy in post-processing'. Step-by-step base (rooftop) + rover logging with two raw-capable receivers and processing with STRSVR, RTKCONV and RTKPOST in kinematic mode; author reports fixed solutions for 97.3% of epochs.
nodes.kt: Complete RTKLIB post-processing walk-through in Russian GLONASS enabled alongside GPS Useful for building ground truth for nav experiments

nodes.n: Как я научил квадрокоптер возвращаться домой без GPS: алгоритм «верёвочной лестницы»
nodes.s: English: 'How I taught a quadcopter to return home without GPS: the rope-ladder algorithm'. Explains why integrating optical flow velocity drifts so that the drone ends up offset after return, and replaces it with stored keyframe 'rungs' matched on the way back. Habr blocked automated fetch, so author and date are not verified (year inferred from the companion repo, created July 2025); content summarised from search snippets and the repo README.
nodes.kt: Flow integration error accumulates; keyframe matching bounds it for return-home Teach-and-repeat is a pragmatic answer when only the way back matters

nodes.n: Уловки, подсмотренные у медоносных пчёл, помогают дронам возвращаться домой без GPS
nodes.s: English: 'Tricks borrowed from honeybees help drones return home without GPS'. Russian translation of a New Atlas piece on TU Delft's Bee-Nav: after a short exploratory flight capturing panoramas, a tiny network (3.4 KB indoors, 42 KB outdoors) estimates direction and distance home. Reported outdoor runs exceeded 600 m, with ~70% success in wind.
nodes.kt: Homing can be learned with kilobyte-size models Wind tilt degrades panoramic matching Shows Russian tech media tracking GNSS-free homing closely

nodes.n: Навигация без GPS, которая уже работает
nodes.s: English: 'Navigation without GPS that already works'. Overview of deployed or demonstrated non-GNSS methods: accelerometer-based subway positioning, a star-tracker drone prototype (Raspberry Pi 5, night only, ~4 km accuracy), quantum-magnetometer map matching (AQNav), quantum accelerometers, and barometric tunnel detection.
nodes.kt: Broad menu of alternative PNT methods with honest limits (night-only, km-level) Magnetic anomaly navigation is presented as the most mature quantum-sensing use

nodes.n: Навигация квадрокоптера с использованием монокулярного зрения
nodes.s: English: 'Quadcopter navigation using monocular vision'. Walk-through of monocular navigation on a Parrot AR.Drone: building an obstacle map from a single camera and correcting the trajectory.
nodes.kt: Early Russian-language introduction to monocular VO/SLAM on a toy platform Scale ambiguity and obstacle mapping are the central difficulties

nodes.n: Технология коррекции навигационных параметров БПЛА в условиях отсутствия сигналов спутниковой навигации с использованием методов оптической одометрии
nodes.s: English: 'Technology for correcting UAV navigation parameters without satellite signals using optical odometry'. Short competition paper from Russia's state aviation systems institute on correcting micro-multicopter navigation with optical odometry when GNSS is absent, framed by autonomy-level roadmaps.
nodes.kt: Shows GNSS-denied optical odometry was an institutional priority in Russia by 2016 Framed around small multicopters

nodes.n: Навигация по снимкам местности на основе сопоставления глубоких признаков и визуальной одометрии
nodes.s: English: 'Terrain relative navigation based on deep feature template matching and visual odometry'. Belarusian journal article: self-supervised (triplet-loss) deep features for matching UAV views to satellite patches across season, weather and lighting; visual odometry bridges featureless forest/field areas; an entropy filter plus path planning steers flights over feature-rich terrain.
nodes.kt: Plan the route over informative terrain instead of only improving the matcher Self-supervised features avoid labelled cross-season data VO bridges texture-poor segments between absolute fixes

nodes.n: Разработка алгоритма абсолютной визуально-инерциальной навигации беспилотных воздушных судов
nodes.s: English: 'Development of an absolute visual-inertial navigation algorithm for unmanned aircraft'. Russian preprint comparing absolute navigation methods against preloaded satellite maps and proposing a season-invariant SIFT keypoint matching approach corrected by INS, optimised for real time and evaluated on real flight data against GNSS reference. Year inferred from the PDF (references run to 2025).
nodes.kt: Absolute map-based fixes + INS is the mainstream Russian approach too Seasonal invariance is the named key problem Evaluated against GNSS reference on real flights

nodes.n: Алгоритм планирования маршрута БПЛА в условиях недостатка визуальных ориентиров
nodes.s: English: 'UAV route planning algorithm under a shortage of visual landmarks'. Journal article (Analysis and Data Processing Systems, vol. 94 no. 2) on planning routes so a video-navigation system keeps seeing enough landmarks when satellite navigation is unavailable.
nodes.kt: Navigation-aware path planning: route choice is a resilience lever Pairs naturally with map-matching VPS that fails over texture-poor areas

nodes.n: GPS complex interference models and the possible antispoofing protective measures
nodes.s: Belarusian conference paper (BSUIR, 'Information radiosystems and radiotechnologies 2022'; English title, Russian-language repository) on GPS interference models and possible anti-spoofing protections. Only the metadata was checked; conclusions not verified.
nodes.kt: Example of the Belarusian academic literature on spoofing defences Metadata only verified

nodes.s: English: 'An ambiguous signal'. Russian-language independent journalism on GNSS interference over Europe: cites an EU states' report to ICAO (about 123k affected flights in Jan-Apr 2025), Estonian, Lithuanian and Polish statistics, jamming vs spoofing mechanics, and trackers such as gpsjam.org and gpswise.aero.
nodes.kt: Interference has spilled far beyond the front line into civil aviation Spoofing shows up as position jumps of hundreds of km and inconsistent instrument readings Public trackers are the main open data sources cited

nodes.s: English: 'Optical Flow navigation - Clover docs'. Russian-language official documentation for enabling downward-camera optical flow on the Clover quadcopter (requires a laser rangefinder), the ROS topics involved and the PX4 EKF2/flow parameters to set, plus tuning advice. Year approximate (docs are continuously updated).
nodes.kt: Concrete parameter list for optical-flow-only position hold in PX4 Rangefinder is mandatory for metric flow Max horizontal speed is limited in flow mode

nodes.s: English: 'Navigation by marker map - Clover docs'. Russian documentation for flying with a map of ArUco markers (floor or ceiling), publishing the resulting pose to the flight controller as a vision position estimate, and commanding flights in the marker-map frame. Year approximate.
nodes.kt: Fiducial maps are the fastest way to get GNSS-free indoor positioning for a demo Shows the generic pattern: external pose => VPE => autopilot EKF

nodes.s: Russian-language page of COEX's international open-source flying-robotics contest built on the Clover platform: format (teams develop open-source projects over months with expert feedback), final standings and links to projects, including a radio-navigation system entry.
nodes.kt: Open-source requirement makes finalist repos reusable Long-format contest, unlike 48 h hackathons Navigation and swarm entries recur across editions

nodes.n: Integrity monitoring for alt-PNT: solution-separation FDE, protection levels and a Stanford diagram
nodes.s: A stdlib-only simulated UAV flight with INS, VIO-like velocity, intermittent visual-geolocalization fixes (repetitive-texture outliers, map-misregistration bias, dropouts over water), optional coarse MagNav-like fixes and a GNSS that is jammed and then spoofed. An 8-state EKF with chi-square innovation gating feeds a solution-separation bank that detects, excludes or (with only two sources) alerts and resolves by dead-reckoning consistency, computes horizontal protection levels against an alert limit, and reports MI/HMI, availability, time-to-alert and an ASCII/SVG Stanford diagram. A monitor-off negative control shows the misleading-information events the monitor removes.
nodes.v: ran with python3.14.7 stdlib on 2026-11-06: default run, --magnav, --no-gnss, --al-sweep, 20-seed Monte Carlo for 8 configurations, CSV and SVG writers (SVG rendered with macOS qlmanage and inspected); 15 unit tests pass (python3 -m unittest), and the detection tests were confirmed to fail with detection disabled. Synthetic data only; no real flight log or indexed repo was run.

nodes.n: ArduPilot EKF3 source-set switch under GPS denial
nodes.s: Flies ArduCopter SITL on GPS, switches EKF3 to an external-nav source set (SITL vicon) with MAV_CMD_SET_EKF_SOURCE_SET, cuts simulated GPS, flies a 15 m leg, then restores it. A --no-switch contrast run shows the EKF losing position and the EKF failsafe landing the copter. EKF_STATUS_REPORT, GPS fix and local position are logged throughout; the flag decoder is stdlib with unit tests.
nodes.v: Ran on 2026-11-06 against ArduCopter Copter-4.6.3 SITL in Docker (samples/sitl-docker, linux/arm64) with pymavlink 2.4.50 on python3.12: source switch accepted, EKF kept POS_HORIZ_ABS with GPS fix_type 1 for 30 s and flew the 15 m leg; --no-switch lost position after ~6 s and triggered 'EKF Failsafe: changed to LAND Mode'. Output in README. ekf_flags.py tests (6) pass on python3.14.7. --switch-via rc not run.

nodes.n: License-clean drone frame to orthophoto geolocalization (ALIKED / DISK / SIFT + LightGlue)
nodes.s: Drone frame => NAIP orthophoto => lat/lon using only permissively licensed parts: ALIKED (BSD-3), DISK and LightGlue weights (Apache-2.0), OpenCV SIFT and MAGSAC (Apache-2.0), rasterio, public-domain NAIP from Microsoft Planetary Computer and CC0 eBee frames from OpenDroneMap. Generates synthetic frames with known truth (rotation, scale, perspective, photometric change, cross-season source) and runs real UAV frames with EXIF GPS as truth. Measured error and CPU runtime per frame are in the README.

nodes.n: GNSS/INS EKF through a GNSS outage and a spoofing walk-off
nodes.s: A stdlib-only 2D loosely-coupled GNSS/INS EKF (8 states, hand-written matrix helpers) on a synthetic vehicle with biased, noisy 100 Hz IMU and 1 Hz GNSS. It compares INS-only, EKF, EKF with a chi-square innovation gate, and a gated EKF that latches into holdover through a 60 s outage and a slowly walking spoofed offset. A sweep shows that the gate catches fast walk-offs but misses slow ones.
nodes.v: ran with python3.14.7 stdlib on 2026-11-06 (default run and --sweep), output shown in README. filterpy_crosscheck.py re-ran both with filterpy 2.0.0's ExtendedKalmanFilter doing covariance, innovation and Joseph-form update (Python 3.12.14) and reproduced the tables to the printed 0.1 m; inflating R 100x in the filterpy path changed them, so that path is live. gnss-ins-sim, KF-GINS and GTSAM were not run.

nodes.n: GNSS interference monitor from u-blox telemetry and ADS-B NACp
nodes.s: A stdlib heuristic scorer turns per-epoch receiver telemetry (C/N0 across SVs, AGC, CW jamming indicator, clock and position jumps, receiver spoofing/jamming flags) into jamming and spoofing scores with stated reasons. A pyubx2 adapter feeds it live from UBX NAV-SAT, NAV-STATUS, NAV-CLOCK, MON-RF and SEC-SIG. A second stdlib module applies the GPSJam percentage method to readsb aircraft.json NACp for area-level interference maps.
nodes.v: scorer.py, adsb_area_map.py and 15 unit tests ran on 2026-11-06 (14 stdlib with python3.14.7; the full set incl. test_ubx_replay with pyubx2 1.4.1 on Python 3.12.14); negative controls: cn0_drop weight 0 fails test_broadband_jamming, disabling NAV-SAT parsing fails test_ubx_replay. ubx_monitor.py replay mode ran on a synthetic UBX capture generated with pyubx2 (gen_synthetic_ubx.py, invented values): jamming 60-89 s and spoofing 120-159 s were flagged on every epoch, clean epochs stayed clean. Not verified: live u-blox receiver (--port/--enable, CFG-VALSET), real recordings, real readsb feed.

nodes.n: Public CORS RINEX to SPP vs RTK with RTKLIB demo5 and gnss_lib_py
nodes.s: Downloads one day of public NOAA NGS CORS RINEX for a rover/base pair 30 km apart, runs RTKLIB demo5 rnx2rtkp in single-point and kinematic RTK modes with exact CLI flags, and scores both against the stations' published ITRF2020 coordinates (propagated for plate motion) in ENU. An optional gnss_lib_py weighted-least-squares SPP covers the same data in Python, after converting RINEX 2.11 to 3.
nodes.v: ran on 2026-11-06 on real NOAA NGS CORS data (P730 rover, P731 base, 2024-04-09 12:00-14:00 GPST, GPS only, 241 epochs): RTKLIB demo5 v2.5.1 built in Docker (docker/Dockerfile) gave SPP E/N/U rms 0.62/1.24/1.02 m and RTK 0.084/0.055/0.071 m with 97% fix, scored by compare_pos.py against the propagated ITRF2020 sheet; gnss_lib_py 1.1.0 WLS (glp_spp.py, after fixing a GPST-vs-UTC epoch tag, per-chunk ephemeris selection and transmit-time SV states) gave 0.65/1.28/1.10 m. compare_pos.py's 4 unit tests ran with python3.14.7. Not verified: other days/stations, multi-GNSS, PPP, antenna phase-centre models, a native (non-Docker) RTKLIB build.

nodes.n: File-based GNSS signal chain: gps-sdr-sim => GNSS-SDR => spoofing/jamming scorer
nodes.s: A Docker (arm64/amd64) testbed that never transmits: gps-sdr-sim synthesizes GPS L1 C/A IQ for a static receiver from the shipped 2022-01-01 broadcast ephemeris, a numpy mixer adds noise, a second spoofer stream (power offset, time offset, ramp) and/or a jamming burst, GNSS-SDR 0.0.19 processes each file into PVT, RINEX and a PVT dump, and an adapter feeds the 1 Hz epochs (position, clock, per-SV C/N0) into the gnss-interference-monitor scorer. Four scenarios: clean, unaligned overpower, jam-then-spoof, and a code/carrier-aligned drag-off that walks the fix 978 m away.
nodes.v: ran end to end on 2026-11-06 with Docker arm64 on Apple Silicon (./run.sh, 223 s): gps-sdr-sim commit 28ca29a, GNSS-SDR 0.0.19 (Ubuntu 24.04 package), RTKLIB demo5 v2.5.1 rnx2rtkp. Real outputs are in out/ and quoted in the README: clean median horizontal error 3.0 m with 0 scorer alerts; drag-off captured the PVT to 977.8 m off truth with the first scorer alert at t=67 s and a missed stretch t=87-129 s; unaligned overpower and jam-then-spoof caused a GNSS-SDR PVT outage, not a capture. GNSS-SDR runs are not bit-identical between runs. Not validated against a hardware receiver; the AGC input is a file-power proxy.

nodes.n: GNSS jammer geolocation from DF bearings to TAK
nodes.s: Locates a GNSS interference source from KrakenSDR-style direction-of-arrival bearings taken at two fixed sites and one moving vehicle, with noise and multipath outliers. A stdlib robust least-squares triangulation (RANSAC + Gauss-Newton + outlier rejection) runs alongside Stone Soup particle filter and UKF estimators; the fix and its 95% error ellipse go out as Cursor-on-Target events (point + u-d-c-e ellipse) so the emitter can be reported on ATAK/WinTAK. An adapter reads the real krakensdr_doa JSON (websocket) and CSV (DOA_value.html) outputs with the bearing convention taken from its source.
nodes.v: Ran 2026-11-06: 11 unittest cases OK with python3.14.7 stdlib (geo, Kraken JSON/CSV parsing incl. HTTP poll against a local server, triangulation, ellipse, CoT build, UDP send to localhost); locate.py --method all ran with Python 3.12.14 + stonesoup 1.9.1 on synthetic data, outputs in README. Not run: a live KrakenSDR, the websocket listener (needs websockets), and rendering of the CoT ellipse on an ATAK/WinTAK client (ellipse angle convention unverified).

nodes.n: Querying the hub from LLM agents via MCP
nodes.s: A stdlib-only MCP stdio server (tools/mcp_server.py) exposes search, show, concept and neighbors over the hub's index and graph so Claude Code, Cursor and other MCP clients can query it as tools. The README covers client registration, a navigation path for agents (llms.txt, INDEX.md, concept pages, records.jsonl) and prompt recipes.
nodes.v: tools/mcp_server.py ran with python3.14.7 stdlib on 2026-11-06 by piping demo_requests.jsonl into it (initialize, tools/list, tools/call for search/concept/neighbors/show, error paths); transcript shown in README. Client registration (Claude Code, Cursor, others) was not exercised.

nodes.n: MagNav.jl quickstart: Tolles-Lawson and EKF on the SGL 2020 flight
nodes.s: A Julia walkthrough with MagNav.jl that downloads the public SGL 2020 challenge flight and Ottawa anomaly maps, compensates the scalar magnetometer with Tolles-Lawson on a calibration box, and runs the MagNav EKF against the map, printing INS-only vs EKF error and the CRLB. The README explains why magnetic anomaly navigation resists jamming and spoofing, and where it breaks down (map coverage, altitude, aircraft noise, temporal variation).
nodes.v: Ran on 2026-11-06 in the julia:1.11 Docker image (Julia 1.11.9, linux/arm64) with MagNav.jl v1.3.5, CSV v1.3.0, DataFrames v1.8.2 and FFTA pinned to 0.2.1 (FFTA 0.3.2 breaks precompilation of GlobalSensitivity): EKF DRMS 31.2 m vs INS-only final error 218.8 m on line 1006.08 with map Eastern_395. Output in README. Artifacts downloaded: sgl_2020_train ~563 MB and ottawa_area_maps ~1.2 GB on disk, plus EMAG2 ~0.5 GB pulled during precompile.

nodes.s: Bridges autopilot GLOBAL_POSITION_INT messages into Cursor-on-Target events so a UAV shows up as a friendly track on ATAK, WinTAK or iTAK. A stdlib-only CoT builder with unit tests is paired with a pymavlink + PyTAK bridge that targets a TAK server or Mesh SA multicast.
nodes.v: cot.py and 4 unit tests ran with python3.14.7 stdlib on 2026-11-06. bridge.py ran end to end on 2026-11-06 with pymavlink 2.4.50 and pytak 7.6.1 (Python 3.12.14): fake_autopilot.py (pymavlink, UDP) => bridge.py => cot_sink.py received well-formed a-f-A-M-F-Q CoT at ~1 Hz over both tcp:// and udp+wo:// (unicast to localhost). Not verified: a real autopilot or SITL, multicast 239.2.3.1, TLS, a real TAK server or ATAK/WinTAK rendering.

nodes.n: PX4 SITL GPS denial: inject, measure drift, recover
nodes.s: Flies a square mission in PX4 SITL (SIH quadrotor, headless; Gazebo also works per PX4 docs), denies GPS mid-mission, logs EKF2 health and estimated vs ground-truth position, then restores GPS and returns home. GPS denial tries MAVSDK failure injection and falls back to SIM_GPS_USED=0 because PX4 v1.17 SIH does not acknowledge GPS failure injection. A stdlib analyzer reports per-phase horizontal drift and time to a 5 m error.
nodes.v: Ran on 2026-11-06 against PX4 v1.17.0 SIH (sihsim_quadx) in Docker from samples/sitl-docker (linux/arm64) with mavsdk-grpc 4.0.5 (its bundled mavsdk_server runs on linux aarch64; the macOS arm64 wheel binary also starts): 15 s GPS denial gave 8.37 m max horizontal error and 12.7 s to 5 m (drift.py on the real log, output in README). MAV_CMD_INJECT_FAILURE for GPS timed out (no ACK) on this target. drift.py tests (4) pass. gz_x500 and ulog_drift.py not run.

nodes.n: Headless SITL in Docker: ArduCopter and PX4 SIH with one compose file
nodes.s: Dockerfiles and a compose file that run ArduCopter 4.6.3 SITL (with a simulated vicon for ExternalNav) and PX4 v1.17.0 SIH quadrotor without Gazebo or a GUI, plus a Python client image with pymavlink and mavsdk-grpc that shares the PX4 network namespace. Built and flown on linux/arm64 (Apple Silicon).
nodes.v: Built and ran on 2026-11-06 with Docker 29.5.2 on Apple Silicon (linux/arm64): both SITL images built, the ArduPilot, PX4 and VIO bridge samples flew against them, and docker compose (v5.7.0, run from the docker:29-cli image) brought both services up and a client container reached both. amd64 not tested.

nodes.n: Stone Soup radar tracking of two UAVs with JPDA and OSPA
nodes.s: Simulates two small UAVs observed by a noisy bearing/range radar with clutter and tracks them with Stone Soup's Extended Kalman filter and JPDA data association. Track quality is scored against ground truth with the OSPA metric, the detect-and-track layer of a counter-UAS airspace picture.
nodes.v: ran radar_jpda_ospa.py with stonesoup 1.9.1, numpy 2.5.4, scipy 1.18.1 on Python 3.12.14 on 2026-11-06: 2 tracks held on 2 truths, OSPA mean 17.0 m / max 53.0 m (c=100 m), identical over 3 runs after fixing set-ordering nondeterminism; output in README. Single seed and scenario, no Monte Carlo; initiators/deleters and live radar input not exercised.

nodes.n: Terrain-relative navigation with a particle filter
nodes.s: A stdlib-only simulation of TERCOM/TRN: an aircraft with a biased INS and a radar altimeter matches its measured terrain profile against a seeded synthetic DEM with a particle filter that also estimates the INS velocity bias. Prints INS-only vs PF error over time, includes a flat-terrain control, and a rasterio loader for Copernicus GLO-30 tiles.
nodes.v: terrain.py and trn_pf.py ran with python3.14.7 stdlib on 2026-11-06, output shown in README; dem_rasterio.py is an unverified sketch: syntax-checked only, requires rasterio (the GLO-30 tile URL returned HTTP 200 on 2026-11-06).

nodes.n: VIO to MAVLink bridge with ENU/FLU to NED/FRD conversion
nodes.s: Sends an external pose source (VIO topic or CSV log) to PX4 EKF2 or ArduPilot EKF3 as VISION_POSITION_ESTIMATE or ODOMETRY for GPS-denied position hold. The frame conversion (ENU/FLU to NED/FRD, world to body velocity, MAVLink covariance layout) is a stdlib module with unit tests, and the pymavlink sender plus small set_params / watch_ekf helpers sit on top.
nodes.v: Ran on 2026-11-06: frames.py tests (8 OK) and --dry-run on python3.14.7; the pymavlink ODOMETRY path ran against ArduCopter 4.6.3 SITL (EKF3 'is using external nav data', flags 0x033f) and PX4 v1.17.0 SIH (estimator_status_flags cs_ev_pos/cs_ev_hgt/cs_ev_yaw/cs_ev_vel True), both in Docker from samples/sitl-docker with pymavlink 2.4.50. Only a stationary pose was streamed; no flight on vision was tested. --msg vpe not run.

nodes.n: Drone frame to orthophoto geolocalization with LightGlue
nodes.s: Matches a nadir drone frame against a georeferenced satellite or orthophoto tile with SuperPoint + LightGlue, fits a MAGSAC homography with OpenCV, and maps the frame centre through the GeoTIFF geotransform to lat/lon. The geometry (affine geotransform, homography mapping, WGS84 UTM, haversine) is a stdlib module with unit tests; the pipeline points at UAV-VisLoc, VPAIR and University-1652 for imagery and at hloc / AnyLoc for retrieval over large maps.
nodes.v: geo_math.py and 12 unit tests ran with python3.14.7 stdlib on 2026-11-06. geolocalize.py ran on 2026-11-06 with torch 2.15.0 (CPU), LightGlue git 5a650c4, opencv-python 5.0.0.93, rasterio 1.5.2 on Python 3.12.14 against synthetic pairs cut from one public OpenAerialMap orthophoto (Tbilisi, CC-BY 4.0): 0.04-0.21 m error for yaw 0/60/135 deg, tilt and 60-150 m priors; 30.7 m error with 162 inliers when 40% of the frame was nodata at the ortho edge; a frame from a different city gave no fix (5 inliers). Frame and map come from the same survey, so this is a pipeline/geometry check, not a cross-season or real-UAV result; UAV-VisLoc/VPAIR/University-1652 were not run.

docs.b: Integration cards - flight stack, C2 and situational awareness What each card gives you in a hackathon. All 23 were written from READMEs, docs, source files and issues read through the GitHub API (plus PyPI metadata where noted). None of these repos was installed or run for the cards, and every snippet is marked "not run". Version-sensitive names (ArduPilot SITL params, PX4 SIH target and aux-global-position params) were checked against both the default branch and the latest stable tag, and the cards say which is which.   Autopilots and simulation - ArduPilot - EKF3 source sets ( EK3_SRCn_ ) switchable from RC, MAVLink or Lua. Includes a SITL ExternalNav recipe taken from the autotest suite, and SITL GPS disable/jam/glitch params ( SIM_GPS1_  on master,  SIM_GPS_  on 4.6). - PX4 - EKF2 aiding bitmasks ( EKF2_GPS_CTRL ,  EKF2_EV_CTRL , aux global position  EKF2_AGP ) and SIH.  failure gps off stuck wrong  sets up a GNSS-loss scenario. v1.17.0 and  main  differ in the target and param names.   MAVLink tooling and GCS - MAVSDK-Python - asyncio scripting for PX4. The PyPI name is now  mavsdk-grpc , because plain  mavsdk  is a different API. Covers failure injection from Python. - pymavlink - codec, connection helper and log tools. Use it to inject  VISION_POSITION_ESTIMATE  /  GPS_INPUT , and to pull GPS/EKF fields out of logs. - mavlink-router - fans out one autopilot link. Per-endpoint msg-id filters can make an agent-facing link read-only, and it logs on the companion. - QGrou

GNSS processing and receivers - RTKLIB (demo5) - Takes logs or RINEX and writes SPP/RTK/PPK/PPP  .pos  files.  str2str  and  rtkrcv  handle live NTRIP corrections. - GNSS-SDR - Software receiver: IQ file or SDR in, RINEX/NMEA/RTCM/PVT out. Streams per-channel C/N0 telemetry over UDP and has built-in Galileo OSNMA. - GPS-SDR-SIM - Generates GPS L1 IQ test files for offline receiver testing. Covers file generation only, because over-the-air transmission is illegal. The repo is archived. - gnss_lib_py - Python toolkit: Android/RINEX 3/GSDC parsers, WLS, EKF and fault detection/exclusion, all on one  NavData  table. - laika -  AstroDog  computes satellite states and tropo/iono/DCB delays and returns corrected pseudoranges for your own filter. - pyubx2 - Pure-Python UBX/NMEA/RTCM reader and writer. The card reads the jamming and spoofing flags from MON-RF, NAV-STATUS and NAV-PVT. - pygnssutils - CLIs  gnssstreamer ,  gnssntripclient ,  gnssserver  and  pyrinexconv  for logging, NTRIP corrections, running your own caster, and converting raw logs to RINEX. - OSNMAlib - Authenticates the Galileo OSNMA navigation message. Reads u-blox, Septentrio SBF, GNSS-SDR or galmon input and writes a JSON trust log.   Estimati

docs.b: Integration cards - perception, visual geo-localization, odometry, alt-nav What each card gives you in a hackathon. All 23 were written from READMEs, source files, LICENSE files and issues read through the GitHub API. None of these repos was installed or run for the cards, and every snippet is marked "not run". Throughput and resolution figures appear only where a source states them. Read the license row before you pick a model. Code license and weights license often differ, and several defaults here are non-commercial.   Feature matching (fine registration) - LightGlue - Sparse learned matcher in a few lines of PyTorch. Its default extractor is SuperPoint, whose weights are non-commercial, so use ALIKED or DISK for clean licensing. - hloc - Retrieval =  matching =  PnP against a COLMAP model, with HDF5 handoffs between stages. The  superpoint_  and  superglue  configs pull in non-commercial Magic Leap code. - RoMa - Dense matcher that holds up across season, lighting and sensor changes. Slow and CUDA-oriented, so use it as a verifier. The indoor weights are trained on ScanNet, which is non-commercial. - XFeat - Small detector/descriptor plus LighterGlue that runs in real time on a laptop CPU. Apache-2.0, weights included. The no-GPU option. - LightGlue-ONNX - Exports extractor plus LightGlue to one ONNX graph for ONNX Runtime (CPU, CUDA, TensorRT, OpenVINO) or plain TensorRT. The Jetson deploy path. Use  raco_aliked  rather than the SuperPoint default. - vismatch - One  get_

docs.s: What each card gives you in a hackathon. All 12 were written from READMEs, docs, source files and issues read through the GitHub API. None of these repos was installed or run for the cards, and every snippet is marked "not run".
docs.b: Integration cards - round 3: TAK feeds, ROS 2 bridges, fusion, simulators What each card gives you in a hackathon. All 12 were written from READMEs, docs, source files and issues read through the GitHub API. None of these repos was installed or run for the cards, and every snippet is marked "not run".   Situational awareness and RF (TAK picture) - adsbcot - readsb/dump1090 JSON or Beast feed =  CoT aircraft tracks through PyTAK. The CoT error circle comes from the NACp category number, not metres, and NIC is never read, so don't use it as a GNSS-integrity signal. - takproto - CoT XML =  TAK Protocol v1 protobuf (mesh and stream framing) and protobuf parsing ( xml2proto ,  parse_proto ). There is no protobuf =  XML function. The library is MIT but the bundled  .proto  files are GPL-3.0. - DragonSync - decoded Remote ID / DJI DroneID on ZMQ =  drone, pilot and home CoT. The default upstream decoder is a closed non-commercial binary. The API port 8088 clashes with TAK server defaults. - Heimdall DAQ firmware - coherent IQ from the 5 KrakenSDR tuners, served over shared memory or TCP 5000/5001, under KrakenSDR DoA. The no-hardware synthetic mode is effectively broken (issue  16). - Sample: GNSS jammer geolocation to TAK - KrakenSDR-format bearings =  stdlib triangulation and Stone Soup PF/UKF =  CoT point plus 95% ellipse (run, with output).   ROS 2 bridges and fusion - Micro XRCE-DDS Agent - PX4 uORB and ArduPilot DDS =  ROS 2.  master  is v3, while PX4 v1.18 expects an XRCE v2

docs.s: One-line: pure-Python generator of reference trajectories plus noisy IMU, GNSS, magnetometer and odometer data from a CSV motion profile, with per-segment GNSS visibility so you can script outages and test your filter against truth.
docs.b: gnss-ins-sim - integration card One-line: pure-Python generator of reference trajectories plus noisy IMU, GNSS, magnetometer and odometer data from a CSV motion profile, with per-segment GNSS visibility so you can script outages and test your filter against truth.        --- ---    Install   Not on PyPI (pypi.org/pypi/gnss-ins-sim returns 404).  git clone https://github.com/Aceinna/gnss-ins-sim && cd gnss-ins-sim && pip install -e .  ( setup.py : name  gnss-ins-sim , version 2.1, requires  numpy 1.10 ,  matplotlib ). Or just run demos from the repo root.     Runs on   Any OS with Python 3 + numpy/matplotlib. The Aceinna DMU380 INS demo ( demo_aceinna_ins.py ) loads prebuilt Windows  .dll s (x86/x64) from  demo_algorithms/dmu380_sim_lib ;  demo_algorithms/aceinna_ins.py  raises  OSError('Only support windows.')  on any other OS. The README's  demo_aceinna_vg.py  is not in the repo.     Inputs   Motion profile CSV: first row initial lat (deg), lon (deg), alt (m), body velocity (m/s), yaw/pitch/roll (deg); then command rows  type, yaw, pitch, roll, vx, vy, vz, duration, GPS visibility  (5 command types). IMU error model: built-in  'low-accuracy' ,  'mid-accuracy' ,  'high-accuracy'  or a dict (gyro bias deg/h, ARW deg/rt-h, bias instability, correlation s; accel bias m/s^2, VRW m/s/rt-h, ...). Optional vibration model. Or logged data via  demo_gen_data_from_files.py .     Outputs   Named data sets:  ref_pos  (LLA rad,rad,m for  ref_frame=0  NED),  ref_vel ,  ref_att_euler ,  ref

docs.s: Python implementation of Galileo OSNMA (navigation message authentication): feed it Galileo I/NAV pages from a u-blox, Septentrio, GNSS-SDR or galmon stream and it tells you, per satellite and subframe, whether the ephemeris and clock data are cryptographically authentic. Basis for an "authenticated position" or anti-spoofing demo.
docs.b: OSNMAlib - integration card Python implementation of Galileo OSNMA (navigation message authentication): feed it Galileo I/NAV pages from a u-blox, Septentrio, GNSS-SDR or galmon stream and it tells you, per satellite and subframe, whether the ephemeris and clock data are cryptographically authentic. Basis for an "authenticated position" or anti-spoofing demo.        --- ---    Install   No PyPI package.  git clone https://github.com/Algafix/OSNMA && cd OSNMA && pip install -r requirements.txt  (bitstring<5, ecdsa, pycryptodome, protobuf, pyserial, reedsolo, ntplib, pandas, pytest...). Runner scripts add  ..  to  sys.path , so run them from their own folder.     Runs on   Python 3.10-3.12 per README; tested on Linux and Windows. No GPU.     Inputs   Galileo E1-B I/NAV pages with transmission WN/TOW: Septentrio SBF ( GALRawINAV , file or IP port), u-blox UBX  RXM-SFRBX  (file, serial, socket; NAV-TIME  / TIM-TP used for time), GNSS-SDR over UDP, galmon live feed, Android GnssLogger files (post-process). Plus GSC-issued  OSNMA_MerkleTree.xml  and public key XML (shipped in the run folders).     Outputs   Verbose log and per-subframe JSON status log (schema in  osnma/utils/json_schema/status_log_schema.json ), saved KROOT / public key, TTFAF and TTFF figures.     Key API / entry points    osnma.receiver.receiver.OSNMAReceiver(input_module, param_dict) ;  .start(start_at_gst=None) ; input iterators in  osnma/input_formats/ :  SBF(path) ,  UBX(path) ,  UBXLiveSerial(port) ,  UBXLiv

docs.b: DragonSync - integration card One-line: Python gateway that subscribes to ZMQ streams of decoded drone Remote ID / DJI DroneID frames (plus kit GPS status, optional readsb aircraft, FPV alerts, Kismet devices) and emits drone, pilot and home-point CoT to ATAK/TAK, MQTT/Home Assistant and Lattice; a ready-made passive drone-detection =  common-operating-picture back end.        --- ---    Install    git clone https://github.com/alphafox02/DragonSync && cd DragonSync && pip3 install -r requirements.txt  ( cffi ,  cryptography ,  gps ,  lxml ,  netifaces ,  psutil ,  pycparser ,  pyzmq ,  requests ). Off-kit also  sudo apt install lm-sensors gpsd gpsd-clients . FAA RID lookup is a git submodule ( faa-rid-lookup , MIT): clone with  --recurse-submodules . docs.b: GPS-SDR-SIM - integration card Generates GPS L1 C/A baseband IQ sample files for a chosen static position or trajectory and time. In a hackathon use it only to produce  files  that a software receiver (GNSS-SDR) processes offline: repeatable test vectors for receiver, integrity and spoofing-detector development with no RF involved.    Legal boundary.  Radiating GNSS signals over the air without authorization is illegal in practically every jurisdiction (in the US under FCC rules and federal law; in the EU/UK under national radio law) and endangers aviation and other users. This card covers file generation and offline processing only. Any hardware test must be cabled into the receiver under test through attenuation, or done in a certified shielded enclosure under the relevant authorization.
