docs.b: px4_ros_com - integration card One-line: PX4's ROS 2 example package (listeners, offboard control in C++ and Python) plus  frame_transforms.h , the NED/ENU and FRD/FLU conversion helpers you need when you publish VIO into  /fmu/in/vehicle_visual_odometry  by hand.        --- ---    Install   In a colcon workspace:  git clone https://github.com/PX4/px4_msgs src/px4_msgs && git clone https://github.com/PX4/px4_ros_com src/px4_ros_com && colcon build . Run the Micro XRCE-DDS Agent ( MicroXRCEAgent udp4 -p 8888 ) next to PX4 SITL. Install details are delegated to the PX4 uXRCE-DDS and ROS 2 guide (README).     Runs on   ROS 2 (Humble/Jazzy per PX4 docs), Linux. Depends directly on  px4_msgs .     Inputs   PX4 uORB topics bridged as  /fmu/out/  (e.g.  sensor_combined ,  vehicle_gps_position ,  vehicle_odometry ,  vehicle_status ).     Outputs   Example publishers to  /fmu/in/offboard_control_mode ,  /fmu/in/trajectory_setpoint ,  /fmu/in/vehicle_command ,  debug_vect . Library  px4_ros_com::frame_transforms  ( include/px4_ros_com/frame_transforms.h ):  ned_to_enu_orientation ,  enu_to_ned_orientation ,  air

docs.s: One-line: pip-installable GeoTIFF/DEM reader that turns a map tile into a numpy array plus an affine transform, so a nav filter can look up terrain height or orthophoto pixels by world coordinate.
docs.b: Rasterio - integration card One-line: pip-installable GeoTIFF/DEM reader that turns a map tile into a numpy array plus an affine transform, so a nav filter can look up terrain height or orthophoto pixels by world coordinate.        --- ---    Install    pip install rasterio  (wheels bundle libgdal; latest release 1.5.2). Conda alternative:  conda install -c conda-forge rasterio  for more format drivers. Source build against system GDAL:  GDAL_CONFIG=/path/to/gdal-config python -m pip install --no-binary rasterio rasterio .     Runs on   Linux, macOS, Windows (official wheels per README). Rasterio 1.5+ needs Python  = 3.12, numpy  = 2, GDAL  = 3.8. No GPU.     Inputs   Any GDAL raster the bundled build supports: GeoTIFF/COG, VRT, JPEG2000, HDF5, netCDF (wheels include these per README); remote via  /vsicurl/  or  s3://  URLs.     Outputs    numpy  arrays (optionally masked),  Affine  transforms,  CRS  objects, written GeoTIFFs.     Key API / entry points    rasterio.open(path, mode="r") ;  DatasetReader.read(indexes=None, window=None, masked=False, ...) ;  DatasetReader.sample(xy, indexes=None, masked=False) ;  rasterio.windows.from_bounds(left, bottom, right, top, transform=None, ...) ;  rasterio.transform.xy(transform, rows, cols, offset="center")  /  rowcol(transform, xs, ys) ;  rasterio.warp.transform(src_crs, dst_crs, xs, ys) ,  reproject(...) ,  calculate_default_transform(...) ;  rasterio.vrt.WarpedVRT(src, crs=..., resampling=...) ; CLI  rio info ,  rio insp . docs.b: FilterPy - integration card Readable NumPy implementations of KF, EKF, UKF, CKF, IMM, ensemble, information, square-root and fading-memory filters plus RTS / fixed-lag smoothers: the fastest way to stand up a prototype GNSS/INS or tracking filter in Python and tune it in a notebook.        --- ---    Install    pip install filterpy  (PyPI 2.0.0, released 2026-10-26; deps numpy, scipy, matplotlib). Also  conda install -c conda-forge filterpy . The author advises against installing from git.     Runs on   Any OS with Python 3 + numpy/scipy. CPU only; numpy overhead dominates for small state vectors.     Inputs   You supply matrices/functions:  x ,  P ,  F ,  Q ,  H ,  R  as numpy arrays (column vectors  (n,1)  in the README example); for EKF a Jacobian  HJacobian(x)  and  Hx(x) ; for UKF  fx(x, dt)  and  hx(x)  plus a sigma-point object. Units and frames are whatever you choose.     Outputs   State  x , covariance  P , prior/posterior copies ( x_prior ,  x_post ), innovation  y ,  S ,  K ,  log_likelihood ,  mahalanobis ;  batch_filter  returns arrays for  rts_smoother . docs.s: One-line: MCP server that gives an LLM client (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Cursor...) discovery and pub/sub/service/action/param access to any ROS 1 or ROS 2 robot through rosbridge, with no changes to robot code; useful for an agent that inspects a nav stack ("is VIO publishing? what is the EKF covariance?") in a demo.
docs.b: ROS MCP Server - integration card One-line: MCP server that gives an LLM client (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Cursor...) discovery and pub/sub/service/action/param access to any ROS 1 or ROS 2 robot through rosbridge, with no changes to robot code; useful for an agent that inspects a nav stack ("is VIO publishing? what is the EKF covariance?") in a demo.        --- ---    Install   Client side:  claude mcp add ros-mcp -- uvx ros-mcp --transport=stdio  (PyPI package  ros-mcp , v3.1.2 at time of writing, Python  = 3.10). Robot side:  sudo apt install ros-<distro -rosbridge-server  and  ros2 launch rosbridge_server rosbridge_websocket_launch.xml .     Runs on   Any host with Python 3.10+/uv for the server; robot needs ROS with rosbridge (ROS 2 Jazzy, Humble and others; ROS 1 too, per README).     Inputs   rosbridge WebSocket, default  127.0.0.1:9090  ( ros_mcp/main.py ); the LLM can call  connect_to_robot  to change IP/port.     Outputs   MCP tool results as JSON; images via  tools/images.py .     Key API / entry points   Tools in  ros_mcp/tools/ : topics  get_topics ,  get_topic_type ,  get_topic_details ,  get_message_details ,  subscribe_once ,  subscribe_for_duration ,  publish_once ,  publish_for_durations ; services  get_services ,  get_service_type ,  get_service_details ,  call_service ; connection  connect_to_robot ,  ping_robots ; plus  actions.py ,  nodes.py ,  parameters.py ,  robot_config.py . Resources  robot_specs ,  ros_metadata .     Time to first result

docs.s: One-line: a complete ROS 2 ground-robot navigation stack (localization, costmaps, planners, controllers, behavior trees, GPS waypoint following) you can drive from a short Python script, so you spend the hackathon on localization under degraded PNT rather than on path following.
docs.b: Nav2 (ROS 2 Navigation) - integration card One-line: a complete ROS 2 ground-robot navigation stack (localization, costmaps, planners, controllers, behavior trees, GPS waypoint following) you can drive from a short Python script, so you spend the hackathon on localization under degraded PNT rather than on path following.        --- ---    Install   Binary:  sudo apt install ros-$ROS_DISTRO-navigation2 ros-$ROS_DISTRO-nav2-bringup  (per docs.nav2.org Getting Started). Source: colcon build of the distro branch ( humble ,  jazzy , ...), or the prebuilt containers at  ghcr.io/ros-navigation/navigation2 . README build table lists humble, jazzy and lyrical Debian builds.     Runs on   Ubuntu with ROS 2 (Humble on 22.04, Jazzy on 24.04 per the build table; main targets the newest distro). amd64 binaries confirmed in the build table; arm64 not checked here. No GPU required. Simulation demos use Gazebo (gz-sim) or the built-in  nav2_loopback_sim  (no physics).     Inputs   TF tree  map =  odom =  base_link  (REP-105),  nav_msgs/Odometry ,  sensor_msgs/LaserScan  /  PointCloud2  for costmaps,  nav_msgs/OccupancyGrid  map from  nav2_map_server  (YAML + PGM), goals as  geometry_msgs/PoseStamped  or  geographic_msgs/GeoPose  (GPS waypoints). Parameters in one YAML file.     Outputs    cmd_vel  ( geometry_msgs/Twist  or  TwistStamped  depending on distro), planned paths ( nav_msgs/Path ), costmaps, action results/feedback on  navigate_to_pose ,  follow_waypoints ,  follow_gps_waypoints , e

CPU only.     Inputs   ROS bags or live topics: IMU, camera images,  sensor_msgs/PointCloud2 ,  nav_msgs/Odometry  (wheel),  sensor_msgs/NavSatFix  (GNSS, e.g.  /gps/fix  in the KAIST config), PoseStamped/TransformStamped (VICON). docs.s: The fastest path from receiver logs or public RINEX to an SPP / RTK / PPK / PPP position file, plus  str2str  and  rtkrcv  for live NTRIP corrections and real-time RTK. Tuned for low-cost receivers (u-blox F9P and friends).
docs.b: RTKLIB demo5 / RTKLIB-EX - integration card The fastest path from receiver logs or public RINEX to an SPP / RTK / PPK / PPP position file, plus  str2str  and  rtkrcv  for live NTRIP corrections and real-time RTK. Tuned for low-cost receivers (u-blox F9P and friends).        --- ---    Install   Windows: prebuilt binaries on the GitHub releases page (latest tag  v2.5.1 ). Linux/macOS CLI:  git clone --depth 1 --branch v2.5.1 https://github.com/rtklibexplorer/RTKLIB.git && cmake -S RTKLIB -B RTKLIB/build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release && cmake --build RTKLIB/build -j  (README:  mkdir build; cd build; cmake ..; make; make test ). Qt5/6 needed only for the GUIs. Old per-app  gcc  makefiles still exist but are marked deprecated. Pre-built Linux packages via openSUSE OBS ( home:ReimannJens/rtklib-qt ), per README.     Runs on   Linux, Windows, macOS (CMake). Plain C, no GPU. Runs fine on a Raspberry Pi class board for  rtkrcv / str2str  (common community use, not stated in README).     Inputs   RINEX 2/3 OBS + NAV (also SP3, CLK, SBAS logs); raw receiver binaries (u-blox UBX, Septentrio SBF, NovAtel, etc.) via  convbin ; RTCM2/3 streams over serial, TCP, NTRIP for live work. Hatanaka  .crx / .d  needs  crx2rnx  on PATH.     Outputs    .pos  text solutions (llh, ECEF xyz or ENU baseline; Q flag 1=fix, 2=float, 5=single), NMEA GGA ( -n ), solution status/residual files ( -y ), KML/GPX via  pos2kml .  str2str  relays/converts streams (e.g. NTRIP =  serial to feed a receiver RTCM). docs.s: CLI and Python glue for GNSS streams: log or forward any receiver stream ( gnssstreamer ), pull RTCM corrections from an NTRIP caster ( gnssntripclient ), run your own caster ( gnssserver ), and convert u-blox raw logs to RINEX ( pyrinexconv ).
docs.b: pygnssutils - integration card CLI and Python glue for GNSS streams: log or forward any receiver stream ( gnssstreamer ), pull RTCM corrections from an NTRIP caster ( gnssntripclient ), run your own caster ( gnssserver ), and convert u-blox raw logs to RINEX ( pyrinexconv ).        --- ---    Install    python3 -m pip install --upgrade pygnssutils  (latest GitHub release v1.3.1;  =3.10 ). Pulls pyubx2 =1.4.0, pyrtcm, pynmeagps, pyspartn, pysbf2, pyunigps, pyqgc, pyubxutils, pyserial, certifi. Also on conda-forge.     Runs on   Any OS with Python 3.10+; pure Python except  cryptography  (via pyspartn), which can fail to build on 32-bit Linux.     Inputs   Serial port, TCP socket, binary file, or NTRIP caster (HTTP/HTTPS). Protocols NMEA, UBX, SBF (Septentrio), UNI (Unicore), QGC, RTCM3, SPARTN. NTRIP credentials via flags or env  PYGPSCLIENT_USER  /  PYGPSCLIENT_PASSWORD .     Outputs   Parsed text, JSON, raw binary to file/socket/serial, or a Python lambda per message. RTCM3 written back into the receiver for RTK. RINEX 3.05 / 4.02 obs + nav files.     Key API / entry points   CLIs from  pyproject.toml :  gnssstreamer ,  gnssserver ,  gnssntripclient ,  pyrinexconv . Classes:  GNSSReader( kwargs)  (multi-protocol reader),  GNSSStreamer( kwargs) ,  GNSSNTRIPClient(app=None,  kwargs) ,  GNSSSocketServer( kwargs) ,  RinexConvertor(app, rinex_version, rinex_type, gnssfilter, obsfilter, minobs, verbosity, logtofile,  kwargs) .     Time to first result   Estimate: 5 min to see RTCM

docs.s: Pure-Python reader/writer for u-blox UBX (plus NMEA and RTCM3 via sister libs): the fastest way to get PVT, raw measurements and the receiver's own jamming/spoofing flags out of a u-blox module or log file.
docs.b: pyubx2 - integration card Pure-Python reader/writer for u-blox UBX (plus NMEA and RTCM3 via sister libs): the fastest way to get PVT, raw measurements and the receiver's own jamming/spoofing flags out of a u-blox module or log file.        --- ---    Install    python3 -m pip install --upgrade pyubx2  (latest GitHub release v1.4.1;  requires-python  =3.10 ; deps  pynmeagps =1.1.8 ,  pyrtcm =1.2.1 ). Add  pyserial  for live ports.     Runs on   Any OS with Python 3.10+, pure Python, no GPU. Fine on Raspberry Pi / Jetson.     Inputs   Byte stream with a  read(n)  method: serial port, socket, or binary log opened  rb  ( .ubx  from u-center, PyGPSClient,  gnssstreamer ). UBX, NMEA 0183, RTCM3 mixed in one stream.     Outputs    (raw_bytes, parsed)  tuples;  UBXMessage  objects with scaled attributes (e.g. NAV-PVT  lat / lon  in deg,  hMSL  in mm). Repeating groups flattened with 2-digit suffixes ( jamInd_01 ,  cno_05 ). Outbound: serialized UBX commands ( msg.serialize() ).     Key API / entry points    UBXReader(stream, protfilter=NMEA_PROTOCOL\ UBX_PROTOCOL\ RTCM3_PROTOCOL, quitonerror=ERR_LOG, validate=VALCKSUM, msgmode=GET) ;  UBXReader.read() -  (bytes, msg) ;  UBXReader.parse(data, msgmode=GET)  (static);  UBXMessage(ubxClass, ubxID, mode,  kwargs) ;  UBXMessage.config_set(layers, transaction, cfgData)  /  config_del  /  config_poll  (Gen9+ CFG-VALSET/VALGET); helpers  ecef2llh ,  llh2ecef ,  haversine ,  utc2wnotow .     Time to first result   Estimate: 10 min to print NAV

docs.s: One-line: pure-Python asyncio library and CLI for sending and receiving Cursor on Target (CoT) over TCP, TLS, UDP multicast, WebSockets or the Marti REST API; the lowest-friction way to put your vehicle position, a DF bearing line or a Remote ID detection on an ATAK/WinTAK/iTAK map.
docs.b: PyTAK - integration card One-line: pure-Python asyncio library and CLI for sending and receiving Cursor on Target (CoT) over TCP, TLS, UDP multicast, WebSockets or the Marti REST API; the lowest-friction way to put your vehicle position, a DF bearing line or a Remote ID detection on an ATAK/WinTAK/iTAK map.        --- ---    Install    python3 -m pip install pytak  (latest release seen v7.6.1, 2026-08-23). Optional extras for TLS enrollment and Protobuf ( takproto ).     Runs on   Any OS with Python 3 asyncio; no required external deps for the core (README). Runs fine on a Raspberry Pi.     Inputs   Your data turned into CoT XML ( <event  with  type ,  uid ,  how ,  time/start/stale ,  <point lat lon hae ce le ). docs.b: x-io Fusion - integration card One-line: a small, dependency-free C AHRS (gyro + accel [+ mag or external heading] =  quaternion) with a matching Python package, so the attitude you prototype on a laptop is the attitude your MCU computes.        --- ---    Install   Python:  pip install imufusion==1.3.3  (latest on PyPI as of 2026-11-06). docs.s: Two off-road ground-vehicle datasets. RELLIS-3D (Texas A&M + US Army CCDC ARL, 2020): Clearpath Warthog on the RELLIS campus with lidar and camera semantic labels. TartanDrive (CMU AirLab, ICRA 2022): instrumented ATV driven aggressively off-road, aimed at learning vehicle dynamics. docs.b: MagNav challenge - paper digest  Signal Enhancement for Magnetic Navigation Challenge Problem  - Gnadt (MIT), Belarge, Canciani, Carl, Conger, Curro, Edelman, Morales, Nielsen, O'Keeffe, Rackauckas, Taylor, Wollaber (MIT, MIT Lincoln Lab, AFIT), arXiv 2020 (v2 2023). paper   code   challenge entry   Read: full text via ar5iv HTML rendering of v2 (the arXiv PDF could not be text-extracted here).   Problem A scalar magnetometer in an aircraft cabin measures the Earth core field ("25,000-65,000 nT"), the crustal anomaly field ("typically less than 1000 nT") and the aircraft's own interference field, all summed. MagNav needs the anomaly field alone to match against a map. The challenge asks for a model that removes the aircraft field from cabin magnetometers, where classical Tolles-Lawson (TL) compensation "does not produce a compensated signal with sufficiently accurate results".   Method This is a challenge-problem definition, not a method paper. What it fixes: - Task: map uncompensated cabin scalar magnetometers plus auxiliary sensors =  compensated anomaly signal. - Truth:  mag_1_c , the professionally compensated tail-stinger magnetometer. Chosen over an anomaly map to avoid position interpolation error and to share weather conditions with the cabin sensors. - Metric: standard deviation of the error between model output and truth, per flight line. - Hold-out: line 1003.10 of Flight 1003 is the evaluation line; the other lines are the build set. - Allowed inputs: diurnal, IGR

docs.b: AirIO - paper digest  AirIO: Learning Inertial Odometry with Enhanced IMU Feature Observability  - Qiu, Xu, Chen, Zhao, Geng, Scherer, IEEE RA-L 2025 (accepted per arXiv v2). paper   code   Read: full text, arXiv HTML v2 (16 Jun 2025)   Problem Learned inertial odometry (RoNIN, TLIO style) works for pedestrians but transfers badly to multirotor UAVs, whose motion is agile and not periodic. Existing UAV variants often need extra inputs (thrust, rotor speed). The paper asks why, and how to get IMU-only learned odometry on drones.   Method - Core claim: the usual practice of rotating IMU data into a global (gravity-aligned) frame couples attitude nonlinearly with the motion force and hides features the network needs. Keeping IMU data in the  body frame  keeps attitude linearly coupled with gravity and more observable. - Supported by latent-feature analysis: PCA reaches 95% energy with k=5 (body) vs k=8 (global) on Blackbird, k=15 vs k=40 on Pegasus; t-SNE separates velocity levels better in body frame. -  Attitude encoding : orientation mapped to so(3), passed through a CNN encoder, concatenated with the IMU encoder output, then bi-directional GRUs. - Two MLP heads: body-frame  velocity  and its uncertainty (diag covariance). Loss: Huber (delta 0.005) plus an uncertainty term weighted lambda 1e-4. - Training uses ground-truth orientation for the attitude input; test uses EKF-estimated orientation. -  EKF : state = rotation, global velocity, position, gyro/accel biases. docs.b: AnyLoc - paper digest  AnyLoc: Towards Universal Visual Place Recognition  - Keetha et al. (CMU, IIIT Hyderabad, MIT, Adelaide), IEEE RA-L 2023 (venue per repo README bibtex). paper   code   Read: full text via ar5iv rendering of arXiv 2308.00688, plus repo README   Problem State-of-the-art VPR models are trained on urban street imagery and break in unstructured domains (indoor, subterranean, aerial, underwater). The paper asks whether off-the-shelf foundation-model features plus unsupervised aggregation give one VPR method that works everywhere without VPR-specific training.   Method - Backbone: DINOv2 ViT-G14, frozen, features from layer 31, "value" facet; per-patch features, CLS token discarded (Sec. III-B, IV-B2). - Aggregation: hard-assignment VLAD with 32 clusters (AnyLoc-VLAD-DINOv2), or GeM (AnyLoc-GeM-DINOv2). Hard assignment beat soft and is ~1.4x faster (Sec. V-C3, Table VII). - Vocabulary (VLAD cluster centers) is built without labels from database images. Three options compared: map-specific, domain-specific (pooled over maps of the same domain, e.g. all aerial), global (Table V). Domain-specific is best. - Optional PCA-whitening down to 512-d for a ~100x smaller descriptor at similar recall (Sec. V-A1). - No training, no fine-tuning; "training-free" still needs reference-database statistics for the vocabulary and PCA.   Data and sensors - Monocular RGB only. - Structured (Table III): Baidu Mall, Gardens Point, 17 Places, Pittsburgh-30k, St Lucia, Oxford RobotCar

Prior work mostly assumes nadir views and planar scenes. Low-altitude oblique imagery breaks that, and nobody had measured how far current retrieval and matching methods fall off there.   Method Not a new model - a benchmark plus a unified coarse-to-fine baseline: - Retrieval: crop the reference map into a gallery, rank tiles against the UAV image (template matching NCC/MI, NetVLAD, CNN/transformer cross-view models such as CAMP, Sample4Geo, MCCG). - Matching: pixel correspondences between UAV image and top tiles (SIFT, ORB, SuperPoint+LightGlue variants incl. docs.b: AI-IMU Dead-Reckoning - paper digest  AI-IMU Dead-Reckoning  - Brossard, Barrau, Bonnabel, IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Vehicles 2020 (arXiv 2019). paper   code   Read: full text via ar5iv HTML render of arXiv 1904.06064   Problem Dead reckoning for a wheeled car from the IMU alone: 3D position, velocity, orientation and IMU biases in real time, so localization survives GNSS loss or camera / lidar failure. Pure integration drifts with t^2 from bias.   Method -  Right-invariant EKF on SE2(3) , 21-dim error state: orientation, velocity, position, gyro and accel biases, plus car-to-IMU misalignment rotation and lever arm (both near-constant random walks). -  Pseudo-measurements : lateral and vertical velocity in the  car  frame are about zero (non-holonomic constraint). Fed as y = 0 with covariance N_n. Car-frame vertical is argued to be more general than world-frame zero vertical velocity. -  Noise adapter : a small 1D CNN reads a window of N=15 raw IMU samples (no state) and outputs z_lat, z_up. Covariance N = diag(sigma_lat^2   10^(beta tanh z_lat), sigma_up^2   10^(beta tanh z_up)), beta = 3, sigma_lat = 1 m/s, sigma_up = 3 m/s. 2 conv layers (kernel 5, 32 channels, dilations 1 and 3), ReLU, then FC. - Only 6210 adapter parameters plus 12 entries of P0 and Q are learned. Q is learned but fixed in time. - Training: Adam lr 1e-4, batches of nine 1-minute sub-sequences at random starts, Gaussian noise std 1e-4, dropout 0.5, grad clip 1, 400 epochs. docs.b: CFEAR Radarodometry - paper digest  CFEAR Radarodometry - Conservative Filtering for Efficient and Accurate Radar Odometry  - Adolfsson, Magnusson, Alhashimi, Lilienthal, Andreasson (Orebro Univ.), IROS 2021. paper   code   Read: full text, ar5iv HTML of arXiv (v3 is latest; Table II is flattened in the HTML, so column alignment for baselines is partly inferred)   Problem Odometry in large GNSS-denied areas where vision and LiDAR degrade (rain, fog, dust, smoke). Spinning FMCW radar sees through these, but its scans are noisy and learned radar odometry generalizes poorly to new places. Goal: learning-free, fast, accurate radar odometry.   Method - k-strongest filtering: per azimuth, keep only the k strongest returns above a noise floor z_min ("conservative" filtering) (Sec. Problem UAV absolute visual localization (AVL): estimating a UAV's absolute position by matching onboard imagery to geo-referenced reference maps (satellite / aerial imagery), as an alternative or complement to GNSS. docs.b: cuVSLAM - paper digest  cuVSLAM: CUDA accelerated visual odometry and mapping  - Korovko, Slepichev, Efitorov et al. (NVIDIA), arXiv technical report 2025. paper   code   Read: full text incl. appendices, arXiv HTML v3   Problem Robots need real-time pose on low-power edge GPUs, with whatever camera rig they carry (1 to many cameras, optional IMU or depth). Most open VSLAM systems target one sensor configuration and use the CPU. cuVSLAM is NVIDIA's CUDA-accelerated VO/SLAM library, used in Isaac ROS.   Method - Classical feature-based pipeline, not learned. Frontend for low-latency local pose, asynchronous backend for loop closure and pose graph optimization (Sec. 2). - 2D module: Shi-Tomasi "Good Features to Track" on an NxM grid for uniform coverage, pyramidal Lucas-Kanade tracking with an NCC check per step, keyframe when tracked count drops below a threshold (Sec. 2.1). - Stereo (default): track left camera, PnP against local-map landmarks, left-to-right tracking + triangulation on keyframes, async CUDA sparse bundle adjustment (Schur complement). - Multi-camera (up to 32 cameras): a Frustum Intersection Graph auto-detects overlapping camera pairs from extrinsics; all observations go into one pose solve. Requires hardware-synchronized cameras. - Visual-inertial: 15-DoF state (pose, velocity, accel and gyro bias) with IMU preintegration factors, gravity estimation from an initial visual-only window, VI bundle adjustment (after Forster et al. and ORB-SLAM3). - RGB-D: dense

docs.b: Factor Graphs for Robot Perception - paper digest  Factor Graphs for Robot Perception  - Dellaert, Kaess, Foundations and Trends in Robotics Vol. 6, No. 1-2, 2017 (DOI 10.1561/2300000043), about 139 pages. paper   code   Read: full text extracted from the free author PDF (figures not viewed). This is a monograph: "headline results" below are its key worked examples and claims, not benchmarks.   Problem How to model and solve large-scale inference in robotics (SLAM, aided navigation, mapping) in one framework that is both a clean modeling language and an efficient solver. The monograph argues factor graphs fit because each sensor measurement maps to one factor.   Method Chapters, in order: - 1 Introduction: Bayes nets as generative models, MAP inference, factor graphs as the posterior p(X Z). Running toy example: 3 poses, 2 landmarks, bearing measurements (Fig. 1.1-1.3). - 2 Smoothing and Mapping: nonlinear least squares; linearization; Gauss-Newton, Levenberg-Marquardt, Dogleg. - 3 Exploiting Sparsity: the sparse Jacobian is the factor graph; QR / Cholesky = variable elimination; the Cholesky factor is a Bayes net, back-substitution solves it. - 4 Elimination Ordering: fill-in, minimum degree (COLAMD), nested dissection, block-level ordering. - 5 Incremental Smoothing and Mapping: Givens updates, marginalization, fixed-lag smoothing, Kalman filter / smoother as special cases, Bayes tree, iSAM2. - 6 Optimization on Manifolds: rotations, exponential map, local coordinates, Pose

docs.b: ETIO - paper digest  Edge-based Monocular Thermal-Inertial Odometry in Visually Degraded Environments  - Wang, Chen, Liu, Zhang (HIT Shenzhen, USTC), IEEE RA-L 2023 (arXiv 2022). paper   code   Read: full text, arXiv HTML v2 (22 Oct 2022) and the v2 PDF (Table II); repo README   Problem Visual-inertial odometry fails in darkness, glare and obscurants (smoke, dust, fog). Thermal cameras see through these but give noisy, low-contrast, texture-poor images, and flat-field correction (FFC/NUC) shutter events interrupt the stream and change image appearance. Corner trackers struggle on such images.   Method - Front end: extract edges from thermal images (Difference of Gaussians, gradient threshold, sub-pixel refinement =  binary edge image). - DT-KLT: track features on the distance transform of the edge image rather than raw intensity, with pyramids - robust to intensity changes between frames. - ADT-KLT: adaptive switch between plain KLT and DT-KLT using a score combining change in edge count and IMU-preintegrated rotation angle. Threshold value not given in the text. - Back end: VINS-style sliding-window MAP optimization (IMU preintegration + reprojection on the unit sphere + marginalization prior, Huber loss, Ceres). Inverse-depth point features. - No explicit FFC/NUC compensation step described; edges are the robustness mechanism.   Data and sensors - Sensors: monocular thermal (own rig: Gobi+ 640, 640x480 @ 50 Hz) + IMU (MTi-G-710 @ 200 Hz). Ground truth from VLP-16 lidar + No

docs.b: FAST-LIO2 - paper digest  FAST-LIO2: Fast Direct LiDAR-inertial Odometry  - Xu, Cai, He, Lin, Zhang (HKU MaRS), arXiv 2107.06829, 2021 (arXiv lists no journal-ref; venue not verified here). paper   code   Read: full text, ar5iv HTML of arXiv v1 (appendix Table VIII not read)   Problem LiDAR-inertial odometry has to run on small onboard computers, cope with motion distortion, and work with both spinning and small-FoV solid-state LiDARs where hand-crafted edge/plane features break down. Maintaining a dense, updatable map in realtime is the main compute cost.   Method - Tightly coupled iterated Kalman filter on manifold (from FAST-LIO), 24-dim state, online LiDAR-IMU extrinsic calibration. Kalman gain computed with a state-dimension inverse, not measurement-dimension. - Direct registration: raw (downsampled) points matched to the map; plane fitted to 5 nearest map neighbours per point; no feature extraction. - Motion compensation by IMU back-propagation of every point to scan-end time. - ikd-Tree: incremental k-d tree with point insertion + on-tree downsampling, box-wise deletion via lazy labels, and parallel re-balancing; O(log n) insert and k-NN. - Map kept as a local cube moving with the sensor (default L = 1000 m); 0.5 m spatial downsampling; 1:4 temporal point downsampling. - Pure odometry: no loop closure.   Data and sensors - LiDAR + IMU. Evaluated with Livox Horizon (solid-state, 81.7 x 25.1 deg FoV), VLP-16, Velodyne HDL-32E; IMUs from 50 Hz to 1000 Hz. - Datasets: lili

docs.b: IMU preintegration (Forster) - paper digest  On-Manifold Preintegration for Real-Time Visual-Inertial Odometry  - Forster, Carlone, Dellaert, Scaramuzza, IEEE Transactions on Robotics 2016 (DOI 10.1109/TRO.2016.2597321; arXiv 2015). paper   code   Read: full text via ar5iv HTML render of arXiv 1512.02363 (two passes, whole page)   Problem Optimization-based VIO is more accurate than filtering but gets too slow as the trajectory grows, and a 200-800 Hz IMU would add a state per sample. Earlier preintegration (Lupton and Sukkarieh) used Euler angles, which are not frame-invariant and break near gimbal lock.   Method -  Preintegration on SO(3) : all IMU samples between two keyframes are summarized into one relative-motion measurement (delta rotation, delta velocity, delta position) that does not depend on the absolute start state, so it is computed once. - Analytic residuals and Jacobians are derived on the manifold (exponential map, right Jacobians). -  Noise propagation : preintegrated noise treated as zero-mean Gaussian to first order; its covariance is propagated iteratively sample by sample (appendix). -  Bias correction : when the bias estimate changes, the preintegrated delta is updated with a first-order Jacobian instead of re-integrating raw samples. -  Structureless vision factors : 3D landmarks eliminated linearly (Schur-style), so each landmark becomes one factor over the keyframes that see it. - Backend: factor graph solved incrementally with iSAM2, keyframe-based;

docs.b: Galileo OSNMA (SIS ICD + Receiver Guidelines) - standard digest  Galileo OSNMA Signal-In-Space ICD, Issue 1.1 (Oct 2023)  and  Galileo OSNMA Receiver Guidelines, Issue 1.3 (Jan 2024)  - EU / EUSPA, European GNSS Service Centre (GSC). SIS ICD   Receiver Guidelines   code: OSNMAlib   Read: full text of both PDFs (ICD 55 pp, RG 65 pp). Annex E (IPR) and the RG test-vector annex were skimmed, not read line by line. The IDD ICD (key/Merkle-root distribution) was not read. Section references below are "ICD x.y" and "RG x.y".   Problem Civil GNSS navigation data can be forged, for example with false ephemeris or clock data from a simulator spoofer. OSNMA lets a receiver cryptographically verify that the Galileo E1-B I/NAV navigation data came from Galileo and was not modified (RG 1.2). It authenticates the  data , not the ranging signal: "as this PVT is computed using non-verified ranging information, it cannot be considered authenticated" (RG Annex D).   Method (protocol in brief) -  TESLA one-way key chain.  Tags (truncated MACs) over the navigation data are broadcast first. The chain key that produced them is disclosed later, and keys go out in reverse order of generation (ICD 1.4, 5.5.2). Problem Online SLAM / sensor fusion needs the full smoothing solution (all past poses) updated every step. Batch sparse factorization gets too expensive as the graph grows. The original iSAM updates the linear system incrementally but needs periodic batch steps for variable reordering and relinearization, which cause spikes and fill-in.   Method -  Bayes tree : a directed tree of cliques encoding the factored density; maps to the square-root information matrix (like a clique tree but directed). Adding a factor only touches the cliques on the path from the affected variables to the root. - Incremental update = detach the affected top of the tree, re-eliminate it into a factor graph, re-insert orphaned subtrees. No matrix-level bookkeeping. -  Incremental variable reordering : the re-eliminated top is reordered with constrained COLAMD (CCOLAMD), forcing the most recent variables to the root so future updates stay cheap. -  Fluid relinearization : only variables whose delta exceeds threshold beta are relinearized, and only their cliques and ancestors are redone. Equations came out garbled, tables and prose legible.   Problem 2D matchers fail under extreme viewpoint change (up to 180 deg, opposite-facing views). DUSt3R, a pointmap-regression 3D reconstruction network, is very robust to this but its correspondences are imprecise. MASt3R adds explicit matching to DUSt3R to get both robustness and pixel accuracy.   Method - Backbone: DUSt3R (ViT-Large encoder, ViT-Base decoder, cross-attention between the two views), initialized from the public DUSt3R checkpoint (Sec. 4.1). - Per pixel it outputs a 3D point (pointmap in camera 1 frame), a confidence, and a new 24-D local descriptor from an added MLP head (Sec. 3.2, App. D). - Losses: DUSt3R confidence-weighted 3D regression (made metric when ground truth is metric) + InfoNCE matching loss over ground-truth correspondences, weight 1. - Fast reciprocal matching: start from k sparse seed pixels, iterate NN back and forth until cycles (mutual matches) form. Complexity O(kWH) instead of quadratic; also improves pose accuracy because it samples matches more evenly (App. B). - Coarse-to-fine: network works at 512 px max; for high-res images, match at low res, then match overlapping 512 px window crops covering 90% of coarse match

docs.b: RoMa - paper digest  RoMa: Robust Dense Feature Matching  - Edstedt, Sun, Bokman, Wadenback, Felsberg (Linkoping Univ. et al.), CVPR 2024. paper   code   Read: full text, arXiv HTML v2   Problem Dense matchers trained from scratch on limited 3D-supervised data (MegaDepth, ScanNet) overfit and break under extreme appearance or viewpoint change. RoMa targets robustness: matching pairs where most methods fail (the WxBS benchmark).   Method - Built on DKM (dense kernelized matching): global coarse match, then a stack of ConvNet refiners at strides 8/4/2/1 that predict warp residuals and certainty. - Coarse features: frozen DINOv2 (foundation model). Table 1 shows DINOv2 features are much more robust than VGG19/ResNet50 for coarse matching. - Fine features: a separate specialized VGG19 ConvNet, because DINOv2 patches are too coarse to localize. Not sharing weights between coarse and fine features helped (Table 2, setup II). - Transformer match decoder that predicts anchor probabilities (classification over coarse cells) instead of regressing coordinates, so the coarse stage can express multimodal hypotheses. - Loss: regression-by-classification for the coarse stage, robust (generalized Charbonnier) regression for refinement. - Output: a dense warp A= B plus per-pixel certainty; matches are sampled from it (10,000 matches with balanced sampling in the paper, Sec. 4.3). - Trained on MegaDepth + ScanNet at 560x560 (Sec. 4.2).   Data and sensors Monocular RGB pairs. Evaluated on IMC20

docs.b: SALAD - paper digest  Optimal Transport Aggregation for Visual Place Recognition  (DINOv2 SALAD) - Izquierdo, Civera (Univ. of Zaragoza), CVPR 2024 (venue per repo README bibtex). paper   code   Read: full text via arXiv HTML v2, plus repo README   Problem Visual place recognition as image retrieval: given a query image, find geo-tagged database images of the same place under illumination, weather, season and viewpoint change. Goal is a compact global descriptor that beats prior single-stage methods and two-stage re-ranking methods, and trains fast.   Method - Backbone: DINOv2-B (86M params), only the last 4 transformer blocks fine-tuned (Sec. 4.1; Table 6 ablates this). - Patch tokens get assignment scores to m clusters from a small 2-layer MLP (not k-means init as in NetVLAD). - A learnable "dustbin" column lets uninformative features be dropped (Eq. 2) - qualitatively it discards sky, road and dynamic objects (Figs. 3-5). - Sinkhorn optimal transport replaces NetVLAD's per-feature softmax, so assignment is balanced feature-to-cluster and cluster-to-feature (Eq. 3). - Features reduced to l dims, summed per cluster (no centroid residual), concatenated with a projected global (CLS) token, intra- and global L2 norm. - Default m=64, l=128, global 256 =  8192+256-d. Smaller: 2048+64, 512+32. - Training: GSV-Cities, multi-similarity loss, 4 epochs, ~30 min on one RTX 3090; train 224x224, eval 322x322.   Data and sensors - Monocular RGB, ground-level street / dashcam / train image

docs.b: Sample4Geo - paper digest  Sample4Geo: Hard Negative Sampling For Cross-View Geo-Localisation  - Deuser, Habel, Oswald (Univ. of the Bundeswehr Munich), ICCV 2023 (venue per repo README). paper   code   Read: full text via ar5iv rendering of arXiv 2303.11851, plus repo README   Problem Cross-view geo-localization: retrieve the satellite image that matches a street-level or drone image. Prior work leans on polar transforms, special aggregation modules or multi-stage refinement, and triplet loss struggles with hard negatives (can collapse). The paper asks how far a plain shared encoder gets with a better loss and better negative sampling.   Method - One shared (Siamese) ConvNeXt-B encoder (88M params) for both views, mean-pooled features, no polar transform, no extra modules (Sec. 3.2, 4.2). - Symmetric InfoNCE loss over the whole batch (street= sat and sat= street), label smoothing 0.1, learnable temperature (Sec. 3.1). - GPS-based sampling in early epochs: batches are filled with geographic neighbours (haversine for CVUSA/VIGOR, UTM Euclidean for CVACT), so in-batch negatives are hard (Sec. 3.3). - Dynamic Similarity Sampling (DSS): every 4 epochs, recompute embeddings and build batches from visually similar but wrong pairs - k=64 of K=128 neighbours, half by similarity, half random (Sec. 3.4). - University-1652 has no GPS per image, so it uses shuffling plus a custom sampler that avoids same-class duplicates in a batch. - Training: 40 epochs, batch 128, AdamW, LR 1e-3 cosine

This is a tutorial: there are no benchmarks; "results" below are the derivations and conventions it pins down.   Problem Quaternion and rotation formulas are scattered across conventions (Hamilton vs JPL, local vs global perturbations, active vs passive), and mixing them silently breaks IMU filters. The note collects one consistent set and derives a full IMU-driven error-state Kalman filter (ESKF) from it.   Method - Sec. 1-2: quaternion algebra, SO(3), exponential / log maps, Rodrigues formula, composition, SLERP; quaternion and rotation-matrix forms side by side. - Sec. 3: conventions. Table 2 lists the 4 binary choices (component order, algebra / handedness, passive function, direction of right-to-left products). Author picks  Hamilton  (scalar first, ij = k, right-handed, local-to-global), matching Eigen, ROS, Ceres. - Sec. 4: perturbations, derivatives, Jacobians (right Jacobian and its inverse), local vs global perturbations, time derivatives, zeroth- and first-order integration of rates. - Sec. 5: ESKF kinematics. STHN instead regresses a homography that places the thermal image directly inside a larger satellite crop, giving a metric position in one forward pass.   Method - Input: thermal image (512 px, about 1 m/px) and a satellite crop of width W_S centered on a position prior (W_S = 512, 1024 or 1536 m, i.e. the thermal image covers 100%, 25% or 11% of the crop). docs.b: STGL (thermal geo-localization) - paper digest  Long-range UAV Thermal Geo-localization with Satellite Imagery  - Xiao, Tortei, Roura, Loianno (NYU, TII), IROS 2023. paper   code   Read: full text, arXiv HTML v3; repo README   Problem Locate a UAV at night, when RGB cameras are useless, by matching downward thermal images against daytime RGB satellite imagery. Two obstacles: paired thermal-satellite data is scarce, and thermal images over desert are low-contrast and self-similar.   Method - SGM (geo-localization module): image retrieval. The satellite map is tiled into a database (512x512 crops, 35 px stride); the thermal query is embedded and matched by nearest neighbour. ResNet-18 backbone + compression conv + NetVLAD (4096-d), triplet loss (margin 0.1). Positives within 35 m, negatives beyond 50 m. - TGM (thermal generative module): pix2pix GAN that turns satellite tiles into synthetic thermal tiles, giving 79,950 extra pseudo-pairs for SGM training. - Domain adaptation: DANN with gradient reversal (weight 0.1). Best variant applies it to positives only; using negatives fights the triplet loss. - Contrast enhancement: linear scaling of thermal images, factor 3. Turns out to be critical (see Table II). - Output: position = center of the best-matching tile, so precision is bounded by tile stride, and the query must be roughly north-aligned and at the map's scale.   Data and sensors - Sensors: nadir FLIR Boson thermal camera (640p, 8.7 mm, 50 deg HFOV), about 1 m/px after ort

Textureless or corrupted thermal frames, outdated or self-similar maps, heading noise and thermal frames that run off the satellite crop all produce confident wrong fixes. UASTHN adds uncertainty estimation so bad fixes can be rejected.   Method - Base: a deep homography estimator (DHN, IHN or STHN two-stage) predicting four-corner displacements =  DLT =  homography =  center position. - CropTTA (data uncertainty): take N_C random crops of the thermal image (offset o_c, 32 best), run each through the network, map the corner predictions back, use per-corner std as uncertainty. Reject when all corner stds exceed a threshold s_c. - Deep Ensembles (model uncertainty): N_m models trained with different seeds, std across models. - Merge: CropTTA and DE combined by max (default), min or add. - Early stopping: run all samples only for the first k refinement iterations to estimate uncertainty, then continue with one sample - cuts latency. - Training: 100k steps, then 200k fine-tuning with CropTTA augmentation; 5 samples at evaluation. - Evaluation of rejection: ROC with predictions above 25 m MACE treated as should-reject. docs.b: Navigation trends 2025-2026 Each item: what changed, the source, and what it means for a navigation hackathon project. Scope is navigation only; weapon autonomy and terminal guidance debates are out of scope.   1. Fiber-optic drones reduce RF reliance, not navigation need - Fiber-optic FPV drones take control and video over a cable and cannot be radio-jammed; both sides fielded them at scale in 2025 (Lowy Institute, Jun 2025); Russian fiber drones reached Kramatorsk (Oct 2025) and Kharkiv (Euromaidan Press, Kyiv Independent). Range is cable-limited and spools leave tell-tale cables (TWZ). - Implication: fiber solves the short-range, operator-in-the-loop case by keeping a human pilot on video. Longer-range, low-altitude and autonomous segments still need onboard navigation, and jamming of GNSS stays the norm ( res:ngrn-ukraine-deftech-2025 ). It also shifts some C-UAS detection away from RF sensing toward EO/acoustic.   2. Cheap visual navigation modules became a commodity - Several vendors sell camera-to-map modules for small UAS: Twist Robotics OSCAR (Jan 2026), Vermeer, Blue Arrow in Ukraine; Theseus, UAVOS NavAI, Spleenlab, Auterion Visual Navigation elsewhere (see products). Theseus started at a February 2024 hackathon (Aviation Week). - IEEE Spectrum (2025) reports onboard optical navigation as the Ukrainian answer to jamming ( res:ieee-spectrum-ukraine-drones-ew-2025 ). - Implication: "drone matches camera to satellite map" is no longer novel to judges. docs.b: Ukrainian- and Russian-language sources: what they add Lane  ua-ru-sources : 38 resources and 12 repos, all tagged  lang:uk  or  lang:ru . Every URL resolved at collection time (Nov 2026). Every repo was checked with  gh api repos/<o /<n . Summaries come from the pages, PDFs and READMEs. Nothing was installed or run. Vendor and author performance numbers are passed on as claims. Strike and terminal-guidance content was skipped. One hit about a strike-oriented navigation product was dropped for that reason.   What this material teaches that English sources mostly don't  1. EW is layered. GNSS is one target among several.  English material usually treats "GPS-denied" as the whole problem. The Ukrainian explainers split it into the control uplink, the video downlink and GNSS. They also say radio reconnaissance has to come before any jamming (DOU on EW). For a navigation team, that means losing GNSS usually comes together with losing the link. Most designs in this set assume both: Vyriy beacons work "without GPS or a link", and the SPbU return-home project states the same requirement.  2. The anti-jam arms race is public and specific.  Ukrainian reporting gives CRPA element counts going from 4 to 16, 24 and 32 (Harxon 32-element, Shahed breakdown). It also shows a state test lab for domestic anti-jam antennas (Brave1 CRPA lab).
